articles.title: FASB Proposal Could Boost Corporate Stablecoin Adoption
articles.text:
US accounting overhaul could make stablecoins more attractive to corporations: Tempo
A Tempo report examines how proposed US accounting rules could change corporate stablecoin holdings, with direct redemption rights determining which tokens qualify as cash.
A new report from Stripe-backed blockchain Tempo argues that a proposed US accounting change could remove a major barrier to corporate stablecoin adoption by allowing qualifying tokens to be classified as cash equivalents on company balance sheets.
The report examines an Accounting Standards Update the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) proposed in August that could make stablecoins more practical for corporate treasury operations. Under current accounting practices, stablecoin holdings may not count toward a company’s reported cash reserves, affecting liquidity ratios and loan covenants even when the tokens are fully backed by dollars.
The proposed change could let companies use stablecoins for payments and settlements without those accounting complications.
According to Tempo, the FASB proposal would require companies to have direct redemption rights with stablecoin issuers. For example, buying USDC through an exchange would not necessarily let a company classify those tokens as cash equivalents.
Tempo cites Coinbase, which classified USDC and other payment stablecoins as cash equivalents in its 2025 annual report, supported by its redemption arrangement with Circle.
“Your contract with the issuer is what qualifies, and the token alone doesn’t get you there,” Tempo said.
The FASB proposal remains open for public comment until Nov. 19. The board will review the feedback before finalizing the accounting changes and setting an effective date.
Related: Crypto’s billions are back, but the premiums aren’t
Stablecoin regulation takes shape in the US
The FASB proposal follows the passage of the GENIUS Act in July 2025, which established the first comprehensive federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins in the United States. The law is scheduled to take effect in January 2027, or 120 days after federal regulators finalize implementing rules, whichever comes first.
While the GENIUS Act establishes requirements for stablecoin issuers, including reserve backing and redemption obligations, the FASB proposal addresses how companies account for stablecoins they hold.
The developments come as the market for US dollar-backed stablecoins has surpassed $300 billion, according to DefiLlama data. The Trump administration is also reportedly exploring ways to promote dollar-backed stablecoins overseas, potentially reinforcing the US dollar’s role as the dominant reserve currency.
According to Bloomberg, the administration is weighing partnerships with private companies to develop stablecoin projects overseas, potentially involving the Treasury Department, State Department and US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC).
Related: US Treasury proposes GENIUS Act rules targeting illicit finance

articles.title: AI Will Hit 40% of Jobs, IMF Warns. Young People Are First in Line - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said Monday in Bangkok that AI investment is keeping global growth near 3% despite an energy shock.
- Georgieva called AI a 'slow-moving tsunami' that will eventually touch about 40% of jobs worldwide and roughly 60% in advanced economies, with young workers hit first.
- The IMF will release its full World Economic Outlook on October 13, its first update to the 3% global growth forecast since July.
Artificial intelligence spending is keeping the world economy growing at roughly 3% a year even as an energy shock drags on most countries, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said Monday in Bangkok.
Georgieva spoke on the opening day of the IMF and World Bank annual meetings, which run through October 18 in the Thai capital. The biggest winners, she said, are the Asian economies that build the hardware behind AI, where adoption could add 0.5 to 1 percentage point a year to growth in advanced economies and 0.2 to 0.8 points in emerging ones.
A percentage point is the raw gap between two growth rates, so an economy growing 2% that gains a full point grows 3%, which is a lot. Georgieva said the high end of that range would more than offset the drag from aging populations across the region.
In its July outlook update, the IMF found that the top four net exporters of AI hardware—Taiwan, South Korea, Thailand, and Malaysia—beat its first-quarter growth forecasts by an average of 4.4% on an annualized basis, with South Korea growing at a 7.5% pace against the 1.8% the Fund had projected in April.
In a speech in Singapore last week, Georgieva said AI hardware and related tech products now make up more than a tenth of world goods trade. She added that AI investment as a share of global GDP will likely surpass what went into building the railroads or the electricity grid.
Georgieva also warned that the boom is bypassing most countries outside that supply chain. The Fund's July update projected 2026 global growth at 3%, down from 3.5% in 2025, as the Middle East war drove energy prices up.
On jobs, Georgieva called AI a “slow-moving tsunami” and said the IMF expects it to eventually touch about 40% of jobs worldwide, even downgrading or eliminating many of them. Exposure runs around 60% in advanced economies and roughly 23% in low-income countries, though she said poorer nations score lower mainly because AI hasn't reached them yet.
Young people entering the workforce are first in line, she said, because AI is absorbing the routine tasks entry-level jobs are built on. Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam, speaking on the same panel, said demand for graduates' first jobs is already falling and warned that AI could widen the gap between rich and developing economies if governments don't act.
AI could also squeeze public finances, Georgieva said, because if it shifts income from workers to the owners of capital, governments lose part of the tax base they lean on most. World Bank President Ajay Banga said the bank is backing “small AI” tools that don't depend on large language models, aimed at farmers, clinics and classrooms in emerging markets.
Georgieva said in Singapore that the AI build-out itself is adding to inflation, and warned that disappointing earnings could spread through markets because major AI companies have borrowed heavily to fund it.
The IMF publishes its full World Economic Outlook at 9 a.m. Bangkok time on October 13, which is 10 p.m. Monday in New York, with its first revision to the 3% global growth forecast since July.

articles.title: Bitcoin Miners Face Rising AI Infrastructure Funding Needs
articles.text:
Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals
The Bitcoin mining industry needs roughly $50 billion to complete planned AI infrastructure projects, with IREN, Riot Platforms and HIVE Digital facing major funding gaps.
Bitcoin mining companies expanding into artificial intelligence and high-performance computing face sharply different borrowing costs as lenders scrutinize large-scale data center projects, adding to the industry’s growing financing challenges.
According to the latest Miner Weekly newsletter from BlocksBridge Consulting, securing major AI customers has only been part of the challenge for miners. Companies must also raise billions of dollars to purchase computing equipment, build facilities and secure the power infrastructure needed to fulfill their contracts.
“[B]ig lenders have become more selective about data center loans and decisions increasingly depend on the customer, the contract and the path to completion,” BlocksBridge said.
IREN, which has expanded from Bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure, illustrates the differences in financing costs. The company secured a $3.65 billion GPU financing package in June at a blended interest rate of 6%, followed by a separate $2.4 billion financing arrangement in August at a fixed rate of 9%. The two agreements cover different projects, so they’re not directly comparable, but they show how borrowing costs can vary even within the same company.
Financing arrangements can also carry costs beyond interest payments. In a separate transaction involving Cipher Digital, Google agreed to backstop $1.4 billion in lease obligations in exchange for warrants representing 5.4% of Cipher’s equity, subject to certain adjustments. Exercising those warrants could dilute existing shareholders.
The financing requirements highlight a broader challenge for Bitcoin miners entering the AI market. Even companies with multibillion-dollar customer contracts may need substantial additional capital before their data centers become operational.
Related: Hut 8, IREN deals lift AI-focused Bitcoin mining stocks
Bitcoin miners face massive AI funding gap
The differences in financing costs come as Bitcoin miners take on billions of dollars in debt to fund their AI expansion plans. At the height of the Bitcoin bull market last October, VanEck data showed that miners’ debt had surged roughly 500% from the second quarter of 2024.
Ironically, capital requirements have continued to grow during the Bitcoin bear market as miners shift away from BTC mining amid deteriorating economics. A June 2026 analysis by BlocksBridge Consulting, citing VanEck data, estimated that publicly traded Bitcoin miners needed roughly $50 billion to complete their planned AI infrastructure projects, including a $21.1 billion funding gap at IREN alone.
Riot Platforms and HIVE Digital also face substantial funding requirements, estimated at $7.2 billion and $4.6 billion, respectively.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

articles.title: Bitcoin Bids Line Up at $82,000 as Oil Gains on Ukraine, Iran Woes
articles.text:
Bitcoin drops 2.2% as Ukraine, Iran strikes send oil toward one-month high
Bitcoin price action stayed rangebound after failing to sustain above $84,000 into the Wall Street open on rising oil prices.
Bitcoin (BTC) gave back early-week gains into Monday’s Wall Street open as doubts compounded over a Russia-Ukraine “energy ceasefire.”
Key points:
- Bitcoin reached $84,250 before falling 2.2% amid market nerves over oil supplies and the Russia-Ukraine “energy ceasefire.”
- Analysis saw too much “risk premium” priced in to oil markets in the face of improving shipping volumes.
- BTC options traders positioned “defensively” while keeping $90,000 and above on the table.
Bitcoin pressured as Brent crude oil rises above $107
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD reaching $84,254 on Bitstamp, its highest level since Wednesday, before dropping up to 2.2%.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The retreat came as Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of continuing to target energy infrastructure despite US president Donald Trump announcing a moratorium on such strikes. Elsewhere, Iran reported that an oil tanker had been hit and was ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices reacted sharply, with WTI crude spiking past $94 per barrel and Brent crude reaching $107.25 — its highest since Sept. 16.
CFDs on Brent crude oil four-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The increases come with markets already on edge ahead of key US inflation data in the form of Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI), due out on Wednesday and Thursday respectively. As Cointelegraph reported, CPI has proven particularly sensitive to rising oil prices.
Commenting, Robin Brooks, former chief FX strategist at Goldman Sachs, argued that oil markets had priced in “too much risk premium,” pointing to improving Hormuz transit volumes.
“Oil volumes out of the Persian Gulf are around 13 mb/d compared to a high of 16.5 mb/d a few weeks ago. This is still way better than the height of the war in March and April, but oil prices are back to their highs,” he noted in a blog post on the day.
BTC bid support seeks to protect $82,000 
Looking ahead to possible BTC price targets, trading company QCP Capital reported duality in Bitcoin options markets, with “defensive” positioning combined with traders considering an upside breakout to still be possible.
Related: BTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week
“Implied volatility has held firm even as spot settled back into the range, while risk reversals show a less pronounced premium for puts than usual. Read together, the market looks less defensively positioned but still priced for a possible breakout,” it summarized in its latest analysis.
“A clean move above $87k would bring $94k into focus.”
Trader and analyst Rekt Capital flagged $83,400 as local resistance on the day, with that level mirroring the area around $77,000 from mid-August through Sept. 21, when BTC/USD broke higher.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
Data from CoinGlass showed ask liquidity clustered around $84,500 on exchanges, with the total at that level circling $180 million. Bids were building around $82,000 at the time of writing, with spot price trending toward that level.
BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass

articles.title: Standard Chartered Will Hold Ripple's Stablecoin in Dubai—And Let Clients Trade With It Without Moving It - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Standard Chartered's Dubai International Financial Centre branch now offers institutional custody for Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin issued on the XRP Ledger.
- A planned integration with LMAX Group would let clients use RLUSD as trading collateral through collateral mirroring, meaning the tokens stay at the bank while LMAX credits their value.
- RLUSD has grown to roughly $2.45 billion in market cap, still under 1% of a stablecoin market worth about $306 billion.
Standard Chartered will now hold Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin for institutional clients in Dubai, and it wants to let them trade with those tokens without ever handing them over to an exchange.
“Standard Chartered today announced that it now supports institutional custody of Ripple USD (RLUSD) issued on the XRP Ledger (XRPL), giving eligible clients access to the Bank’s digital asset custody infrastructure. The service is available through Standard Chartered Bank’s DIFC Branch, which is regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA).” the British bank announced Monday
Custody is the unglamorous plumbing of finance: a regulated institution keeps your asset in its vault and answers for it if something goes wrong. The institution has the legal responsibility over your assets and will respond to you, but will also get permission to supervise, freeze and control your funds while they are under custody.
RLUSD is a stablecoin, a crypto token designed to always be worth $1 because it is backed by dollars, U.S. government bonds, and cash equivalents. Ripple launched it in December 2024 on Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, a public blockchain closely tied to Ripple, and the bank’s service covers the XRP Ledger version.
The bank also joined a planned integration with LMAX Group, a London-based marketplace for currencies and crypto, to make RLUSD eligible collateral on agreed LMAX products. Collateral, or margin, is the money a trader parks with a venue as a safety deposit against potential losses.
Under what Standard Chartered calls collateral mirroring, the RLUSD would stay at the bank while LMAX receives a mirrored record of its value that counts toward the client’s trades. The coins never travel to the exchange.
With mirroring, an exchange blowup would leave a trader’s collateral sitting at Standard Chartered, one of 29 banks the Financial Stability Board considers too big to fail and holds to tougher capital rules.
“Institutional clients want to participate in digital asset markets without compromising on how their assets are safeguarded,” said Waqar Chaudry, who heads digital assets in the bank’s securities services unit.
Standard Chartered has offered crypto custody in Dubai since 2024, and in July it said it became the first global systemically important bank to let institutions mint and redeem Circle’s USDC directly.
RLUSD got the Dubai regulator’s green light in June 2025. The LMAX leg is not live yet. The bank said it remains subject to final documentation, testing and regulatory approvals, and gave no date for when clients will be able to post RLUSD as margin.

articles.title: XRP Treasury Evernorth’s Shares Up 5% at Nasdaq Opening Print

XRP treasury Evernorth’s shares rise 5% at Nasdaq opening print
Evernorth’s share price rose by 5% as investors welcomed the Nasdaq debut of the first pure-play XRP digital asset treasury.
The newly listed shares of XRP-focused treasury company Evernorth Holdings (XRPN) jumped as much as 5% on their Monday Nasdaq stock exchange debut, according to Yahoo Finance data.

articles.title: Meta's New Muse Wonder Finally Puts Zuckerberg in the Frontier AI Race - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Monday, the first frontier-class models from Meta Superintelligence Labs, with a 1 million token context window.
- On Meta's own charts, Wonder Full leads GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 on long-horizon coding, legal agent work and memory, but Artificial Analysis ranks Opus 5.5 first at 58 versus Wonder Full's 56.
- The API version, Muse Wonder, costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, the same as Opus 5.5 and below GPT-6 Astra's $10 and $50.
Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Monday, the first models from its Superintelligence Labs that the company is willing to put head-to-head with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic.
“Muse Wonder is a major leap towards delivering personal superintelligence for everyone,” Zuckerberg wrote on Threads. “Congrats to everyone on our team for achieving this milestone. I’m looking forward to seeing how you all use it.”
That wording keeps him safely on the right side of President Trump, who said on Truth Social last Thursday that the White House considers anyone saying “Artificial Intelligence” instead of his preferred term ‘Super Intelligence’” to be "the enemy."
Meta has called its AI division Meta Superintelligence Labs since 2025, so Zuckerberg was compliant before it was “mandatory.”
Introducing Muse Wonder, our new family of frontier models with state of the art performance for personal and professional agentic work. pic.twitter.com/NKHrybrGKQ
— Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) October 12, 2026
Meta's announcement rests on two features: Active Memory, which carries what you told the model in one conversation into the next, and Active Focus, which keeps it grinding at a hard goal, trying new approaches and checking in with you before doing anything important.
Muse Wonder is live now through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, Meta's coding agent, while the bigger Muse Wonder Full is reserved for paying Muse Code subscribers. Both hold 1 million tokens in their context window (how much text a model can keep in view at once, roughly 750,000 words), per Meta's model card.
In April 2025, Meta's open-source Llama 4 models arrived with big promises, then stumbled in independent tests amid suspicions that the version scoring well on a popular public leaderboard behaved differently from the one people could download.
Zuckerberg answered with a roughly $14 billion deal for Scale AI and put its founder, Alexandr Wang, in charge of a new unit called Meta Superintelligence Labs. Its first model,Muse Spark, launched in April as a small, fast, closed model, and it marked the death of the open source Llama family.
Muse Wonder arrives weeks after OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra on September 3. Anthropic followed on September 22 with Claude Opus 5.5, which it says matches its pricier Claude Fable 5.1 on most work.
On Meta's Personal Superintelligence Index, an in-house composite of personal and professional assistant tasks where higher is better and the exact formula hasn't been published, Wonder Full scored 59.1. Claude Opus 5.5 scored 55.2, GPT-6 Astra 54.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 49.9.
Introducing Muse Wonder, our new family of frontier models with state of the art performance for personal and professional agentic work. pic.twitter.com/NKHrybrGKQ
— Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) October 12, 2026
SWE-Marathon, which measures how well an AI model can code, shows promising results for Meta’s AI models. Wonder Full scored 57.5 versus 46.3 for Opus 5.5 and 42.5 for Astra, though Meta admits that row isn't a controlled comparison and its model ran at maximum effort.
Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark hands AI models more than 1,200 lawyer-style assignments and counts a task as done only if the work passes every single check on an expert rubric, with no partial credit. Wonder Full scored 13.1, Astra 8.6 and Opus 5.5 just 4.2.
On MemoryBench, Meta's own test of whether a model can recall facts, including ones that were later updated, across conversations of 64,000 to 100,000 tokens, both Wonder models scored around 85.5. Opus 5.5 scored 81.5 and Astra 81.4.
Those are Meta's numbers, and two of the tests are Meta's own creations. The independent ranking from Artificial Analysis, a weighted average of 10 evaluations covering AI agents, coding, general knowledge and scientific reasoning, still puts Opus 5.5 first at 58, with Wonder Full tied with Anthropic's cheaper Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 56.
Muse Wonder, the version developers can actually buy, scores 52 on that index, a point below Astra and Fable 5.1. It costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens (tokens being the word fragments AI models read and write), exactly what Anthropic charges for Opus 5.5 and well under the $10 and $50 that OpenAI charges for Astra.
For regular people, the memory pitch cuts both ways, because an assistant that remembers everything also holds a lot of your life—and Meta is not precisely popular for handling private data responsibly. Last month, Inc. columnist Jason Aten found that Meta’s Muse agent had synced more than 187,000 rows of his private iMessages after he said he declined access, then claimed it had only seen notification previews.
Meta now calls Wonder “our most aligned model to date,” and the model card reports a 0% result on Agentic Misalignment, a test that pressures a model and scores how often it takes a harmful action. That comes two months after Meta disclosed that a Muse Spark model escaped a sandbox during a security evaluation and hacked a third-party service.
Meta says a full safety report is coming “soon,” and Wonder will reach the Muse app first for paying subscribers, with no date yet for free users.

articles.title: Ledger Implant Tests Bitcoin ETFs as Safer Custodial Solutions Than Hardware Wallets
articles.text:
Ledger implant tests Bitcoin ETFs as safer custodial solutions than hardware wallets
The discovery of an unauthorized Ledger hardware implant reignited debate on whether Bitcoin ETFs are safer than self-custodying Bitcoin via hardware wallet devices.
The newly discovered Ledger exploit has stirred broad industry debate over the safety of hardware wallets compared to effectively custodying Bitcoin holdings through exchange-traded funds (ETFs).
Bitcoin analyst Plan B said his then-controversial decision to move his Bitcoin (BTC) holdings to ETFs in 2025 was the right call in light of the recent Coldcard and Ledger exploits. “Zero regrets” about my ETF decision, wrote the analyst in a Monday X post.
Large holders have been converting self-custodied assets to ETFs for “enhanced security” for years, which is one of the main “selling points” for ETFs, 21Shares co-founder Ophelia Snyder told Cointelegraph in an email on Monday, adding that the recent exploits made this phenomenon part of the “public discourse.”
The remarks follow the discovery of a compromised Ledger wallet that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Some blockchain investigators estimated that losses from these implants could top $86 million, raising questions about the security of self-custodial cold wallets.
Related: Standard Chartered plans institutional crypto custody in Singapore
Hardware wallets are still safe, but providers need better threat modelling: Adam Back
To be sure, hardware wallets can still be secure custodial options, but providers need a better understanding of the emerging threat landscape, according to Blockstream CEO and Hashcash inventor Adam Back.
“Surprisingly few manufacturers understood the generic attacks, or so it seemed from their marketing and design choices, for the last decade. Time to catch up with threat-modelling,” wrote Back in a Saturday X post.
Source: Adam Back
However, Snyder said the main issue with self-custodial wallets is that their security depends on investors’ technical expertise and individual setup. She said:
“Without taking the time and rigor to set up properly, self-custody will always be less secure than handing over the assets to a specialist firm whose job it is to manage those protocols for you.”
Bitcoin security researcher and cypherpunk Jameson Lopp also said that self-custodial wallets can be a robust option, but urged investors to avoid mass migration to create new central points of failure during rushed transactions.
Magazine: Bitcoiners turn to dice throws as self-custody setups are re-evaluated

articles.title: From GTA V on iPhone to Free Photoshop: This AI Tool Is Upending Software - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- REA, an open-source toolkit that connects AI coding agents to reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra, went from under 10,000 GitHub stars on October 6 to more than 100,000 by October 12.
- Claude Opus 5.5 has fueled a wave of AI-decompiled game mashups and ports, from Spider-Man swinging through Arkham City to an unofficial PC port of Fable 2.
- Developer Brandon Thomas released ArtCraft, free Rust-built Adobe alternatives made with Claude, but calls it a clean-room rebuild that never touches Adobe's code.
Would you like to kill a boss in Skyrim using an AK47 from Counter Strike? Give your NPCs a real genius-level brain that gives you unique answers instead of predefined strings of text? Would you like to run GTA V on your iPhone? What about using paid software for free, and legally? Well, people are doing that and more with AI right now.
A free tool that lets AI agents pull apart almost any piece of software has become the hottest project on GitHub, jumping from fewer than 10,000 stars on October 6 to more than 100,000 by Monday.
It’s called REA, short for Reverse Engineer Anything. Stars are GitHub’s version of a bookmark, and REA collected more than 30,000 of them on October 11 alone, after sitting mostly ignored since its creation in April.
How REA works
Apps and games ship as machine code, the raw instructions a processor reads and humans basically can’t. Decompiling tries to turn that back into readable code, a bit like tasting a cake and working backward to the recipe.
Reverse engineering is the bigger umbrella: figuring out how something works without its blueprints, whether by watching what an app does and the data it sends, or by reading its code. This repository does exactly that.
In practice, a user points an agent at a program, asks how one feature works, and lets it dig from what happens on screen all the way down to the binary. It works on desktop apps, Android apps, and websites.
REA hooks AI coding assistants such as Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex up to the professional tools that do that job, like Ghidra, the reverse-engineering suite the NSA released to the public in 2019. The bridge is MCP, the Model Context Protocol, a standard Anthropic created so AI models can plug into outside tools—basically a universal adapter.
The developer’s “readme” file itself is far more modest than the hype, stating that REA “does not claim to recover original source code or automatically clone an application.” It doesn’t even ship its own decompiler.
This actually makes the whole operation legal(ish). The developer has never read the code, and just ships a similarly coded alternative that does exactly the same, but isn’t exactly the same.
The gates are open
People are doing all sorts of weird things with REA. For example, some players ended up watching Spider-Man swing through the Gotham of Batman: Arkham City, and creepers fight Elden Ring boss Malenia after someone stuffed about 1,600 Minecraft items into FromSoftware’s game. Another modder dropped Escape from Tarkov’s guns and menus into Skyrim and called it “Escape from Skyrim lol.”
Old console exclusives are escaping their consoles too: In September, a fan used an open-source AI model and a recompilation toolkit to bring Fable 2, the only mainline Fable game never released on PC, to Windows. The AI got it booting in about an hour, followed by a long stretch of manual fixes. Another one got to run GTV on iOS fluidly—something not even Rockstar Games bothered doing.
gta v running natively on ios (a recent fun project of mine) pic.twitter.com/5k6w06hoLY
— C22 (@c22_dev) October 9, 2026
Using these techniques (not the tools), developer Brandon Thomas took the idea to software people pay for every month, using Claude Opus 5.5 to build ArtCraft, a set of free, open-source apps written in Rust that mirror Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom and other Adobe programs, for Mac, Windows, and Linux.
Thomas says he snapped after Adobe charged him its cancellation fee one too many times. He isn’t alone in that grudge: Adobe agreed in March to a $150 million settlement with the Justice Department, which accused it of hiding early termination fees and making subscriptions a pain to cancel, though the company denied wrongdoing.
ArtCraft isn’t built with REA, and Thomas calls the project a clean-room rebuild, meaning the code is written from scratch using public documentation and observed behavior, never the original code, the same legal approach Compaq used to clone IBM’s PC BIOS in the 1980s.
The apps are labeled “early alpha” or “in development” on the project’s site, and one pixel artist has already called the Photoshop clone “completely unusable.”
Anything that runs on your own device can now be read by an AI agent with enough patience and tokens, which erodes the oldest copy protection in software: the sheer pain of reading machine code. That means cheaper clones and better game preservation, but also easier piracy and fewer places for security flaws to hide.
Activision has already pulled footage of an AI-decompiled Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, and Bethesda sent a cease-and-desist letter over an AI-made browser game called Fallout: New York.
UPDATE: Due to copyrights I had to take down this game. BUT I will have an updated version of the game up and running soon!
If you want to play it now and give me feedback as I fix things just reply to this comment and I'll DM you the new link.
— CHRIS FIRST (@chrisfirst) October 4, 2026
That seems to be the only defense studios have against a trend that may easily force open source everything.
REA, meanwhile, keeps shipping, with eight releases between October 3 and October 11. Thomas has already walked back his promise to match Adobe’s feature set within a month, and now says it will take months.

articles.title: Strategy Adds 250 Bitcoin as Holdings Reach 848,250 BTC
articles.text:
Strategy adds 250 Bitcoin as holdings reach 848,250 BTC
Michael Saylor’s Strategy said Bitcoin holdings reached 848,250 BTC after its latest purchase, while maintaining a $4.88 billion cash reserve.
Strategy bought 250 Bitcoin for $21.5 million last week, marking a second consecutive weekly decline in purchases as its Bitcoin holdings reached 848,250 BTC.
The company funded $21 million of the purchases through sales of its common stock and the remaining $500,000 with existing cash between Monday and Sunday, according to an announcement published on Strategy’s website.
Strategy also continued repurchasing shares of its STRC preferred stock, spending $192.4 million during the week, up from $176.3 million the previous week.
The company’s Nasdaq-traded common stock, MSTR, was up less than 1% ahead of Monday’s market opening, according to Yahoo Finance. The preferred stock was poised to open at $99.68 a share.
The company said it maintains a $4.88 billion US Reserve to support preferred stock dividends and debt interest payments. Its separate USD Cash balance stood at $640.5 million as of Sunday.
The purchase followed a Sunday post by founder and executive chair Michael Saylor, who signaled another Bitcoin purchase with the message, “There’s always room for more orange.” Strategy typically reports its Bitcoin purchases in filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, which is closed Monday for the Columbus Day holiday.
Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation has slowed in recent months. Its holdings grew just 0.2% during the third quarter, as the company acquired 7,218 BTC while selling 5,553 BTC.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

articles.title: Solana Treasury Firm DeFi Development Keeps Buying SOL as CHAD Preferred Stock Hits Record - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- DeFi Development Corp added about 22,070 SOL and SOL equivalents last week, lifting its treasury to roughly 2,586,282 tokens, up 12% since August 12.
- Its CHAD perpetual preferred stock, which pays a 13% annual dividend on a $10 stated amount, hit record highs in the week ended October 9 and is approaching $10 after an IPO priced at $8.
- DFDV common stock traded near $4.41 on Monday, giving the company a market value of about $144 million against roughly $287 million worth of SOL.
DeFi Development Corp, the Nasdaq-listed Solana piggy bank, added about 22,070 SOL—worth about $2,373,211—and “SOL equivalents” to its treasury last week, according to a press release published Monday.
That brings its stash to roughly 2,586,282 tokens, worth about $287 million with SOL near $111. Weekly buys keep shrinking, from 101,381 SOL in mid-September (around $11.4 million) to 47,706 ($5.8 million), then 26,202 ($3.1 million).
DFDV is a digital asset treasury company, a public firm that holds a cryptocurrency so stock investors can bet on it without opening a crypto account. It was a real estate software firm called Janover until April 2025, when it pivoted to Solana and copied Strategy’s Bitcoin playbook.
CHAD, the company’s perpetual preferred stock, hit all-time highs in the week ended October 9 and is approaching $10. Perpetual preferred shares never mature and get dividends before common stock; CHAD pays a variable 13% a year on its $10 stated amount, or $1.30 per share, declared each business day.
“CHAD reaching new highs and approaching $10.00 even as SOL pulled back is an encouraging sign that investors are recognizing its distinct income proposition,” said Dan Kang, Chief Strategy Officer. “For common shareholders, CHAD provides a funding source that can support accretive SOL per share growth without issuing additional common shares. For CHAD holders, it offers daily income supported by that growing, productive treasury,” he added.
That record sounds less dramatic once you know the shares priced their IPO at $8 in September, below their own stated amount. Last week DFDV even authorized buybacks for whenever CHAD trades under its $10 par value. Mission nearly accomplished.
The price matters because DFDV funds its SOL purchases through a $300 million at-the-market program, which sells new CHAD shares gradually at market prices. The closer CHAD trades to $10, the more SOL each new share buys.
“Short-term volatility has not changed our conviction or our commitment to accumulating SOL,” CEO Joseph Onorati said in the release.
SOL fell about 9% over seven days, and nearly $1 billion in long positions, or bets that prices would rise, were liquidated in 24 hours. Liquidation is forced selling: when traders bet with borrowed money and prices fall far enough to wipe out their collateral, exchanges close the bet automatically, pushing prices lower still.
A 13% dividend looks generous, but CHAD is backed by a company whose main asset trades about 62% below its January 2025 peak of roughly $295. The release itself warns that staking rewards may not be enough to cover dividends.
DFDV’s common stock traded near $4.41 on Monday, a market value of about $140 million—roughly half the value of its SOL, though it also carries debt. When a treasury company trades below its crypto stash, selling shares to buy tokens stops making sense, one reason the sector is under pressure.
CHAD holders will keep collecting $0.00516 per share for each business day through October 30, and the next macro test arrives Wednesday with the U.S. September inflation report.

articles.text:
Australia proposes leverage caps for crypto-settled derivatives
ASIC’s proposal would extend leverage limits and protections against negative balances to certain derivatives settled in digital assets.
Australia’s securities regulator wants to extend leverage limits and other retail investor safeguards to certain trading contracts settled in crypto.
On Monday, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) proposed expanding the rules for contracts for difference (CFDs), which let traders bet on price movements without owning the underlying asset.
The rules generally cover contracts settled in cash or by offsetting obligations between the parties. ASIC wants to add contracts settled by transferring digital assets, including those tracking non-crypto assets, provided they meet the other criteria for a CFD.
ASIC said that certain crypto futures and options with fixed expiration dates would remain outside the CFD rules.
Australia’s existing framework, introduced in 2021, caps leverage and requires providers to close positions when account funds fall below specified levels. Negative balance protection also limits losses to the funds in a client’s CFD trading account.
The regulator is seeking feedback on the proposed extension and amendments until Nov. 9.
Separately, Australia passed legislation in April to bring crypto exchanges and tokenized custody platforms under its financial services licensing framework, with the new regime taking effect on April 9, 2027.
ASIC also required crypto firms relying on temporary enforcement relief under existing financial services law to apply for licenses by Sept. 30 or seek changes to their existing licenses.
Related: Australia says it removed 45 crypto, remittance registrations over the past year

articles.title: Bitcoin Traders Eye $82,500 Support Zone Ahead of US CPI, PPI Data
articles.text:
BTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week
Bitcoin traders braced for inflation-based volatility after BTC price action preserved key weekly support around $82,500.
Bitcoin (BTC) starts the third week of October by defending support at $82,500 ahead of key US inflation data.
Key points:
- US CPI print on Wednesday and PPI data on Thursday provides the week’s major risk-asset volatility catalyst, with markets seeing CPI at 3.7% year-on-year.
- Oil prices react to the US plan to buy Russian diesel, but WTI crude heads higher after dropping below $90 per barrel on Monday.
- Bitcoin seals a weekly close above key support at $82,500, avoiding a drop into its previous 2026 macro range between $60,000 and $80,000.
Markets see September inflation creeping higher
US inflation data is in traders’ crosshairs this week ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee’s Oct. 28 meeting on interest-rate policy.
The September prints of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) will be released on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.
In August, CPI broadly conformed to expectations at 3.4% year-on-year, with markets now seeing an uptick to 3.7% this month on the back of ongoing military action in the Middle East and associated fuel-price surges. PPI is expected at 0.3% month-on-month versus 0.2% in August.
US CPI 12-month % change by category. Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics
Crypto, stocks and gold traditionally benefit from lower-than-expected inflation readings as these reduce the odds of the Fed tightening policy, allowing for capital inflows to strengthen. Speaking to Reuters about current gold prices and US bond yields, Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, drew attention to the impact of a surprise move to the downside for CPI and PPI readings in particular.
“In the short term, a cooler-than-expected US inflation reading would be the clearest near-term catalyst, as it would reduce the odds of further Fed tightening and ease pressure on real yield,” he said.
CME FedWatch shows that markets see just an 18.8% chance of a rate hike on Oct. 28 from the current 3.75-4.00% range. The following meeting, in December, is attracting 70.6% odds of the Fed hiking by 25 basis points to 4.00-4.25%.
Fed target-rate probabilities (screenshot). Source: CME Group
Fed chair Kevin Warsh is due to hold a discussion with Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), at an event in Bangkok, Thailand on Friday.
Oil briefly cools on US-Russia diesel announcement
US bond yields have come off 24-year highs seen last week, with the 10-year and 30-year yields at 5.24% and 5.60%, respectively, on Monday.
US 10-year bond yield one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Stocks futures were green to start the week, with the S&P 500 index up 0.25% and around 30 points off new all-time highs.
S&P 500 futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
An announcement by US President Donald Trump over a deal to buy 300,000 tons of diesel from Russia appeared to have only a modest knock-on effect on oil prices, with the plan facing growing bipartisan backlash. Trump also announced an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine.
“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed,” he wrote on Sunday in a post on Truth Social. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was unaware of the energy ceasefire.
WTI crude traded around $91.50 per barrel on Monday, up 2% from the day’s low of $89.60. Data from motorist group AAA put the average price of diesel at $6.26 per gallon versus all-time highs of $6.52 seen on Sept. 22.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
PVM analyst Tamas Varga told Reuters Russia’s reduced output capacity made the impact of the deal “questionable.”
“However, Moscow has partially lifted its ban on diesel exports, allowing 500,000 tonnes (around 3.7 million barrels) to be released onto the international market, equivalent to roughly one day of US consumption and around 13% of global demand,” he noted.
Bitcoin avoids support breakdown at weekly close
At around $83,700 on Bitstamp, Sunday’s weekly candle close cemented a 3.2% weekly decline for BTC/USD.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
At the same time, the pair preserved a key support level at $82,500 on weekly time frames, thus avoiding a return to its previous long-term range between $60,000 and $80,000. As Cointelegraph reported, $82,500 remains on traders’ radar as a crucial line in the sand for Bitcoin bulls.
Last week, trader and analyst Rekt Capital wrote that a weekly close above $82,500 would mark a “successful” support retest. This in turn could see investors continue to reaccumulate BTC at current levels, opening up the path higher in a manner similar to Bitcoin’s recovery from its 2022 bear market.
BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
In light of Bitcoin’s multiple support retests after its initial breakout in July, trader and analyst Aksel Kibar drew comparisons between crypto and stock markets. Since May, the S&P 500 has seen multiple retests at key levels, initially at 7,300 points and then at 7,600 points.
S&P 500 one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Bitcoin could be experiencing a “hard retest” of support in a similar manner, with the implication that BTC/USD should shift higher if those retests continued to be successful, Kibar wrote in an X post on Sunday.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Aksel Kibar on X.com

articles.title: Ripple-Backed Evernorth Hits Nasdaq Holding 473 Million XRP Worth Far Less Than It Paid - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Evernorth began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN on Monday after closing its merger with SPAC Armada Acquisition Corp. II on October 9, holding about 473 million XRP and $300 million in gross cash.
- About 80.3% of Armada's public shareholders redeemed their shares for roughly $10.58 each, pulling about $195 million out of the deal and leaving a thin float that sent the stock as high as $53 before the close.
- XRP fell from $2.37 when the deal was signed to a $1.43 reference price at closing, valuing Evernorth's treasury at roughly $677 million versus the more than $1 billion it originally raised.
Evernorth, the Ripple-backed company built to stockpile XRP, started trading on the Nasdaq on Monday under the ticker XRPN, giving anyone with a regular brokerage account a way to bet on the cryptocurrency without ever opening a crypto wallet.
The listing caps a merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II that closed on Friday. Armada was a SPAC, short for special purpose acquisition company: a listed shell with no business of its own that raises cash, parks it in a trust, and waits to merge with a private firm that wants to skip a traditional IPO.
Evernorth enters public markets holding roughly 473 million XRP and about $300 million in gross cash. At the $1.43 XRP reference price used in the deal's closing filing, that stash is worth about $677 million.
The $677 million figure falls well short of the pitch Evernorth made when it first announced the deal in October 2025, when it touted more than $1 billion in funding to buy XRP. The merger documents priced the token at $2.37 at signing, so by closing day XRP had lost roughly 40% of its value.
Evernorth spent roughly $947 million buying XRP in late October 2025, and by February that pile was worth about $446 million less than it paid. XRP hit an all-time high of $3.65 in July 2025; the $1.43 closing reference price sits about 61% below that peak.
Evernorth belongs to a crowded category known as digital asset treasuries, or DATs: public companies whose main business is holding a cryptocurrency and raising money to buy more of it. Strategy (formerly Microstrategy) pioneered the playbook with Bitcoin, and Evernorth says it is now the largest publicly traded company devoted to XRP.
The model runs on a ratio called mNAV, or market-to-net-asset value, which divides a company's stock market value by the value of the crypto it holds. Above 1, a DAT can sell new shares at a premium and buy more tokens; below 1, raising money means dilution, where each existing share ends up representing a smaller slice of the company.
About 80.3% of Armada's public shareholders, holding 18.5 million shares, chose redemption, the SPAC investor's right to hand shares back for cash from the trust. They took about $10.58 per share, pulling roughly $195 million out of the deal before it closed.
That exodus left only about 4.5 million original public shares, a tiny float (the pool of shares available for everyday trading) that lets small orders move the price wildly. Days after the redemption window shut, XRPN touched an intraday high of $53 on October 2 and closed that Friday at $39.42, before sliding to $17.09 on October 9, the day the merger closed. On its first day trading as Evernorth, the stock briefly jumped toward $19 before fading to $16.64 by midday Monday, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Tokyo-listed financial group SBI Holdings now controls 39.9% of Evernorth's voting shares, while the fund of Arrington Capital, which sponsored the SPAC, holds 19.9%, and Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen is tied to 9.9%, according to the filing. Ripple and its affiliates are capped at 9.9% of the voting power, and Ripple, a Larsen-linked trust and Arrington's fund signed six-month lock-ups that bar them from selling until April 2027.
Most of the treasury came from existing holders swapping tokens for stock. Arrington's fund contributed about 211 million XRP, Ripple handed over about 127 million, the Larsen-linked trust added 50 million, and roughly 84 million were bought at an average of $2.53 using $214 million in early funding.
Rather than simply sitting on its tokens like a passive fund, Evernorth plans to earn yield through DeFi, or decentralized finance, apps that lend and trade crypto without a bank in the middle, and to run validators, the computers that confirm transactions on the XRP Ledger, all aimed at growing the amount of XRP behind each share.
On Monday, the company named Hugo Jeandesboz, formerly co-chief investment officer at Coinbase Asset Management, to run that strategy. Michael Arrington said in the merger announcement that Evernorth brings “scaled capital, active participation and the standards of a public company” to the institutional build-out of XRP's infrastructure.
Evernorth plans to celebrate the listing by ringing Nasdaq's ceremonial closing bell on Wednesday, October 14, two days after its shares began trading. Alongside the stock, its warrants, which give holders the right to buy shares at $11.50 each, now trade under the separate ticker XRPNW.

articles.title: Global watchdog warns the $300 billion stablecoin market could face bank runs even with full reserves
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The FSB warns that stablecoins could face redemption crises even when their total reserves are sufficient but spread across different countries.
- Delays moving reserves between jurisdictions could trigger depegging, forced asset sales and broader financial-market stress.
- Regulators will discuss the risks at the Oct. 15 G20 meeting, but coordinated cross-border crisis procedures remain undeveloped.
The Financial Stability Board (FSB) warned that stablecoins could face redemption crises if, during market stress, reserves become inaccessible across borders.
In an Oct. 12 report, the global financial watchdog said stablecoin issuers operating through affiliated entities in different countries could struggle to meet concentrated withdrawal demands when their reserve assets are held elsewhere.
The warning comes ahead of an Oct. 15 meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors, as regulators confront growing risks from a stablecoin market valued at approximately $300 billion in mid-2026, with 99% of its value pegged to the US dollar.
FSB Chair Andrew Bailey said international regulatory coordination remains underdeveloped, leaving authorities without mature arrangements for managing cross-border stablecoin failures.
Stablecoin reserves face cross-border stress test
The FSB identified particular vulnerabilities in stablecoins issued by multiple affiliated companies that share liability for the same token while maintaining separate reserves.
Under such arrangements, holders may be able to redeem their tokens through any participating issuer, regardless of where the stablecoins were originally issued.
That flexibility can create liquidity mismatches when redemption demand concentrates in one jurisdiction while much of the collateral backing the tokens remains in another.
Moving reserves between entities could resolve the imbalance under normal conditions. However, banking restrictions, settlement delays and differences in national regulations could complicate those transfers during a market panic.
The speed at which stablecoins circulate amplifies the risks.
Digital tokens can move across borders and trade around the clock, while the Treasury securities, bank deposits and other traditional assets backing them remain subject to local financial-market operating hours and settlement arrangements.
The FSB warned that delays in meeting redemptions could push holders to sell stablecoins at discounts on secondary markets, potentially destabilizing their dollar pegs.
A sufficiently large run could also spill into traditional finance if issuers liquidate reserve assets rapidly or withdraw substantial deposits from banks to meet redemption requests.
For context, Circle's European stablecoin arrangements illustrate how cross-border reserve management can affect redemption procedures.
Under its redemption policy, updated in September, Circle co-issues USDC through its French entity for the European Economic Area and its US entity for markets outside the region.
The policy allows Circle France to adjust or defer certain redemption requests during a defined stress event when the two entities cannot complete reserve rebalancing.
Those measures could include temporary redemption limits for European crypto-asset service providers, while preserving holders' rights to redemption at par.
The provisions describe contingency arrangements rather than an existing liquidity failure. They also operate under Circle's specific jurisdictional redemption rules, which differ from the FSB's unrestricted cross-issuer redemption model.
Nevertheless, the regulator's concerns extend to affiliated issuers' legal responsibilities when a stablecoin faces distress.
The FSB noted that issuers may struggle to identify where their tokens are held because blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, complicating efforts to determine which entities are responsible for particular redemption obligations.
Differences in national insolvency laws could create additional uncertainty over which regulator has authority to intervene and how remaining reserves should be distributed.
Those challenges are compounded by uneven regulatory development.
The FSB's 2025 assessment found substantial gaps in countries' implementation of its global stablecoin recommendations, increasing opportunities for issuers to structure operations across jurisdictions with different supervisory requirements.
FSB seeks stronger regulatory regime
In response, the watchdog is seeking stronger international information-sharing arrangements and closer monitoring of where stablecoins circulate, where redemptions occur and where reserve assets are held.
It also wants regulators to assess the depth of secondary-market liquidity and develop more coordinated approaches to handling stablecoin distress or insolvency.
However, regulators face significant information gaps. The FSB said blockchain analytics providers often use different methods to estimate stablecoin activity, and reliably establishing holders' geographic locations and cross-border transactions can be hard.
The proposed measures build on the FSB's 2023 recommendations and are non-binding, leaving national authorities responsible for implementing any changes.
At this week's G20 meeting, officials will receive the FSB's findings as part of discussions on financial stability.
The watchdog has identified further work on cross-border monitoring, information sharing and crisis planning, but has not established a timetable for common procedures governing a stablecoin issuer's failure across multiple jurisdictions.

articles.title: Kraken Parent Receives VARA Approval for UAE Expansion
articles.text:
Kraken parent clears Dubai’s final hurdle for dirham trading rollout
Payward received full market approval from Dubai’s VARA to expand its digital asset services in the UAE, building on the preliminary approval received in May.
Payward, the parent company of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, has received approval from the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) for its local entity, Payward FZCO, to provide crypto services.
At launch, Kraken’s clients in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) will be able to access spot and margin trading in UAE dirham (AED)-denominated pairs and make direct deposit withdrawals, Payward announced on Monday. The company is targeting launch in the coming weeks.
VARA’s public register shows that the regulator issued Payward FZCO a virtual asset service provider (VASP) license on Oct. 6, enabling it to offer management and investment services, as well as broker-dealer services.
Payward said the approval allows it to serve retail, professional and institutional investors. It follows its preliminary approval in May 2026.
Dubai’s VARA registry currently lists 58 licensed providers, up from 49 active companies in May 2026.
Banks and brokers are also expanding their crypto offerings under the UAE’s other regulatory regimes.
In September, Standard Chartered launched spot Bitcoin and Ether trading for institutional clients in the UAE through its Dubai International Financial Centre branch, which is regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority.
In August, trading platform Capital.com revealed plans to offer spot crypto services to clients in the UAE after its affiliate, Capital Vault, secured a virtual-asset license from the country’s Capital Market Authority (CMA).
Related: Nasdaq invests $100M in Kraken parent at $21B valuation: Report

articles.title: Bitcoin Spooked? Crypto Fear and Greed Index Drops to Pre-Rally August Lows - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 56 (neutral) on Monday from 67 a week earlier and an Aug. 26 peak of 82, the highest reading of the year.
- Bitcoin dropped about 6%, from $86,978 to $81,749.83, as oil topped $101, the 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.70% and spot.
- Myriad traders now give 45% odds of Biticoin hitting $87,500 and 56% odds of BTC dropping to $80,000 in October, both lower than on Oct. 7.
After a red hot summer lifted Bitcoin and the rest of crypto out of a brutal bear market, sentiment has now clearly shifted, bucking typically reliable seasonal trends.
Bitcoin is now trading just above $82,000, down close to 5% for the week, and the cryptocurrency market’s Fear and Greed Index fell to 56 on Monday, a “neutral” reading, after reaching “extreme greed” in late August.
The Fear and Greed Index is a 0-to-100 gauge that measures investor appetite, where 0 is extreme fear and 100 extreme greed. The index peaked at 82 on Aug. 26, its high for the year, and read 68 a month ago.
Bitcoin peaked at $86,978 early last week and slid as low as $81,749.83 on Oct. 8, a drop of about 6%, before recovering to roughly $83,800 on Monday. That leaves the largest cryptocurrency about 34% below its all-time high of above $126,000, set on Oct. 6, 2025 back when extreme greed was the norm.
That slide marked a rough stretch that extended until August of this year. The August rally led to a 24.9% increase in the price of Bitcoin, enough for industry participants such as Fundstrat co-founder and Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee and Crypto Quant’s Kim Yong Yu to announce the end of the bear market.
But the increased appetite for crypto bets has now cooled, at least for now, as the Fear and Greed Index indicates.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $484.9 million last week on Wednesday, their worst day since June, and another $244.1 million the following day. A $21.1 million inflow on Friday left the funds down a net $386.3 million for October while Ethereum funds extended their outflow streak to nine days, with $635 million out this month.
In terms of catalysts, macroeconomic headwinds have weighed on Bitcoin and the rest of crypto.
Brent crude topped $101 a barrel last week as ship attacks around the Strait of Hormuz piled up, and the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.70%, its highest since 2002. Stocks, gold and Bitcoin sold off together that day, which points to a macro trade rather than a crypto problem. Brent is trading near $110 today, even after President Donald Trump said the U.S. would not engage in war at least until November.
Oil is an input cost for shipping, manufacturing, farming and travel, so a sustained jump in crude tends to filter into consumer prices. Higher inflation makes it harder for the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates and more likely to raise them, which is the path the central bank's latest minutes describe.
Bond investors respond by demanding higher yields, since inflation erodes the fixed payments Treasuries make. Because the Treasury yield is the benchmark "risk-free" return, a 30-year paying 5.70% pulls money away from riskier bets and raises borrowing costs across the economy. Bitcoin pays no yield and trades alongside stocks as a risk asset, so rising yields and rate-hike expectations tend to push it lower, as they did on Oct. 7.
The background likely explains why the Fear and Greed Index has dropped so much. Traders are more cautious, especially with high risk assets such as Bitcoin.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, give Bitcoin a 45% chance of touching $87,500 in October. That is down from 55% on Oct. 7. The odds of Bitcoin reaching $90,000 have slipped to 28% from 36%.
Myriad traders are also now pricing in 56% odds that Bitcoin drops to as low as $80,000, followed by 33% odds for a drop to $77,500 and 20% odds on $75,000.

articles.title: FTX's former Bitcoin mining bet gets new life as parent raises €800 million for AI
articles.text:
Quick Take
- SWI Group has raised €800 million to expand AI infrastructure as it prepares to transform FTX-backed Bitcoin miner Genesis Digital Assets.
- CoinShares estimates AI infrastructure could generate three times Bitcoin mining's annual profit per megawatt, driving miners toward computing.
- SWI has yet to disclose how much funding Genesis will receive or when its mining facilities will begin generating AI revenue.
SWI Group has raised €800 million to expand AI infrastructure, advancing its plan to repurpose FTX-backed Bitcoin miner Genesis Digital Assets.
On Oct. 12, the Amsterdam-listed company announced a capital increase backed by institutional investors, valuing the group at €6.1 billion and bringing total equity raised since March above €1 billion.
The financing will support data-center development, power infrastructure and computing deployments across Europe and the United States, where SWI is converting its digital infrastructure portfolio toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.
The expansion includes Genesis Digital Assets (GDA), a former major investment of bankrupt crypto exchange FTX's trading affiliate, Alameda Research, which SWI acquired control of earlier this year.
The fundraising comes as Bitcoin miners increasingly redirect capital toward AI infrastructure, attracted by stronger projected profitability and rising valuations for companies with access to electricity and data-center capacity.
Former FTX investment becomes foundation for AI expansion
Genesis was among Alameda Research's largest venture investments before FTX collapsed in November 2022.
The trading firm invested approximately $1.15 billion in Genesis between 2021 and 2022, when the miner was valued at about $5.5 billion.
The investment later became the subject of bankruptcy litigation, with FTX's recovery trust seeking to reclaim funds it alleged Alameda improperly transferred. The trust dismissed the lawsuit in June 2026.
SWI has since consolidated control of Genesis, completing the acquisition of a stake exceeding 70% in August through share purchases and restructuring.
The company plans to rename the miner SWI Digital and use its US mining infrastructure as a foundation for high-performance computing and AI services.
Genesis's existing power-connected sites are central to that strategy, giving SWI access to infrastructure it can redevelop for more demanding computing workloads.
SWI previously disclosed that its combined European and American digital infrastructure portfolio exceeded 4 gigawatts of power capacity, with more than 80% of its capital allocated to the sector.
The group also plans to develop its own AI cloud platform, extending its business beyond data-center ownership into computing services for enterprises and developers.
SWI Chief Executive Max-Hervé George said the latest fundraising would help the company expand alongside growing demand for computing capacity.
The new shares will be issued in several series, although SWI did not identify the participating investors or disclose how much of the proceeds would be allocated specifically to Genesis.
Bitcoin miners' AI pivot delivers stronger returns
SWI's expansion follows a sharp divergence in the financial outlook for Bitcoin mining and AI infrastructure.
According to CoinShares' second-quarter mining report, AI computing infrastructure could generate approximately $1.5 million in annualized profit per megawatt, compared with an estimated $500,000 from Bitcoin mining.
That threefold difference has helped drive a substantial revaluation of former mining companies pursuing AI opportunities.
CoinShares found that 10 of the 12 publicly traded mining companies it tracked gained between 70% and 195% during the second quarter.
Companies focused on AI infrastructure, including Hut 8, Cipher Mining, TeraWulf and Core Scientific, traded at an average of 19.4 times forward sales, compared with 6.6 times for a group of more mining-focused competitors.
The shift reflects growing investor demand for companies with existing electricity connections and infrastructure capable of supporting AI workloads.
However, converting those assets remains capital-intensive.
CoinShares estimates that developing AI-grade facilities from mining infrastructure can cost $8 million to $15 million per megawatt, compared with approximately $700,000 to $1 million for mining infrastructure.
The report also found that more than $100 billion in disclosed AI computing contracts across the covered companies supported only about $1.1 billion in annualized revenue, with roughly 550 megawatts generating billings against more than 4 gigawatts of contracted capacity.
That gap has made project execution increasingly important as investors assign higher valuations to companies transitioning away from Bitcoin mining.
SWI's €800 million capital increase provides additional financing for its expansion, but the company has not disclosed which Genesis facilities will be converted first, their development costs or when they will begin generating AI computing revenue.

articles.title: Standard Chartered Adds RLUSD Stablecoin Custody
articles.text:
Standard Chartered adds Ripple USD custody, eyes LMAX collateral deal
Standard Chartered has launched custody for Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger and plans to let institutions use the tokens as trading collateral.
Standard Chartered has launched institutional custody services for Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin, with plans to expand its use as trading collateral.
The UK-based multinational bank announced Monday it rolled out RLUSD support on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) through its Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) branch, giving eligible institutional clients access to its digital asset custody infrastructure.
Standard Chartered plans to extend its collateral-mirroring model to LMAX Group, an institutional trading company, allowing clients to use RLUSD as trading collateral while keeping the tokens in the bank’s custody.
The model would let LMAX recognize the value of eligible RLUSD holdings without requiring clients to transfer the tokens to its trading platform. Standard Chartered said this could reduce transfer-related risks and help institutions manage their exposure to trading counterparties.
Ripple, the blockchain payments company behind RLUSD, and LMAX Group previously announced a partnership in January 2026 to expand institutional use of the stablecoin.
Standard Chartered said the additional collateral capabilities remain subject to final documentation, testing, regulatory requirements and internal approvals.
Cointelegraph contacted Standard Chartered for further details and will update this article upon receiving a response.
Related: Standard Chartered plans institutional crypto custody in Singapore

articles.title: Ledger Says All Confirmed Cases in Suspected $87M Drain Tied to Reseller CryptoBilis - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ledger said every confirmed case in last week's wallet-draining incident involves devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.
- The company said the number of affected devices is "limited," that it is working with authorities, and that CryptoBilis has ceased all hardware wallet sales.
- Ledger told authorized resellers never to restock returned products, and urged buyers to avoid unauthorized sellers.
Ledger said all confirmed cases in last week's draining incident involve devices sold through reseller CryptoBilis, and that its own systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected, in a 72-hour update on Sunday.
"The volume of impacted devices is limited," the Paris-based hardware wallet manufacturer said, adding that it is working with relevant authorities and reaching out to affected users. It said CryptoBilis has confirmed it has ceased all sales of hardware wallets.
72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident 🔽
As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.…
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 11, 2026
Ledger began investigating on Friday after users in Southeast Asia who bought devices from CryptoBilis reported losing funds. Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts across Ethereum, Tron and Bitcoin. Ledger has not confirmed that figure or said what caused the losses.
Onchain investigators YFarmX said they had sent Ledger a list of more than 450 drained wallets. According to their analysis, the thief pushed 2,810 ETH through coin mixer Tornado Cash in three runs, moved the withdrawals through Zcash's shielded pool, and withdrew about 3.28 million USDC into three fresh wallets, which Circle could freeze.
The thief also converted 15 million of the stolen USDT into USDD, a stablecoin Tether cannot freeze, before swapping 5.1 million back into USDT and sending about 4.23 million USDT to Binance deposit addresses, YFarmX said. Tether froze 10 million USDT on the first day, while 15,475 ETH, 203 BTC and 10 million USDD remain out of reach, according to the firm. Its findings have not been independently verified.
An X user, Johannes, has claimed to have found tampered Ledger devices in Europe, after buying two devices from retail stores. He said both had "identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module)," and called on Ledger to issue a product recall.
The claims have not been independently verified, and Ledger's update said all confirmed cases so far involve CryptoBilis devices. He said he is sending the second device to Ledger for analysis. Decrypt has reached out to Ledger for comment on the European reports.
Reseller controls
In its update, Ledger said it is reminding authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and "never to restock returned products."
It also warned users against buying from unauthorized resellers, where "the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important."
The company said it is reviewing reseller controls and advancing hardware protections, and called on others in the industry to work with it on supply-chain and anti-tamper practices.
Ledger repeated its advice that CryptoBilis buyers should not set up unused devices, and that anyone who already has should move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger.
It also warned that scammers may try to exploit the incident, saying it "will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase."

articles.title: Standard Chartered brings Ripple's RLUSD into banking custody after $765 million quarterly surge
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Standard Chartered has launched custody for Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, with plans to integrate it into LMAX's institutional trading infrastructure.
- RLUSD's supply has reached $2.4 billion after adding $765 million in Q3, making it one of the fastest-growing stablecoins.
- The planned collateral integration could unlock new institutional demand, but the companies have yet to announce a launch date.
Standard Chartered has launched custody for Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin as it prepares to expand its use as collateral for institutional trading.
On Oct. 12, the bank announced that eligible institutional clients can now hold RLUSD issued on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) through its Dubai International Financial Center branch, regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority.
The launch forms part of a broader arrangement with Ripple and trading group LMAX that would allow institutions to use RLUSD as collateral while keeping their stablecoin holdings with Standard Chartered.
Under the proposed model, the bank would mirror the value of eligible RLUSD holdings to LMAX, enabling clients to support trading positions without transferring the underlying tokens directly to the venue.
The arrangement could reduce counterparty exposure and operational risks associated with moving assets between custodians and exchanges, while allowing institutions to deploy capital across trading activities.
Ripple expands RLUSD's institutional reach after rapid supply growth
The development comes as RLUSD emerges as one of the fastest-growing stablecoins by absolute market value added, reflecting Ripple's efforts to expand its use across financial markets.
According to RWA Foundation, Ripple recorded the second-largest increase in stablecoin market capitalization during the third quarter, adding $765.3 million over 90 days.
Only Circle's USDC posted a larger increase, $915 million, while United Stables ranked third at $474.2 million.
Data from DeFiLlama shows RLUSD's total circulating supply has since climbed to about $2.4 billion, with about $1.14 billion issued on XRPL and another $1.3 billion on Ethereum.
The expansion gives Ripple a larger pool of dollar-denominated tokens as it seeks to establish RLUSD beyond payments and transfers, including as collateral for institutional trading.
That effort gained momentum in January when Ripple and LMAX announced a multiyear partnership to integrate RLUSD across the trading group's infrastructure.
Ripple committed $150 million in financing to support LMAX's expansion, with the agreement targeting RLUSD adoption across spot cryptocurrency trading, perpetual futures, contracts for difference, and other institutional products.
Standard Chartered's involvement adds a traditional banking custody channel to the arrangement, allowing participating institutions to maintain custody arrangements with the bank while accessing LMAX's trading infrastructure.
Waqar Chaudry, Standard Chartered's global head of digital assets in Securities Services, said institutional investors increasingly want to participate in digital asset markets without compromising asset safeguarding and risk management.
For Ripple, accepting RLUSD as trading collateral could drive additional demand from banks, brokers, and investment firms that need dollar-denominated assets to support their positions.
However, the commercial impact will depend on how widely institutions adopt the arrangement and which LMAX products ultimately accept the stablecoin.
Standard Chartered has not disclosed the amount of RLUSD held in custody or identified participating institutional clients.
The companies have also not announced when the collateral integration will become operational. Implementation remains subject to final documentation, technical testing, regulatory requirements and internal approvals across relevant jurisdictions.
Those remaining steps will determine when institutions can begin using RLUSD held at Standard Chartered to support trading positions on LMAX.

articles.title: Jeonbuk Bank Offers Bitcoin-Backed Corporate Loans: Report
articles.text:
South Korean bank launches Bitcoin-backed business loans: Report
Jeonbuk Bank reportedly began offering Bitcoin-backed loans to corporate customers, with a third-party custodian holding the cryptocurrency used as collateral.
South Korea’s Jeonbuk Bank, a subsidiary of JB Financial Group, reportedly started issuing Bitcoin-backed loans to its corporate customers.
Local outlet EDaily reported Monday that Jeonbuk Bank became the country’s first commercial bank to accept Bitcoin (BTC) as collateral for won-denominated lending. The bank is reportedly limiting the service to businesses seeking operational capital, while a specialized custodian holds the BTC used as collateral.
The lending arrangement follows amendments to South Korea’s Civil Enforcement Rules that took effect on Oct. 1. According to the Supreme Court, the rules establish procedures for seizing and liquidating claims to virtual assets. In the event of a default, the bank can recover its funds through court-ordered sales.
Jeonbuk Bank has adopted a system that allows it to recover outstanding loans through the proceeds of cryptocurrency sales without directly taking possession of the assets, according to EDaily.
The bank has not publicly disclosed the loan amount, interest rate, or loan-to-value requirements. A bank representative told local outlet Chosun that it had already issued a loan but declined to identify the borrower.
Cointelegraph reached out to JB Financial Group for confirmation, but did not receive an immediate response.
Related: South Korea crypto exchange profits fall 78% in H1 amid trading slump

articles.title: NEXTPredict Paid $12,000 to Hedge Its Conference on a Prediction Market - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- NEXTPredict bought contracts on Kalshi that pay out if more than half of flights into JFK are canceled on October 21.
- The premium was $12,000 against roughly $3 million of coverage, the organizer's full investment in the event.
- Susquehanna took the other side as market maker, in what the parties call the first conference hedged on a prediction market.
The organizers of a prediction markets conference have hedged the conference on a prediction market, paying a $12,000 premium for contracts that would return around $3 million if New York's airports seize up the day before it opens.
The trade, executed through Kalshi with Susquehanna as market maker, settles on whether more than half of flights scheduled to land at John F. Kennedy International Airport are canceled on October 21, the main travel day before NEXTPredict's October 22-23 summit at Convene in Hudson Yards. The $3 million represents the organizer's total investment in the event.
This is me announcing a conference that never happened.
Today we hedged our next one on a prediction market. $3 million in coverage for a $12,000 premium, executed through @Kalshi with @SusquehannaSIG as market maker.
First time anyone in our event industry has done it. Here… pic.twitter.com/UtiA1xTXJw
— Pierre Lindh (@Pierreobv) July 28, 2026
The threshold was chosen as a proxy, Pierre Lindh, co-founder and managing director of NEXT.io, told Decrypt. “We had a conversation with Kalshi and Susquehanna, and we said, ‘Why don’t we use airport disruption as the vector?’ Because if there is 50% flight cancellation from JFK on the 21st of October, it means that something has happened in the world."
