The risk is all too real. Lindh opened a thread on the trade with an image of himself announcing a conference in 2020 that never took place. "A few months later the entire world locked down and we lost 100% of our revenue for the entire year," he wrote.
Across 13 years and around 800 events the exposure has recurred. A blizzard hit New York weeks before the company's March show there, and conflict in the Middle East escalated shortly before it opened, leaving delegates unable to travel and the company processing refunds, he said. By May, with its flagship Malta event approaching, the worry was European airports running short of fuel.
"Event insurance is focused around what happens inside the venue," Lindh told Decrypt, describing cover for fires, rigging failures and injuries. Standard force majeure cover typically only pays out when an event is canceled. If a hurricane closes the airport, he said, "it doesn't mean that we have to cancel our conference. It probably means that we will need to organize it but short-handed." The costs are already sunk and the revenue is already lost, but the policy may never trigger, he told trade publication G3 Newswire. "The material financial damage has already happened, but standard event insurance might not trigger because the conference itself went ahead."
Force majeure has historically "just been accepted as part of the deal," he said. "You commit millions, you cross your fingers."
Lindh's second objection is the claim itself: insurance is slow to arrange and, he says, "when the moment comes, the insurer's incentive is to find the reason not to pay."
A market settles differently. Claiming on a policy means a potential argument with the insurer over whether the circumstances qualify, Lindh told the trade publication G3 Newswire, whereas on a prediction market, "Kalshi is in the middle determining whether the conditions of the contract have been met."
Kalshi self-certified the flight cancellation contracts with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on July 14 and built this market to order after NEXT.io approached it as an institutional customer. Retail traders cannot access it. Certain causes of disruption, including drone incidents and bomb threats, do not trigger payment.
The contracts drew criticism when they appeared, on the grounds that someone could profit by disrupting flights. Lindh addressed it directly, calling the worry fair and arguing that the hedge is the other face of the same instrument: "A business with real exposure, buying protection, on a regulated venue, with an institutional market maker taking the other side."
Both counterparties see a larger market behind it. Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour called it "prediction markets moving beyond forecasting and becoming practical business infrastructure." Joe Grubb, who heads prediction markets business development at Susquehanna, said the structure allows the transfer of institutional risk "that historically had no path for execution."
Lindh expects company. "Our whole industry has been carrying this risk on the chin for decades because there was no instrument for it," he wrote. "Now there is one."
Brought to you by NEXTPredict
Learn More about partnering with Decrypt.

articles.title: Bitcoin options price a quiet CPI week while shorts cluster at $76,000–$80,000
articles.text:
Quick Take
- An Oct. 12 Deribit snapshot puts $451 million in underlying notional at the $76,000, $78,000 and $80,000 put strikes for Friday’s expiry.
- Friday’s outstanding puts exceed calls by about 43%, while later-dated calls carry substantial exposure at higher strikes.
- Laevitas reports seven-day implied volatility at 32.01%, down from 34.5%, as Wednesday’s CPI approaches.
Bitcoin options expiring Friday carry substantial put exposure below the market price, while short-term volatility pricing has fallen ahead of Wednesday's US inflation report.
Data from Coinbase-owned Deribit, a crypto options exchange, showed that in an Oct. 12 snapshot the Oct. 16 settlement carried approximately 15,502 BTC in outstanding options, comprising 9,128 BTC in puts and 6,373 BTC in calls. The put-to-call ratio stands at 1.43, with about $451 million in underlying notional exposure concentrated in puts at $76,000, $78,000 and $80,000.
The snapshot put Bitcoin near $83,450 after last week's selloff, while derivatives platform Laevitas reports declining short-term volatility expectations ahead of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) release.
Bitcoin puts cluster between $76,000 and $80,000
Deribit's options data shows the largest concentration of puts at the $80,000 strike, with outstanding contracts carrying about $188 million in underlying notional exposure.
Another $162 million is concentrated at $78,000, while the $76,000 strike accounts for approximately $101 million.
Combined, the three levels represent nearly 35% of the $1.29 billion options expiry, highlighting the scale of downside positioning after Bitcoin briefly fell toward $80,000 during last week's market downturn.
Additional put exposure worth about $89 million is concentrated at $83,000, near Bitcoin's current trading price.
The concentration suggests traders remain concerned about renewed selling pressure, although put open interest also includes contracts sold by investors seeking to collect premiums rather than exclusively buyers seeking protection.
Deribit data shows approximately $94 million in call exposure at $90,000, followed by $70 million at $87,000 and $55 million at $85,000.
Together, the three levels account for $219 million in outstanding notional exposure, less than half the amount concentrated at the three major downside put strikes.
The distribution leaves Bitcoin's largest downside positions relatively close to prices tested during the recent decline, while the $90,000 call strike requires an advance of nearly 8% from current levels.
Meanwhile, Deribit's maximum pain calculation stands at $83,000, indicating the settlement level that would minimize the aggregate intrinsic value of outstanding options based on current positioning.
Later-dated Bitcoin options also carry substantial upside exposure: Deribit’s Oct. 30 expiry has approximately $4.54 billion in call notional across the $90,000, $95,000 and $100,000 strikes.
Bitcoin volatility expectations retreat before Wednesday's CPI
Laevitas’s Oct. 12 brief described a volatility curve that prices Wednesday’s CPI as a non-event.
Bitcoin's seven-day at-the-money implied volatility declined to 32.01% from approximately 34.5% a week earlier.
That compares with 34.66% for 30-day contracts, 37.29% for 90-day options and 38.24% for 180-day maturities.
For illustration, converting the annualized seven-day implied volatility to a weekly move at the $83,450 snapshot price gives a one-standard-deviation move of roughly 4.4%, or $3,700, under conventional volatility assumptions.
That would place the modeled weekly range between approximately $79,750 and $87,150, encompassing the $80,000 put strike but falling short of the substantial call concentration at $90,000.
Meanwhile, Laevitas reported that Bitcoin's seven-day 25-delta options skew shifted from +1.98 to -2.40 over the past week, a 4.38-point reversal.
Laevitas characterized the move as an unwind from a call-bid extreme toward nominally put-bid pricing, with puts still cheaper relative to calls than their 52-week median.
Bitcoin perpetual-futures open interest fell 1.9% over the past week to approximately $29.33 billion, while annualized funding rates stood at 5.6%, according to Laevitas.
The positioning comes as investors assess whether US inflation could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again at its Oct. 27-28 policy meeting.
MarketWatch’s Oct. 12 preview cited expectations for September headline inflation to accelerate to approximately 3.7% annually from 3.4% in August, partly reflecting higher energy costs. Monthly core inflation, which excludes food and energy, is forecast to rise 0.2%.
Laevitas described an October increase as close to priced out, with December pricing around an 85% probability of a hike.
However, elevated oil prices and Treasury yields continue to complicate the outlook for risk assets, with stronger-than-expected inflation potentially reviving expectations of another rate increase.
In illustrative price scenarios, hotter inflation could pressure Bitcoin toward the heavily populated $78,000–$80,000 put strikes, while softer inflation could encourage a recovery toward the higher call concentrations.
The CPI report arrives Wednesday, Oct. 14, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, followed by producer-price inflation and retail-sales data Thursday, Oct. 15, giving traders two days of economic releases to absorb before Friday's $1.29 billion options expiry.
Bitcoin is -3.07% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

articles.title: Solana’s offline-signing proposal would keep approvals valid after failed transactions
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Solana proposes replacing durable nonces with signer programs, preserving offline approval while changing affected account authorities.
- Both proposed designs can leave failed approvals executable later, making deadline enforcement and nonce revocation material custody controls.
- Durable nonces remain usable, with removal conditional on an audited mainnet replacement and no fixed activation date.
Solana’s plan to retire durable nonces, which let transactions be signed offline and broadcast later, would preserve cold-key approval while changing which addresses control the affected assets. For exchanges, custodians and treasury operators using that signing method, the proposed replacement adds a program between the cold key’s approval and execution.
The Solana Foundation’s October deprecation plan points to onchain signer programs that verify an offline signature and execute its approved instructions. A program-derived address, or PDA, would control the affected accounts. The original key would still authorize actions, while a separate online operator submits them and pays the network fee.
The replacement creates a different custody architecture: operators must migrate the relevant assets or permissions, applications must accept actions arriving through another program, and risk teams must approve the new signing path.
Durable nonces remain usable. The Foundation has not set a removal date or made a final choice between Anza’s Programmatic Signer and Blueshift’s Vector. Its roughly six-month migration window is conditional on a suitable replacement being ready, audited and live on mainnet.
The key keeps approving, but the account changes
Durable nonces solve a timing problem. Instead of signing a transaction tied to a recent blockhash that soon expires, an offline signer can approve one using a stored nonce. That allows approval and broadcast to happen at different times.
Solana’s separate 200ms slot upgrade reached its final mainnet stage on Oct. 9. Faster block production leaves less wall-clock time for ordinary blockhash-based approvals, although expiry depends on block production rather than a guaranteed timer. CryptoSlate’s earlier coverage examined that timing change; the nonce proposal concerns the architecture used to avoid the short approval window.
Under Programmatic Signer, the cold key signs an authorization message rather than the transaction sent to the network. A relayer places that approval in a fresh-blockhash transaction. The signer program verifies the authorization and executes the approved instructions with the key’s derived address as signer.
The PDA has no private key of its own. Its ability to act comes from the signer program verifying the original key’s approval. Deriving the address does not move any assets or permissions: those must be transferred separately.
The migration guide describes moving native SOL into the derived address, transferring token balances into accounts controlled by it, and moving mint or freeze permissions to it. Stake accounts can move the staker authority, withdraw authority or both, depending on the permission being migrated. These are separate controls, rather than one universal wallet switch.
The Foundation proposes completing those handoffs while legacy durable nonces still work. For an affected treasury, approving the new signing software is therefore only part of the job. Its account inventory and the permissions each key currently holds determine what must change.
The two candidate designs also handle native SOL differently. Programmatic Signer’s derived SOL account is System-owned and can send SOL through an approved ordinary transfer. Vector initializes a program-owned account and releases SOL through its own authorized withdrawal or closing operation.
What the cold signature lets a relayer do
The implementation choice affects how tightly an approval constrains the transaction around it.
Programmatic Signer’s message documentation says the cold signatures bind the executor, nonce account and embedded execution message. A relayer cannot alter those authorized bytes while retaining valid signatures. It can, however, choose the outer fee payer and blockhash and add instructions before or after the submission.
Vector commits to the top-level instruction buffer, including the data and accounts used to pass approved actions into other programs. Instructions surrounding those actions must already be included when the cold key signs. A relayer cannot insert, remove or reorder them afterward without invalidating the approval.
Programmatic Signer allows an execution context to be assembled around an approved action; Vector requires the surrounding instruction sequence to be approved in advance. In both cases, paying for broadcast does not grant permission to rewrite the signed action.
| Control | Programmatic Signer | Vector | 
|---|---|---|
| Cold approval covers | The authorization and embedded execution message | The committed top-level instruction buffer | 
| Extra surrounding instructions | Relayer may add them outside the authorization | Must be included before signing | 
| Replay state | A separate program nonce account | Nonce stored in the Vector account | 
| Derived-address setup | No signer-address registration | Account initialized under the Vector program | 
A failed execution attempt can leave a cold approval executable later. A current durable-nonce transaction that passes validation but fails during execution still consumes its nonce. Programmatic Signer’s architecture commits the nonce advance and application changes together, or rolls them back together. Vector documents the same ability to retry a failed action.
For operators, retryability means a failed submission has not necessarily invalidated the approval. Without an enforced deadline, it can remain available for later execution while its nonce is unchanged.
Vector explicitly warns that a relayer could withhold a transaction until conditions change, or that a signature exposed by a failed attempt could execute later. A timeout included in the signed instructions can reject execution after a deadline. Revocation requires a separately authorized nonce advance to land. A deadline rejection itself does not consume a nonce whose changes roll back with the failed transaction.
Application access is a separate custody test
The Foundation’s rationale is to simplify validator handling. Durable nonces require special replay-prevention rules, complicate asynchronous execution and make invalid transactions harder to filter. Moving approval and replay state into ordinary programs leaves validators processing normal blockhash transactions.
Applications then receive approved actions through cross-program invocation, or CPI: one program calls another. That can conflict with an application’s rule that an action must arrive directly as a top-level instruction. Checks that inspect only top-level repayment or signature-verification instructions can also miss an action nested inside the signer program.
More available call depth does not resolve a rule that rejects the call’s position or cannot inspect the nested instructions. The Foundation suggests supporting known signer programs or offering another execution path. Whether an application accepts a PDA’s signature is consequently a different question from whether the offline approval is cryptographically valid.
Token-2022’s CPI Guard shows why compatibility needs a precise account-level assessment. With the guard enabled, CPI transfers and burns require delegate authority; approvals through CPI are prohibited, and changing the owner is prohibited even outside CPI. Permanent delegates have transfer and burn exceptions.
Those rules are more specific than a blanket ban on every PDA action. A delegate-based transfer route may exist, but establishing or using that authority introduces its own permission and custody-policy decision.
Institutional concerns raised in March centered on application access and the controls under which funds may move. In the March 4 discussion, a participant identifying himself as Michael from Fireblocks supported nonce deprecation while objecting to CPI Passthrough’s migration, contract dependence and DeFi compatibility burdens. He favored transaction envelopes, with Sudo as an alternative, rather than the proposed CPI-based signing path.
Grant, who identified himself as being at Unit 410, said the same day that a small, auditable signer program might make authority migration acceptable. He rejected a workaround that temporarily moves assets to a hot signer, even for an atomic operation, because funds must remain associated with cold storage in its noncustodial model.
A testable design still needs a production migration path
Programmatic Signer’s current documentation reports devnet deployment and audits in progress, with remediation required before its v1 release and any mainnet deployment. Its interfaces may change. The usage documentation still marks simulation and relay submission as coming soon, while several migration operations are similarly unfinished in the guide.
Vector publishes implementation code and program IDs; its README does not state an audit or mainnet deployment status.
Meanwhile, Fireblocks’ current protocol onboarding kit still describes automatic durable-nonce injection for selected WalletConnect integrations, including Jupiter and Kamino, with a default provider-managed 15-minute validity window. That describes an existing approval workflow which a replacement must accommodate.
An operational migration needs an audited mainnet replacement, usable tools and application paths that retain each operator’s approval controls.

articles.title: FSB Outlines Stablecoin and AI Priorities for G20
articles.text:
Global watchdog flags stablecoin risks, AI threats ahead of G20
The Financial Stability Board flagged cross-border stablecoin risks and AI-related cybersecurity threats while urging G20 policymakers to support stronger safeguards.
The Financial Stability Board (FSB), a global financial watchdog, has outlined financial stability risks associated with artificial intelligence and regulatory concerns surrounding stablecoins.
In a letter published Monday, FSB Chair Andrew Bailey warned that cross-border mechanisms for stablecoin oversight and crisis management “remain immature or are not yet developed.” In its 2025 review, the FSB found that 11 of 28 surveyed jurisdictions had finalized stablecoin regulatory frameworks.
He also urged G20 members to support the FSB’s newly finalized practices for responsible AI adoption in the financial sector.
“AI therefore requires our continued close attention alongside careful management by financial institutions,” Bailey wrote.
The FSB submitted the letter to Group of Twenty (G20) finance ministers and central bank governors ahead of their Thursday meeting. The G20 brings together the world’s major economies to coordinate financial policy and regulatory priorities.
Stablecoin risks extend to traditional financial markets
In a report accompanying the letter, the FSB warned that stablecoin runs could spill into traditional markets through forced sales of reserve assets and withdrawals of bank deposits. The watchdog also identified risks for multi-issuer stablecoins where redemption demand could concentrate on one issuer while reserves are held in different jurisdictions.
These concerns echo what regulators have previously raised. In 2025, European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde warned of similar redemption risks involving stablecoins issued inside and outside of the European Union.
AI safeguards target cybersecurity and third-party risks
The FSB’s AI practices cover organization-wide governance, AI development and deployment, cybersecurity and third-party service risks. Bailey also warned that sophisticated cyber threats enabled by AI could undermine the resilience of critical financial institutions and market infrastructure.
Related: Tether, Kazakhstan cenbank mull tenge stablecoin and asset tokenization
The risks have similarly drawn regulatory attention. In July, European central bankers warned that advances in AI could amplify market volatility and cybersecurity threats.
In June, the FSB had proposed 12 practices for responsible AI adoption, before finalizing its guidance for the upcoming G20 meeting.
Magazine: China’s P2P stablecoin wallets surge 43x, Korea’s $450B crypto economy: Asia Express

articles.title: XRP Ledger’s Payment Engine Had a Counterfeiting Bug Hiding Since 2015 - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- XRP Ledger maintainers disclosed and patched a critical payment-engine overflow bug, reported via bug bounty in September, that could have let an attacker create counterfeit XRP.
- The flaw sat unnoticed since 2015 because no normal payment triggers it, and the ledger’s “no XRP created” safety check used the same broken arithmetic.
- There is no evidence the bug was ever exploited, XRP Ledger devs say.
Developers behind the XRP Ledger have disclosed and fixed a critical vulnerability that, left unaddressed, could have let an attacker conjure XRP out of thin air, a flaw that sat dormant in the network’s code for roughly a decade.
In a disclosure published Friday, the ledger’s maintainers said a researcher reported the bug through the XRPL bug bounty program in September. The issue was an integer overflow in the payment engine, the part of the software that processes payments.
When a single payment consumed hundreds of specially crafted offers from the order book, the sum of what the buyer owed exceeded the maximum value the system could store and “wrapped around” to a tiny number. The engine paid each seller in full but charged the buyer almost nothing, with the difference amounting to newly minted XRP that should never have existed.
Worse, the ledger’s built-in safety check meant to confirm no transaction creates XRP used the same flawed arithmetic, so it wrapped around identically and caught nothing. The maintainers said an attacker could have created spendable XRP far beyond the token’s total supply in a single transaction, then moved it, traded it or sent it to exchanges.
RippleX engineers confirmed the bug had been present since the current payment engine was written in 2015 and went unnoticed because no ordinary payment comes anywhere near triggering the overflow.
There is no evidence it was ever exploited, the team said. The fix shipped in version 3.4.1 on Sept. 25, and more than 80% of the network’s trusted validators were running it that day.
Notably, the patch bypassed the ledger’s usual amendment process, which requires validators to vote and wait two weeks before a change takes effect, the first time a transaction-processing change has deliberately shipped that way since the system was introduced over a decade ago. The maintainers said the severity justified it, since the open-source fix would have revealed the bug while leaving it exploitable for weeks.
The disclosure echoes a counterfeiting scare that rocked Zcash this year, when the privacy coin raced to patch a soundness bug in its shielded pool that could have allowed forged coins. That episode sent ZEC tumbling before the network’s Ironwood upgrade resolved it.
XRP didn’t escape the week unscathed. The token traded at $1.38 on Monday, down 1.6% over 24 hours, the worst performance among major cryptocurrencies, and off 9.4% over the past seven days.

articles.title: DATA Network to migrate to Sui, retire its own chain
articles.text:
DATA Network to migrate to Sui, retire own chain
The migration is backed by a $30 million investment from Sui Foundation.
DATA Network, formerly known as Story, is planning to retire its independent blockchain and move its AI training data protocol to Sui, backed by a $30 million investment from Sui Foundation.
The project’s Trace registry, which launched in June, will join the Sui ecosystem, while Walrus, a decentralized storage platform in the Sui ecosystem, will become the default storage layer for applications operated by DATA Foundation, its partners said on Monday.
Speaking to Cointelegraph, a DATA Foundation spokesperson said running a dedicated blockchain for a single use case meant carrying the costs of validators, network security and infrastructure.
“Building storage and access control at that scale ourselves would have meant rebuilding what Sui already has in Walrus and Seal,” they said.
The decision followed Story Foundation’s rebrand to DATA Foundation in June, pivoting from intellectual property licensing to building a “full stack for AI training data.” It also launched Trace to track the origin and licensing rights of training data.
As Trace grew to more than 270 million registrations in about four months, running an independent blockchain for one use case no longer made sense, the representative said.
The DATA Network will continue to operate until the upgrade is complete, and a detailed timeline and holder transition plan will be published prior to the upgrade, it said.
Asked how much Sui Foundation’s investment influenced the move, the representative said the $30 million investment was a separate part of the partnership.
DATA Network’s existing chain will continue operating until the upgrade is complete. The partners said a detailed timeline and holder transition plan would be published before the migration.
Related: Story Protocol rebrands to DATA Foundation in AI pivot

articles.title: Bitmine Adds $32M in Ethereum as Tom Lee Says Firm Is Nearly 'Done Stacking' - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitmine acquired 12,532 ETH over the past week, bringing its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, or 4.9% of Ethereum's supply.
- Chairman Tom Lee said the firm needs about 100,000 more ETH to reach its 5% target, after which it will be "done stacking."
- Lee predicted the largest crypto bull market ever, citing tokenization, a generational wealth transfer and supply held by treasury firms.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies bought 12,532 ETH over the past week, worth about $31.9 million at the $2,544 price the company used to value its holdings and lifting its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, the company said Monday.
The stash represents 4.9% of the total 122.1 million Ethereum token supply, leaving the firm 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5%, a target it calls the "Alchemy of 5%."
🧵
1/
BitMine provided its latest holdings update for October 12, 2026
$16.2 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":
- 6,028,946 ETH at $2,544 per ETH (per @coinbase)
- 214 Bitcoin (BTC)
- $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast
- $85 million stake in Eightco Holdings…
— Bitmine (NYSE-BMNR) $ETH $BMNP (@BitMNR) October 12, 2026
Bitmine bought $41 million more ETH the week before. In a press release, the firm's Chairman Tom Lee claimed that its “track record of consistent buying of crypto is unmatched by any public company in the world.”
The company valued its ETH at $2,544 per token, and put its total crypto, cash and investment holdings at $16.2 billion. That includes 214 BTC, $612 million in cash and marketable securities, and stakes worth $180 million in Beast Industries and $85 million in Eightco Holdings.
The firm has staked 5,067,309 ETH, which Lee said generates annualized staking revenue of about $336 million.
'Done stacking'
In his monthly Chairman's message last week, Lee said Bitmine needs "about 100,000 more ETH, and that's about it." He has said the firm's Ethereum buying will stop once it reaches its target.
"Now we're done stacking while a bull market is starting," Lee said in the video. "So if we're done stacking, but ETH goes up a lot, you can imagine that we'll outperform Ethereum."
Lee predicted the crypto bull market would be "the biggest bull market we've ever seen," driven by tokenization, a wealth transfer to younger investors, supply absorbed by digital asset treasury firms, and AI agents using crypto wallets.
He said Bitmine shares, then around $26, are 90% correlated with ETH, and projected that ETH at $22,000 would put the stock at $300 to $500.
Lee also pointed to Bitmine's 9.5% perpetual preferred stock, BMNP, which was issued at $80 in June and last closed at $99.53, according to the release.

articles.title: Eclair merges fixes for Lightning flaws that could burn Bitcoin in fees
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Eclair merged October repairs that limit peer-selected replacement fees when nodes contribute funds to channel openings or splices.
- In Eclair-signer mode, new checks verify actual fees against supplied budgets and confirm rebuilt contributions pay the same fee.
- September's v0.14.3 remains the latest listed release, so the October merges alone do not confirm a packaged upgrade.
Eclair, ACINQ's Lightning node software, has merged two repairs for gaps that could make a node lose Bitcoin through excessive mining fees during channel funding and splicing. One limits a peer's fee-bump demands when Eclair contributes funds; the other checks transactions from a compromised Bitcoin backend while Eclair retains the signing keys.
The repairs merged into the project's master branch on Oct. 2 and Oct. 5. As of Oct. 12, its release page still listed September's v0.14.3 as latest. The two October fixes postdate that packaged release.
Bitcoin Optech's Oct. 9 newsletter highlighted both changes as closing protection gaps during dual funding and splicing.
The first repair, PR #3388, concerns peer-initiated replace-by-fee, or RBF, attempts during a dual-funded channel opening or a splice that adjusts a channel's funding. A peer could request a replacement transaction with a higher fee rate. Eclair kept its wallet contribution and paid for its inputs at that rate, without an upper bound or fee budget on this path.
That let a malicious peer impose an arbitrary mining fee rate on the contributing node while contributing nothing itself. The loss would be paid as fees to miners rather than transferred directly to the peer.
The repair rejects attempts above the maximum funding fee rate Eclair recommends to its peer. Two exceptions remain: the peer buys liquidity and pays the fees for Eclair's inputs, or the Eclair node contributes no funds to the transaction. In those cases, Eclair does not bear the cost addressed by this limit.
Keeping keys is only part of the defense
PR #3390 addresses a separate threat in Eclair-signer mode. Bitcoin Core's backend, bitcoind, selects coins and builds transactions, while Eclair retains the keys and signs.
A compromised backend could report a fee within budget while constructing a transaction that actually paid more, including by dropping the change output. Under Bitcoin's transaction accounting, input value not assigned to outputs becomes a miner fee. Missing change can therefore spend funds without paying an attacker's address.
When a fee budget is supplied, the repair calculates the actual fee from the amounts of the coins being spent, fetched by transaction ID to authenticate their values. It checks that the backend's reported fee matches and applies the budget to the actual fee. It also checks that Eclair's rebuilt contributions pay the same verified fee and rejects invalid change-output positions.
These are distinct from the cooperative-closing fee flaw covered in CryptoSlate's September report and the restart denial-of-service issues covered Oct. 2.
These repairs address Eclair's dual-funding, splicing and signer configurations. Operators should check that their installed build contains the October changes.

articles.title: Strategy Scoops Up $21.5M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $192M in STRC - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy bought 250 BTC for $21.5 million last week, at an average price of $86,194 per coin, bringing its holdings to 848,250 BTC.
- The company also repurchased 1.93 million shares of its STRC preferred stock for $192.4 million.
- Strategy funded the Bitcoin purchase mainly by selling $21 million of MSTR common stock, and holds $5.5 billion in U.S. dollar assets.
Strategy bought 250 BTC last week and spent $192.4 million repurchasing its STRC preferred stock, the company said on Monday.
The Bitcoin treasury firm paid $21.5 million for the coins between October 5 and October 11, an average of $86,194 per Bitcoin including fees, according to its release. It now holds 848,250 BTC, a new record, acquired for a total of $64 billion at an average of $75,444 per coin.
Strategy raised $21 million by selling about 125,000 shares of its MSTR common stock through its at-the-market offering program, and used $500,000 of cash to cover the rest. It sold none of its preferred stock during the week.
The company repurchased 1,932,145 shares of STRC, its variable-rate Stretch preferred stock, leaving $354.8 million available under its program to buy back preferred shares.
Last week, Strategy bought $29 million in Bitcoin and repurchased $176 million of STRC as it posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain.
Strategy's dollar reserves
As of October 11, Strategy held $4.88 billion in a U.S. dollar reserve set aside for preferred dividends and debt interest, and $640.5 million in cash for broader purposes such as buying Bitcoin.
Strategy set up its USD reserve with $1.44 billion, and later established the separate USD cash pot after raising $2 billion by selling MSTR stock.
The company has also proposed that its preferred stock dividends accrue 365 days a year, and has said it could sell up to $1.25 billion of Bitcoin under its digital credit capital framework.
Strategy CEO Phong Le defended selling Bitcoin as the "right trade" in September, weeks before the firm set a new holdings record at the end of the month with a $143 million purchase. Despite the uptick in buying, traders on prediction market Myriad, owned by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, do not expect the firm's holdings to surpass one million BTC by the end of the year, putting just a 5% chance on that outcome.

articles.title: France Lawmakers Back $112K Crypto Wallet Disclosure Proposal
articles.text:
French lawmakers back reporting rule for crypto wallets over $112K
Holders could face fines of up to 10,000 euros for failing to declare qualifying assets.
French lawmakers have backed a proposal that would require holders of self-custodied crypto assets to report holdings equal or above 100,000 euros ($112,000) or face penalties.
The amendment, numbered I-CF821, was adopted by the National Assembly’s Finance Committee on Friday, and would introduce reporting requirements for crypto that isn’t held by a crypto-asset service provider, including assets stored in personal wallets.
The amendment would add a provision to France’s general tax code. Under the proposal, holders would be required to disclose holdings based on their value as of Dec. 31, and could face fines up to 10,000 euros for failing to declare.
The sponsors said the measure was intended to combat tax evasion, citing a parliamentary inquiry into the taxation of wealthy individuals, which found that crypto capital gains reached 3.5 billion euros in 2021, while only 400 million euros in crypto holdings were declared to tax authorities that year.
Proposal faces legislative hurdles
The amendment was introduced by Charles de Courson, Jean-Pierre Bataille and Michel Castellani, three members of France’s Liberties, Independents, Overseas and Territories (LIOT) parliamentary group.
The wallet disclosure measure was among five crypto-related amendments adopted by the Finance Committee last week.
Other proposals previously reported by Cointelegraph included imposing an exit tax on cryptocurrency holdings exceeding 800,000 euros when taxpayers move abroad and ending tax deferrals on conversions into fiat-backed stablecoins.
Related: French lawmakers back stablecoin swap tax in 2027 budget bill
However, while the Finance Committee adopted the amendments on Friday, it subsequently rejected the revenue section of the broader 2027 budget bill by 31 votes to 3.
Lawmakers are scheduled to begin debating the revenue section of the budget in the National Assembly on Tuesday, starting from the government’s original draft.
The crypto amendments would need to be submitted again and approved during the parliamentary proceedings before becoming part of the legislation, according to French tech publication Clubic.
Magazine: Ledger attack spreads to EU, AI finds ’18 trillion XRP’ bug: Hodler’s Digest

articles.title: France’s tax proposal would tax Bitcoin-to-USDC swaps before investors cash out
articles.text:
Quick Take
- France’s committee-approved amendment would recognize gains or losses on swaps into MiCA e-money tokens, before any cash withdrawal.
- Pre-2027 holdings would have two basis routes; the irrevocable allocation option could shift how much gain the first disposal recognizes.
- Taxable swaps would reset received tokens’ basis, while existing rules would still prevent net crypto losses offsetting later-year gains.
France’s proposed crypto tax changes would make a move from Bitcoin or Ether into certain stablecoins a taxable disposal, even if the investor never withdraws cash.
The National Assembly’s Finance Committee adopted amendment I-CF1826 on Oct. 7, adding that proposed exception to a broader overhaul of how private crypto gains are calculated. The provision would apply to disposals and exchanges from Jan. 1, 2027 if enacted.
For an investor selling Bitcoin exposure into USDC, the consequence would be a change in the tax timing of a risk-reduction trade. A gain could become reportable while the proceeds remain in a crypto wallet or exchange account. But the proposal also changes the cost deducted from those proceeds, and gives older holdings a transition choice.
Under French tax authority guidance, covered crypto-to-crypto exchanges without a cash balancing payment receive tax deferral. Converting into fiat or using crypto to obtain other goods or services can already be taxable under the private-disposal regime, subject to its applicable exemption.
CF1826 would remove the exchange deferral when the investor receives e-money tokens as defined by the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, or related rights. The operative wording targets the asset received. A swap out of Bitcoin into a qualifying token could therefore recognize a gain before any later cash withdrawal.
MiCA’s definition describes a crypto-asset that seeks to maintain stable value by reference to one official currency. That legal definition sets the exception’s scope. The amendment invokes it without an express issuer-licensing condition.
USDC provides a concrete example: Circle’s European white paper identifies it as an e-money token under the same MiCA provision. The illustrations below use native USDC, with transactions measured in euros.
The amendment’s sponsors justify the change by describing deferral on fiat-backed stablecoin conversions as a legislative loophole. For an investor using a swap to reduce market exposure, the practical effect would be earlier recognition of any gain.
The proposed tax calculation concerns the gain above cost. It subtracts the acquisition basis of the assets surrendered from the disposal price. That basis is the cost recognized for tax purposes; a transaction can produce a gain, no gain or a loss.
Two ways to value older holdings
France’s existing portfolio-based calculation allocates part of the acquisition price of the entire crypto portfolio to each taxable disposal. Current guidance deducts total portfolio acquisition price multiplied by the ratio of disposal price to portfolio value immediately before the transaction.
The proposed replacement would focus on the crypto-assets actually disposed of. For assets of the same nature purchased at different prices, it specifies weighted-average acquisition value.
For holdings acquired before 2027, the amendment offers two routes. An investor could use evidenced actual acquisition costs, determined under the new basis rules. Alternatively, the investor could allocate the portfolio acquisition price calculated under the old rules at Dec. 31, 2026 among the assets held then, in proportion to their values on that date.
The allocation option preserves a pool of acquisition cost and distributes it among holdings. The available cost pool remains the acquisition price calculated under the old rules, rather than the portfolio’s full market value. The text makes that choice irrevocable for the entire portfolio when the first return reporting a taxable disposal after Jan. 1, 2027 is filed.
Consider a hypothetical investor whose Bitcoin cost €20,000 and is worth €60,000, while their Ether cost €40,000 and is worth €40,000 at the transition date. The portfolio has €60,000 of acquisition cost and a €100,000 value. Assume no prior disposals, fees or cash balancing payments, no other holdings of the same tokens, and unchanged euro values through the transactions.
Under the allocation option, Bitcoin represents 60% of the portfolio value and receives €36,000 of basis. Ether receives the remaining €24,000. Using actual costs instead would leave their bases at €20,000 and €40,000, respectively.
The same Bitcoin-to-USDC transaction would then produce different first-disposal gains:
| Hypothetical transaction or basis | Proposed actual-cost route | Proposed allocation route | 
|---|---|---|
| Bitcoin basis before the swap | €20,000 | €36,000 | 
| Gain on swap into €60,000 of native USDC | €40,000 | €24,000 | 
| Basis of the USDC received | €60,000 | €60,000 | 
| Gain on later Ether disposal for €40,000 | €0 | €16,000 | 
The table compares hypothetical gross gains under the proposal. Under the current rules, the qualifying swap itself would receive deferral. Under either proposed transition route, the Bitcoin-to-USDC swap would become a taxable event.
Changing only the historical costs to €50,000 for Bitcoin and €10,000 for Ether reverses the first-disposal comparison: actual cost would produce a €10,000 Bitcoin gain against allocation’s €24,000. The remaining Ether gain at unchanged values would be €30,000 under actual cost or €16,000 under allocation. Historical costs determine which method recognizes more gain first.
Basis resets and the cost of loss timing
The proposal expressly distinguishes exchanges that retain deferral from exchanges that become taxable. A deferred exchange carries the surrendered assets’ basis into the assets received. A taxable exchange gives the received crypto-assets a basis based on the consideration value already used to calculate the gain, adjusted for any cash balancing payment.
For the Bitcoin-to-USDC swap in the first example, the reset rule would give the USDC received €60,000 of basis under either transition route. Selling it later for the same €60,000 would produce no further gain. That reset would prevent repeat recognition of the original Bitcoin gain when the unchanged-value proceeds finally reached a bank account.
USDC references the dollar, so the unchanged-euro-value assumption is essential. A later disposal at a different euro value would require its own gain or loss calculation.
If the investor also sold the remaining Ether for €40,000, the first example would produce aggregate realized gains of €40,000 under either proposed transition route. Actual cost recognizes all of that in Bitcoin; allocation splits it between Bitcoin and Ether.
The amendment would change the swap exception and basis rules without rewriting the existing crypto loss restriction. The tax authority says crypto gains and losses offset within the same tax year, while a net crypto loss cannot be carried into later years or used against gains on other assets.
A separate hypothetical shows the effect of recognizing losses and gains in different years. Under the proposed actual-basis rules, a sole Bitcoin holding bought for €30,000 and swapped into €20,000 of native USDC would recognize a €10,000 loss. The USDC would receive €20,000 of basis.
If that USDC were later exchanged into Bitcoin without a cash balancing payment, the swap would retain deferral because Bitcoin is outside the received e-money-token exception. It would carry the €20,000 basis into Bitcoin. A subsequent taxable Bitcoin sale for €30,000 would recognize a €10,000 gain. Assume no fees, other token pools, cash adjustments or other gains and losses.
Those amounts could offset if realized in the same tax year. If the net loss arose in one year and the gain in a later year, the earlier loss would not shelter that later gain under the existing rule. Recognition in different years can therefore change the taxable result even when the transaction sequence returns the holding to its original value.
The reporting trade-off follows from the same mechanics. Asset-specific basis would remove the portfolio-wide allocation formula for new disposals, but investors would need to preserve acquisition evidence, weighted averages and the basis carried or reset through swaps. For older holdings, the proposed allocation route would also require a Dec. 31 valuation and a whole-portfolio decision that the text makes irrevocable.
The next legislative test remains ahead. The 2027 budget dossier, checked Oct. 12, lists National Assembly plenary discussion for Oct. 13.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s rebound approaches the $85,000 zone where past buyers may sell
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin climbed above $84,000 while Ethereum reclaimed $2,500 as both cryptocurrencies extended their weekend recovery.
- Bitcoin approaches a dense $84,000–$85,000 acquisition-cost zone; Ethereum still had 10.58 million ETH of futures open interest in an Oct. 10 snapshot.
- A failed Bitcoin breakout could expose $77,000–$79,000 support, while renewed ETH volatility risks triggering fresh liquidations.
Bitcoin and Ethereum extended their weekend recovery, although on-chain indicators and derivatives positioning suggest the rebound faces significant obstacles.
Data from CryptoSlate showed that Bitcoin briefly climbed above $84,000 after falling toward $80,000 during last week's selloff. Ethereum also recovered above $2,500, reversing part of its recent losses as buying activity returned to the cryptocurrency market.
However, Bitcoin's advance has brought it closer to a major concentration of investor acquisition costs between $84,000 and $85,000, where selling pressure could intensify. Meanwhile, Ethereum's recovery comes as larger derivatives traders appear to be reducing their bullish exposure despite substantial outstanding positions.
Bitcoin's $85,000 resistance threatens to stall recovery
Bitcoin's recovery gained momentum during Sunday's trading session as traders appeared to capitalize on a liquidity concentration above the prevailing market price.
CryptoQuant analyst J.A. Maartunn said on Oct. 11 that a liquidity cluster formed just above Bitcoin's trading level, giving traders an opportunity to push prices higher.
According to Maartunn, traders appeared to establish a substantial wall of buy orders beneath the market, providing support as Bitcoin advanced toward the overhead liquidity.
The spot Bid/Ask Ratio, which measures buying and selling liquidity within 1% of the prevailing price, rose to 0.3.
The increase indicated that visible buying interest had strengthened relative to selling orders. Such liquidity can also disappear if traders cancel their orders.
Checkonchain data highlighted by analyst Darkfost on Oct. 11 showed that approximately 53% of Bitcoin's invested capital had an estimated acquisition price above $83,000 when the cryptocurrency traded around that level.
The measure weights acquisition prices by invested capital, so larger positions carry more weight.
More importantly, the largest concentration of acquisition costs sits between $84,000 and $85,000, making the region a potential obstacle to further gains.
Investors who acquired Bitcoin around those levels could become more willing to sell as prices approach their estimated cost basis, increasing the supply that buyers must absorb.
A sustained move through the region would suggest buying demand is strong enough to overcome that potential selling pressure. If it fails to do so, Bitcoin could be vulnerable to another decline, with Darkfost identifying the $77,000 to $79,000 range as a possible support area.
Ethereum's $2,500 rebound faces risk from leveraged traders
Ethereum's recovery faces another challenge as derivatives positioning among larger market participants continues to deteriorate.
Alphractal CEO Joao Wedson noted on Oct. 10 that Ethereum's 30-day and 180-day open-interest deltas were both negative, along with weakening readings in its Whale vs. Retail Delta indicator.
He interpreted the combination as evidence that major traders have reduced their bullish exposure while increasingly favoring defensive or short positions.
The negative open-interest readings indicate that outstanding derivatives positions have contracted over the measured periods.
Despite the contraction, Ethereum's total futures open interest remained substantial at approximately 10.58 million ETH, indicating that considerable derivatives exposure was still outstanding.
Valued at $2,500 per ETH, that represents roughly $26.5 billion in notional exposure.
The combination of weakening bullish positioning and substantial remaining exposure increases the potential for sharp price movements if volatility returns.
A renewed decline could push leveraged long positions toward forced liquidation, potentially adding selling pressure and accelerating losses. Conversely, a sustained recovery could force short sellers to close positions, contributing to further upward momentum.
Wedson warned that Ethereum's derivatives market remains vulnerable to further liquidations despite the recent reduction in outstanding positions.
Bitcoin is -3.07% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

articles.title: XRP Ledger Defends Emergency Patch Amid Criticism
articles.text:
XRP Ledger defends emergency patch for unlimited XRP bug
The XRP Ledger Foundation pushed back against claims that its emergency security patch was forced on network operators.
XRP Ledger developers have defended the emergency security patch used to fix a bug capable of creating XRP beyond the network’s fixed supply, saying they could not wait for the network’s usual two-week validator vote without exposing the flaw to attackers.
The fix, released on Sept. 25, came three days after a bug bounty report, and took effect immediately on any server that installed it. It was the first deliberate bypass of the normal amendment process since the system was introduced more than ten years ago, they said.
“With a normal amendment vote, the fix would have been public for weeks before it took effect, risking network security,” XRPL developers said in an X post on Sunday.
The expedited fix led to questions about XRPL’s level of decentralization. On its website, XRPL claims it is a fully decentralized, public blockchain — a characterization that has been central to arguments that its native token, XRP, is not a security.
XRPL security fix “raised a lot of questions”
Cyber Capital founder Justin Bons said Thursday that marketing XRP to retail investors as decentralized amounted to “straight-up fraud.” He argued that the Sept. 25 emergency release shipped as binaries only, temporarily withheld the source code and pressured operators to upgrade.
However, XRPL Foundation said the decision to skip the normal amendment process was made jointly by the Foundation, RippleX, core developers and validators after assessing the severity of the bug.
“No single party could make that call alone. Every validator and node operator chooses what software to run, and 3.4.1 only became required through a normal amendment vote with more than 80% validator support for two weeks. Protocol changes still go through amendments,” the foundation said.
Related: Ledger confirms unauthorized hardware implant, says losses may exceed $86M
XRP Kuwait, an independent validator operator, also rejected claims that the coordinated upgrades signaled centralized control.
“We disagree with the claim that operators coordinating an update is, in itself, proof of centralized control,” it said. “Coordination is not the same as control. Independent operators can assess a situation, communicate with one another, and reach the same conclusion without giving up their independence.”
Bug could have minted unlimited XRP
The bug was an integer overflow in the XRP Ledger’s payment engine that had been present since 2015, according to the project’s vulnerability disclosure report.
XRP balances are stored as 64-bit integers with a fixed maximum. When a sum exceeded that maximum, the calculation wrapped to a smaller number instead of failing.
An attacker could exploit this by creating hundreds of specially priced offers, each asking for a very large amount of XRP, then sending one payment that consumed them all.
The engine would credit each offer owner their full amount but charge the buyer only the tiny wrapped total. The difference would be newly created, spendable XRP.
The attack required deliberately constructed offers and could not be triggered by normal trading activity, according to the report. Developers said they found no evidence that the issue was exploited on any public network.
Magazine: Ledger attack spreads to EU, AI finds ’18 trillion XRP’ bug: Hodler’s Digest

articles.title: Bitcoin Ranges Near $83K as Traders Look to US Inflation Data - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin is trading near $83,330, up 0.6% on the day but down around 3% on the week.
- Analysts say rising Treasury yields and a stronger dollar are weighing on Bitcoin, even as bets on an October Fed rate hike fade.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $21.13 million on Friday after two days of heavy outflows.
Bitcoin inched higher on Monday, trading at $83,327, up 0.6% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko data. The asset is still down 2.9% over the past week.
The cryptocurrency has "struggled against an increasingly challenging macroeconomic backdrop," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, told Decrypt.
"Rising energy prices have reignited inflation concerns, pushing US Treasury yields higher and strengthening the dollar as investors reassess the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory," she said. "Despite its reputation as a potential alternative store of value, recent price action suggests investors continue to treat Bitcoin predominantly as a risk asset rather than a reliable geopolitical hedge."
Traders see a 19.4% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's October 28 meeting, down from 22.1% a week ago and 42.5% a month ago, according to CME FedWatch. Prediction markets Polymarket and Myriad both put the odds of a hike at 17% (Disclaimer: Myriad is a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company Dastan).
A shift in rate expectations should in principle support Bitcoin, Bitfire's Jade Shi said, but elevated long-term Treasury yields mean broader financial conditions have not fully eased. That helps explain why Bitcoin has held up without decisively clearing resistance, she said.
Yields and ETF flows
The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 5.24% and the 30-year yield at 5.60%, according to CNBC, having hit 52-week highs of 5.37% and 5.73% last week. Yields reached their highest levels in more than two decades, CoinShares head of research James Butterfill wrote on Thursday.
Butterfill argued that if those yields increasingly reflect concerns about U.S. public finances rather than stronger growth, Bitcoin begins to look "less like a conventional risk asset and more like an alternative to government-issued money."
Digital asset fund flows have lost momentum after $11.1 billion of inflows since mid-July, according to CoinShares.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs drew $21.13 million in net inflows on Friday, after outflows of $487.07 million on Wednesday and $244.13 million on Thursday, according to SoSoValue.
Technically, Bitcoin has been trading mainly between about $80,300 and $87,100, according to Bitfire. A break above $85,600 on stronger volume could open the way toward $87,395, while a drop below $82,000 would raise the risk of a move toward $79,000.
"The recent easing of Middle East tensions has provided some breathing room, but the sustainability of the rebound will depend on whether the improvement in sentiment translates into a more meaningful retreat in bond yields and the dollar," Hathorn said. "Attention now turns towards upcoming US inflation data, which could prove decisive in shaping expectations for the Fed's next move."

articles.title: UK Freezes $12M London Penthouse of Alleged Prince Group Finance Chief - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- UK authorities have frozen the £8.9 million London penthouse of Thet Li, the alleged finance chief of Prince Group, The Times reported.
- Authorities will ask a court on Monday to continue the seizure of Li's watches and jewelry, valued at £10.6 million, and £92,570 in cash.
- The U.S. has sought forfeiture of about $14 billion in Bitcoin tied to Prince Group, which denies any wrongdoing.
UK authorities have frozen a London penthouse overlooking Buckingham Palace that belongs to Thet Li, the alleged finance chief of Prince Group, The Times reported Sunday.
Li, 39, paid £8.9 million in 2022 for the 13th-floor apartment near St James's Park, according to the report. Authorities placed a freezing order on its Land Registry record following a Foreign Office investigation.
The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Li in October 2025 among 146 Prince Group targets, describing him as a "de facto illicit finance CFO" involved in "bulk cash smuggling and managing dirty money."
The UK sanctioned him in March under its global human rights regime, citing his links to Chen Zhi and Prince Group, whose Cambodian scam centers it says subject workers to forced labor and cruel treatment.
UK authorities also accuse Li of being a "key lieutenant" to the group's leader who "managed the Prince Group's international financial network," according to The Times.
UK authorities describe Prince Group as a front for "industrial scale" online fraud, including the romance and investment scams known as pig butchering, per The Times, which cited United Nations estimates that more than 100,000 trafficked workers are forced to work in its operations.
Prince Group-linked London assets
Freezing orders also cover a £12 million mansion in St John's Wood and a £100 million office building in the City of London tied to Prince Group chairman Chen Zhi, the newspaper reported. Chen was arrested in Cambodia and extradited to China.
Assets linked to Chen's alleged second in command, Wu An Ming, including a £30 million Holland Park mansion and a £53 million Belgravia townhouse registered to a woman alleged to be his wife, have also been frozen. Wu was reportedly arrested in Japan in June.
Police raided two Isle of Man homes apparently owned by Li last October in a joint operation with the FBI. Prince Group obtained gaming licenses on the island that were allegedly used to launder the proceeds of its crimes, according to the report.
The U.S. has sought forfeiture of about $14 billion in Bitcoin tied to the group, and a Washington-based Scam Center Strike Force has reported $580 million in crypto seizures and freezes.
The UK has also sanctioned crypto marketplace Xinbi as part of a crackdown on Southeast Asian scam centers, and Interpol has called the scam compound network a global threat.
Prince Group said last year that it "categorically rejects the notion that it or its chairman, Chen Zhi, has engaged in any unlawful activity."
Authorities will apply to a court on Monday to continue the seizure of Li's watches and jewelry, valued at £10.6 million, along with £92,570 in cash.

articles.title: EU targets MiCA loophole that lets crypto exchanges serve 27 countries with one license
articles.text:
Quick Take
- EU finance ministers have agreed to place major crypto companies under direct ESMA supervision in a proposed overhaul of MiCA.
- The change aims to address regulatory gaps that allow crypto firms licensed in one country to serve customers across all 27 EU states.
- Only 10 to 15 of roughly 360 providers may face centralized oversight, leaving most firms under national regulators.
EU finance ministers agreed to shift oversight of major crypto companies to a central watchdog, reshaping supervision under MiCA.
The Council of the European Union reached a political agreement on Oct. 9 to give the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) direct responsibility for the bloc's most significant crypto-asset service providers, as part of a wider package to integrate European financial markets.
The proposed overhaul addresses a weakness in the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), which allows firms licensed in one member state to serve customers across the 27-country bloc while remaining primarily supervised by their home-country regulator.
The compromise, however, is considerably narrower than the European Commission's original plan to move all crypto service providers under ESMA. Officials estimate that only 10 to 15 of roughly 360 providers would qualify for centralized supervision, Reuters reported.
The agreement sets the Council's negotiating position rather than changing the law immediately. The Council must still negotiate the proposal with the European Parliament.
National licenses expose gap in EU-wide oversight
MiCA's passporting system was designed to provide crypto firms with a single route into the European market. Under the regulation, a provider authorized in one member state can offer approved services elsewhere in the EU without establishing a physical presence in every country it serves.
That arrangement reduces duplication for firms expanding across borders, but it also places considerable responsibility on the national authority issuing the initial approval. This is because a company's operations, client assets, and technology systems can grow well beyond the market where it was licensed.
The consequences emerged in a July 2025 ESMA review of the Malta Financial Services Authority's authorization of an unnamed crypto provider.
ESMA questioned why the company received approval while material issues remained unresolved. Its reviewers found insufficient evidence that the licensing assessment adequately addressed governance, potential conflicts of interest, technology infrastructure, custody arrangements and certain anti-money-laundering risks.
The review did not establish that every Maltese license was deficient. It also credited the Maltese regulator with sector expertise and sufficient supervisory resources, while recommending improvements to its authorization process.
Malta subsequently said it was implementing the recommendations but opposed transferring supervision to ESMA, arguing in September 2025 that MiCA was too new to justify an additional regulatory layer. The authority warned that centralization could introduce bureaucracy and hamper competitiveness.
The dispute highlighted a broader tension: one regulator's authorization decision can affect crypto customers across Europe, even when other national watchdogs view the required level of scrutiny differently.
Largest crypto providers face new thresholds and EU enforcement
In response, EU regulators are proposing a new framework to address these issues.
Under the Council's draft, ESMA would take direct oversight of crypto providers with at least 15 million active EU users, or those meeting three of five additional significance criteria covering their customer base, custody assets, transaction volumes and financial interconnectedness.
Those criteria include more than 1 million active users, over €1 billion in crypto assets under custody and more than €4 billion in annual client transactions.
Together, these factors mean a provider's overall scale and connections to the financial system, rather than its place of incorporation alone, would determine whether supervision moves to ESMA.
The agency would gain powers to request information from directly supervised firms, conduct inspections, investigate breaches, and impose financial penalties. The draft also envisages the authority to restrict services or withdraw authorization where firms do not meet regulatory requirements.
While most crypto service providers would remain under national regulators, ESMA would use guidelines, peer reviews, coordinated investigations, and certain intervention powers to address uneven enforcement across jurisdictions.
The overhaul would also create a full-time ESMA executive board, including a chair and five independent members, to handle operational and company-specific decisions. National regulators would continue participating in broader policy and supervisory coordination.
The Council envisages a two-year transition in which joint teams transfer information, operational responsibilities and expertise to ESMA. Existing MiCA licenses for companies brought under direct supervision would remain valid, avoiding the automatic need to seek new authorization.
The proposed structure would bring greater supervisory scrutiny to a small group of large firms while leaving the majority of the market within the current national model. The decisive questions now concern the final thresholds, ESMA's available resources, and how providers near the boundary are treated.
The Council must formally adopt its negotiating position before talks can begin once the European Parliament establishes its own. Those negotiations will determine how many crypto companies ultimately move from national to EU-level supervision and when the transfer can begin.

articles.title: Thailand wants a piece of the $120 billion Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF market, but on its own terms
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Thailand has finalized rules allowing domestic Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs to trade on its stock exchange from a new regulatory framework.
- Restrictions on retail access to foreign crypto ETFs could direct more investor capital toward domestic fund managers.
- The rules take effect Oct. 16, but no ETF has been approved or given a trading date.
Thailand has finalized rules allowing domestic Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs while restricting retail access to competing overseas investment products.
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced on Oct. 8 that 11 regulatory notifications will take effect on Oct. 16, establishing a framework for cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds listed exclusively on the Stock Exchange of Thailand.
Thailand's move follows the success of spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs in the United States, which have attracted about $70.37 billion in combined cumulative net inflows since their launches.
According to SoSoValue data, the funds held about $121 billion in combined net assets as of Oct. 12, illustrating the scale of the market Thailand seeks to enter.
Thailand prioritizes domestic ETFs over foreign competitors
Under the new framework, Thailand will initially prohibit the issuance and offering of investment products linked to foreign crypto ETFs, including depositary receipts that would otherwise allow local investors to gain exposure to overseas funds through domestic securities markets.
Securities companies will also be restricted from facilitating investments in foreign crypto ETFs for clients who do not qualify as institutional or ultra-high-net-worth investors.
The restrictions are targeted rather than a comprehensive prohibition on overseas crypto investments. They primarily affect specified investment products and brokerage services available to ordinary investors.
The SEC said the measures aim to support the development of Thailand's domestic crypto ETF ecosystem and strengthen local financial institutions' capabilities.
The regulator has also expanded the investment options available to existing asset managers.
Previously, Thai mutual funds and private funds could invest in foreign crypto ETFs but not domestic equivalents. Under the revised rules, they may invest in Thai-listed crypto ETFs, subject to existing investment limits.
Together, these changes could establish an additional source of demand for domestic products while reducing the availability of some foreign alternatives.
The framework may also create opportunities for Thai asset managers, custodians and other licensed digital asset businesses to participate in the emerging market.
However, the restrictions could leave retail investors with fewer competing products, making the fees, liquidity and tracking performance of domestically listed funds particularly important once trading begins.
Thailand imposes margin restrictions and investor safeguards
Beyond restrictions on foreign products, Thailand's framework sets operating requirements to limit risk and ensure crypto ETFs function within the country's existing securities market.
Initially, only Bitcoin and Ethereum will qualify as underlying assets, with each ETF required to passively track a single cryptocurrency.
Funds must maintain average net exposure of at least 80% of their net asset value to the chosen asset over each accounting year.
Asset managers must demonstrate adequate personnel, operational systems and service-provider arrangements before establishing a fund. Digital assets held by the ETFs must also be safeguarded by custodians regulated by Thailand's SEC.
Investor protections extend to trading activities.
Securities companies will be prohibited from providing margin loans for crypto ETF purchases, preventing investors from using that form of broker financing to increase their exposure.
Before trading, investors must receive education about the products' characteristics and risks and formally acknowledge their understanding.
Brokers must also emphasize portfolio diversification and investment decisions consistent with individual risk tolerance.
The regulator has separately permitted licensed digital asset fund managers to undertake outsourced investment management functions, while qualified digital asset businesses may apply to serve as mutual fund supervisors.
The final regulations follow consultations conducted between April and September, during which the SEC said most respondents supported the proposals.
The next milestone is Oct. 16, when the regulatory framework becomes effective. The SEC has not yet approved a Bitcoin or Ethereum ETF or announced when either product will begin trading on Thailand's stock exchange.

articles.title: Quản lý gia sản: Cuộc đua mới của ngân hàng
articles.text:
Đón bắt nhu cầu ngày càng tăng
Cùng với sự lớn mạnh của doanh nghiệp, tài sản của các gia đình doanh nhân cũng ngày càng đa dạng, từ cổ phần doanh nghiệp, bất động sản đến tiền gửi, chứng khoán, trái phiếu, bảo hiểm và các khoản đầu tư khác. Khi doanh nghiệp bước sang một giai đoạn phát triển mới, câu hỏi đặt ra với người sáng lập cũng thay đổi.
Không còn đơn thuần là làm thế nào để doanh nghiệp tăng trưởng, mở rộng thị trường hay tối ưu lợi nhuận, nhiều doanh nhân bắt đầu phải tính đến những vấn đề dài hạn hơn: Ai sẽ kế nghiệp? Tài sản được chuyển giao cho thế hệ sau như thế nào? Làm sao để thành quả tích lũy trong hàng chục năm không bị phân mảnh hoặc suy giảm khi chuyển giao giữa các thế hệ? Làm sao để những khối tài sản lớn ngày càng sinh lợi hiệu quả nhất?
Trao đổi với PV Tiền Phong, bà Nguyễn Thị Thu Hương, Cố vấn cấp cao của FIDT, cho rằng đây là một trong những động lực quan trọng thúc đẩy nhu cầu quản lý gia sản tại Việt Nam. Theo bà Hương, sự trưởng thành của thế hệ doanh nhân đầu tiên sau đổi mới đang khiến nhiều gia đình bước vào giai đoạn phải giải những bài toán về kế nghiệp doanh nghiệp, hoạch định thừa kế và quản trị gia đình.
Dẫn số liệu của BCG (hãng tư vấn chiến lược hàng đầu thế giới), bà Hương cho biết tại châu Á, gần một nửa số doanh nghiệp lớn vẫn do thế hệ sáng lập điều hành, trong khi độ tuổi trung bình của nhóm lãnh đạo này đã trên 70. Câu chuyện kế nghiệp doanh nghiệp và chuyển giao tài sản giữa các thế hệ đang ngày càng trở nên đáng chú ý.
Đây không chỉ là câu chuyện của một vài gia đình sở hữu khối tài sản lớn. Khi tài sản ngày càng đa dạng, bài toán quản trị cũng trở nên phức tạp hơn.
Một gia đình có thể đồng thời sở hữu doanh nghiệp, bất động sản, cổ phiếu, trái phiếu, bảo hiểm, tiền gửi, các khoản đầu tư tư nhân, du thuyền thậm chí tài sản ở nước ngoài. Nếu tài sản chỉ tập trung vào một căn nhà hay một khoản tiền gửi, nhu cầu quản trị tổng thể chưa thực sự rõ ràng. Nhưng khi tài sản trải trên nhiều lớp, nhiều pháp nhân và nhiều quốc gia, việc quản lý từng khoản riêng lẻ không còn đủ. Đó cũng là lúc khái niệm quản lý gia sản - wealth management - trở nên quan trọng.
Theo tư liệu McKinsey được dẫn lại, tài sản tài chính cá nhân của người Việt, gồm tiền mặt, tiền gửi, trái phiếu và chứng khoán, đạt khoảng 360 tỷ USD vào cuối năm 2022 và có thể tăng lên khoảng 600 tỷ USD vào năm 2027. Riêng quy mô tài sản được quản lý chuyên nghiệp có thể tăng thêm khoảng 65-75 tỷ USD trong giai đoạn này.
Ở nhóm giàu có nhất, Knight Frank ước tính Việt Nam hiện có khoảng 1.233 cá nhân sở hữu tài sản ròng từ 30 triệu USD trở lên và con số này có thể tăng lên khoảng 1.960 người vào năm 2031. Những con số trên cho thấy câu chuyện không chỉ nằm ở việc người Việt có nhiều tài sản hơn, mà còn ở nhu cầu đưa tài sản vào một hệ thống quản trị chuyên nghiệp hơn.
Tại một sự kiện mới đây, TS Jens Lottner, Tổng Giám đốc Techcombank cho rằng, khi GDP bình quân đầu người đạt khoảng 5.000-6.000 USD, người dân bắt đầu có nguồn tiền nhàn rỗi để tiết kiệm và đầu tư thay vì dành toàn bộ thu nhập cho các nhu cầu sinh hoạt. Khi đó, nhu cầu đối với các sản phẩm đầu tư, bảo hiểm và quản lý tài sản bắt đầu xuất hiện và có thể phát triển nhanh.
Đây cũng là sự chuyển dịch đáng chú ý trong tư duy tài chính của người dân: từ câu hỏi “đầu tư vào đâu để sinh lời?” sang câu hỏi rộng hơn “làm thế nào để quản trị toàn bộ tài sản của gia đình?”.
Quản lý tài sản đầu tư chủ yếu trả lời câu hỏi một khoản tiền nên được đầu tư như thế nào để đạt mục tiêu lợi nhuận và rủi ro. Trong khi đó, quản lý gia sản đặt ra bài toán rộng hơn: toàn bộ tài sản của một gia đình được cấu trúc, quản lý, bảo toàn, tăng trưởng và chuyển giao cho thế hệ tiếp theo như thế nào.
Sự khác biệt này đặc biệt có ý nghĩa với cộng đồng doanh nhân - những người không chỉ sở hữu tài sản tài chính mà còn gắn tài sản cá nhân với doanh nghiệp, thương hiệu, cổ phần và kế hoạch kế nghiệp.
Khi ngân hàng bước vào cuộc đua
Khi nhu cầu của khách hàng thay đổi, thị trường tài chính cũng bắt đầu thay đổi theo. Thời gian gần đây, nhiều ngân hàng lớn tuyển dụng, đào tạo đội ngũ chuyên gia quản lý gia sản, đồng thời xây dựng các dịch vụ dành riêng cho nhóm khách hàng giàu có và siêu giàu.
VPBank phát triển dịch vụ Private Banking với định hướng không chỉ cung cấp sản phẩm tài chính mà còn xây dựng hệ giải pháp quản trị và gia tăng gia sản. Các dịch vụ được giới thiệu gồm tư vấn chiến lược tài chính cá nhân dài hạn, quản lý danh mục đầu tư, phân bổ tài sản, hỗ trợ pháp lý, thuế, thừa kế, du học và các giải pháp tài chính phục vụ đầu tư.
Ngân hàng này cũng hợp tác với các công ty quản lý quỹ như VinaCapital, Dragon Capital, SSIAM, UOBAM và các đơn vị tư vấn thuộc nhóm Big4 nhằm mở rộng khả năng cung cấp giải pháp đầu tư, pháp lý và thuế cho khách hàng.
Không riêng VPBank, NCB đã tuyển dụng chuyên viên quản lý gia sản từ cuối năm 2025. Techcombank xây dựng và đào tạo đội ngũ cán bộ quản lý gia sản thông qua các chương trình chuyên biệt theo chuẩn quốc tế. Tại Đại hội đồng cổ đông thường niên năm 2026, LPBank cũng lần đầu hé lộ định hướng phát triển dịch vụ quản lý gia sản cho khách hàng cao cấp...
Những động thái này cho thấy ngân hàng đang muốn dịch chuyển từ vai trò cung cấp từng sản phẩm tài chính riêng lẻ sang trở thành nơi đồng hành dài hạn với khách hàng trong quá trình quản trị tài sản. Lợi thế của ngân hàng nằm ở chính mối quan hệ sẵn có với khách hàng. Ngân hàng có khả năng quan sát dòng tiền, tiền gửi, tín dụng và giao dịch của khách hàng. Đặc biệt với chủ doanh nghiệp, tổ chức tín dụng có thể đồng thời phục vụ hoạt động tài chính của doanh nghiệp và nhu cầu tài chính cá nhân của người chủ.
Bên cạnh đó, mạng lưới khách hàng rộng cùng hệ sinh thái gồm chứng khoán, quản lý quỹ, bảo hiểm và các đối tác quốc tế giúp ngân hàng có thêm công cụ để xây dựng những giải pháp tổng thể.
Nhưng phía sau cuộc đua về sản phẩm là một câu hỏi khó hơn: ai thực sự đủ năng lực để quản lý cả một gia sản, thay vì chỉ bán thêm một sản phẩm tài chính?
Bởi quản lý gia sản không đơn giản là gom nhiều sản phẩm tài chính vào một gói dịch vụ cao cấp. Thách thức lớn hơn nằm ở chất lượng tư vấn và lợi ích dài hạn của khách hàng. Nếu chuyên viên tư vấn vẫn được đánh giá chủ yếu dựa trên doanh số tiền gửi, bảo hiểm, trái phiếu hay lượng tài sản khách hàng đầu tư vào sản phẩm nội bộ, nguy cơ xung đột giữa mục tiêu kinh doanh của tổ chức và lợi ích dài hạn của khách hàng vẫn tồn tại.
Knight Frank ước tính Việt Nam hiện có khoảng 1.233 cá nhân sở hữu tài sản ròng từ 30 triệu USD trở lên và con số này có thể tăng lên khoảng 1.960 người vào năm 2031.
Bà Nguyễn Thị Thu Hương, Cố vấn cấp cao FIDT nhận định: “Tôi cho rằng chắc chắn đây sẽ là một trong những sân chơi cạnh tranh quan trọng của ngành tài chính Việt Nam trong những năm tới. Thực tế quá trình này đã bắt đầu. Để thực sự chuyển từ cung cấp sản phẩm tài chính cho người giàu sang quản lý gia sản, các tổ chức cần thay đổi đồng bộ từ hệ sinh thái sản phẩm, cơ chế đánh giá và đãi ngộ nhân sự, năng lực đội ngũ cố vấn đến quy trình quản lý xung đột lợi ích. Đây cũng chính là điểm quyết định chất lượng của một thị trường quản lý gia sản chuyên nghiệp”.
Bà Hương cho hay, so với những trung tâm tài chính như Singapore hay Hong Kong (Trung Quốc), Việt Nam vẫn đang ở giai đoạn đầu. Tại các thị trường phát triển, hệ sinh thái quản lý gia sản đã bao gồm ngân hàng tư nhân, quản lý đầu tư, văn phòng quản lý tài sản gia đình, quỹ tín thác, hoạch định thừa kế, tư vấn thuế và khả năng tiếp cận sản phẩm đầu tư toàn cầu. Khoảng cách này đồng thời cũng là dư địa phát triển cho thị trường Việt Nam.

articles.title: Cách làm từ thiện của ông chủ nhỏ
articles.text:
Từ những cuộc chơi vô nghĩa
Tôi gặp anh Nguyễn Văn Xuân tại xưởng nội thất ô tô nhỏ, ven đường ở phường Hòa Bình, tỉnh Phú Thọ. Giữa tiếng máy bắn đinh phành phạch, tiếng máy khâu ro ro xen lẫn tiếng mưa tháng tám lộp bộp trên mái tôn, anh vẫn cặm cụi với từng đường kim, mũi chỉ. Người đàn ông có dáng vẻ phong trần này từng là một “dân chơi” có tiếng. Anh từng rong ruổi từ Phú Thọ, Hải Phòng, Hà Nội đến Lào Cai... chỉ để thỏa mãn thú câu cá.
Vừa khâu những đường chỉ hình quả trám trên bộ ghế da ô tô, anh vừa kể: “Tôi từng là cần thủ có tiếng ở đất miền Bắc. Cứ có lời mời là lại lên đường và đốt không biết bao nhiêu tiền”.
