articles.title: Citroën has brought back the iconic 2 CV as an electric concept car - Engadget
articles.text:
Citroën has brought back the iconic 2 CV as an electric concept car
The French automaker is targeting a 15,000-euro price tag for an eventual production version.
After teasing the return of the 2 CV as an all-electric car in March, Citroën finally showed off the revival of its iconic compact city cruiser during the Paris Motor Show. The 2 CV Concept is only a concept for now, but it's one that draws from the original, which was notably James Bond's choice of car in For Your Eyes Only. However, Citroën announced that the concept will inspire a production model that will go to market within the next two years with a target starting price of 15,000 euros, or around $16,800.
Following in the footsteps of the original that was revealed during the Paris Motor Show in 1948, the 2 CV Concept shares a similar design language that's been updated with some modern tweaks. Citroën wanted to emphasize the "affordability, lightness, practicality, versatility" of the original, as well as include quirky additions like a brake pedal with a tortoise symbol and an accelerator with a rabbit.
The 2 CV Concept's interiors were made to maximize passenger space with recessed door panels, wide seats and a removable front seat. Citroën amped up the modularity of the EV with a removable storage basket instead of a center console, and opted for a detachable radio. Instead of a traditional dashboard, the 2 CV Concept has a singular stem that supports a steering wheel, control lever, paddle-shift gear selector and an eight-inch touchscreen.
As with most conceptual cars, most of these fun ideas likely won't make it to a production model that's subject to strict auto regulations. However, Citroën said it's looking to create a "more accessible, lighter and more essential electric car," with the eventual market version of the 2 CV Concept. For anyone in the US, it's worth a reminder that the French automaker doesn't sell its cars stateside.

articles.title: Smart just unveiled a new ultra-compact EV at the Paris Motor Show - Engadget
articles.text:
Smart just unveiled a new ultra-compact EV at the Paris Motor Show
The Smart #2 is absolutely teensy and gets around 180 miles per charge.
Smart just unveiled its #2 ultra-compact EV at the Paris Motor Show, four years after the company introduced the Smart #1. The Smart #2 looks to be a return to (miniature) form for the company, after a string of SUV releases. This thing is teensy and similar to the iconic Smart Fortwo ultra-compact.
The Smart #2 fits two people and has been designed to make "navigating tight city streets and parking in narrow spaces effortless." They will be available in a variety of two-tone color options, which recall the original Fortwo.
There's a rear-mounted 60kW electric motor that provides 130Nm of torque to the back wheels. These rear tires are actually larger than the front wheels, which should enhance stability.
The floor-mounted battery can get up to 180 miles (290km) per charge, which is a decent enough metric for an ultra-compact. The car also supports fast-charging, which can go from 10 to 80 percent in 20 minutes at the outlet. Smart promises "sportier handling and greater comfort," due to a five-link rear suspension system.
The Smart #2 may look like an old-school Fortwo, but it's packed with modern features. It comes equipped with driver assistance systems, a 10.1-inch central screen and an 8.8-inch driver display. These EVs can connect wirelessly to devices via 4G, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
There will be several trims available to choose from here. The Pure is the entry-level model, and includes everything I mentioned above. The Pure+ adds 11kW AC charging and a heated driver seat. The Premium adds even more perks, like a glass roof, heated leather seats and a seven-speaker Sennheiser sound system. There are also more color options here. Finally, the Couture Edition includes a white exterior, a gold-painted roof and tires with gold detailing. This one will be limited to 999 units.
We don't have exact pricing or availability just yet, but Smart says the starting price will be under $26,500 (£20,000.) Preorders will open in the Spring and deliveries should happen at some point during the summer.
However, this car likely won't be coming across the pond. Smart hasn't sold anything in America since 2019 and this country seems to dislike small and budget-friendly EVs.

articles.title: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background | TechCrunch
articles.text:
One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you’ll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to listen, watch, or record users’ activity all the time and gather all possible context.
There’s obviously privacy and data security concerns with anything that’s collecting data about you continuously. But startups are building such apps undeterred anyway, arming themselves with the belief that the market for personalized assistance is big enough to swallow such concerns.
Former Plaud exec Peter Mo is building Ambi to do something similar. The app aims to provide real-time intelligence and insights to people by listening to them all the time.
The company said on Monday that it has raised $26 million across multiple funding rounds led by Luminous Ventures, which has backed companies like Meituan and Unitree Robotics, and original design manufacturer (ODM) Huaqin.
Ambi is also releasing apps for iPhones, Macs, and Apple Watch. These apps act like meeting notetakers, but users can choose to have them listening so they can capture context all day.
Meeting notetaking companies have been working to automate tasks that follow once calls are done, based on the summaries and action items they gather during the conversation, and using multitudes of connectors to software systems. Ambi wants to take this a step further by having its agent start the work during the meeting itself.
The company’s promise is that its AI agent can proactively give you suggestions or surface relevant knowledge while you are in a meeting, based on your calendar, meetings, knowledge base, and web data. Users can also start a task on one device and continue it on another.
“The way we interact with intelligence is limited. Often the intelligence is trapped on the screen, and if you use hardware like Plaud, you need to wait for recording to transfer to the phone, upload to the cloud, and get intelligence after processing. That’s why we are building Ambi to use AI anytime and anywhere,” Mo, the company’s co-founder and CEO, told TechCrunch.
The company has ambitions to capture more information. Its upcoming desktop app will be able to look at the work that users do and store important parts in its memory to give more personalized suggestions. Apps like Littlebird or Minimi already do something similar.
The startup is also planning to launch its own hardware device, which will have a screen, a speaker, a camera, and microphones to capture context and display information.
Question of privacy
Ambi’s launch comes amidst growing concerns around AI devices that don’t have enough indicators to suggest they are capturing data on people around the user. It is not clear if Ambi’s apps or its upcoming device will have enough indicators to alert third parties that their conversations are being recorded if the user doesn’t disclose their use of Ambi’s tech.
Some meeting notetakers have even been sued because their tech recorded people’s conversations and data without their consent. Plus, the recent release of Apple’s Audio Intelligence feature, which transcribes speech continuously, has raised privacy concerns.
Mo said that users can turn off ambient data capture on Ambi’s apps and devices at any time, and the feature is off by default. The startup said it doesn’t store any recordings of users and encrypts the data, but it didn’t specify what kind of encryption it uses. Despite these measures, the onus of declaring ambient capture is still on the users. He classified this as an industry-wide problem.
“We have to inform our users that they have to tell others about ambient capture. We, as an industry, haven’t solved this problem [of disclosure]. We have tried to put the information about disclosure in every place possible, but if users try to hide the capture, we can’t just solve the problem,” he said.
Ambi currently has over 50 staff across offices in San Francisco, Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen. The company is hiring for its go-to-market function and AI engineers for working on speech-recognition models.

articles.title: Phát minh của Trung Quốc làm rung chuyển ngành vật liệu: Trộn tre với nhựa, tạo ra loại composite bền hơn 81% và dai hơn 173%, chống được sóng điện từ
articles.text:
Các nhà khoa học Trung Quốc phát triển một loại nhựa composite gia cường bằng vật liệu từ tre, có độ bền kéo tăng 81% và độ dai tăng 173%.
Vật liệu mới được nhóm nghiên cứu tại Đại học Nông nghiệp An Huy, thành phố Hợp Phì, Trung Quốc, phát triển. Công trình được công bố trên tạp chí Sustainable Carbon Materials.
Điểm đáng chú ý là thay vì chủ yếu phản xạ sóng điện từ như nhiều vật liệu che chắn truyền thống, composite mới hấp thụ phần lớn năng lượng đi vào, qua đó hạn chế hiện tượng nhiễu thứ cấp.
Nhóm nghiên cứu cho rằng vật liệu có thể được ứng dụng trong điện thoại thông minh, máy tính xách tay và nhiều thiết bị điện tử cần lớp bảo vệ chống nhiễu điện từ.
Nhiễu điện từ, hay EMI, là những tín hiệu không mong muốn có thể ảnh hưởng đến hoạt động của mạch điện và thiết bị điện tử. Khi mật độ thiết bị không dây ngày càng tăng, việc kiểm soát nhiễu trở thành một vấn đề quan trọng trong thiết kế phần cứng.
Các vật liệu dẫn điện thông thường có thể chắn sóng điện từ, nhưng phần lớn hoạt động bằng cách phản xạ chúng. Điều này đôi khi tạo ra nhiễu mới ở khu vực xung quanh.
Để giải quyết vấn đề, nhóm khoa học sử dụng than sinh học từ tre - vật liệu giàu carbon được tạo ra bằng cách nung tre trong môi trường có rất ít hoặc không có oxy, quá trình gọi là nhiệt phân.
Than sinh học được xem là nguồn nguyên liệu tái tạo có tiềm năng thay thế một số chất độn dẫn điện truyền thống. Tuy nhiên, hai hạn chế lớn là độ dẫn điện còn thấp và khả năng liên kết với nhựa kém.
Nhóm nghiên cứu trước tiên nung bột tre trong môi trường nitơ để tạo than sinh học. Sau đó, vật liệu được xử lý bằng phương pháp gia nhiệt Joule chớp nhoáng, sử dụng một xung điện năng ngắn để thay đổi cấu trúc carbon.
Các hạt tiếp tục được xử lý bằng APTES, một hợp chất giúp tăng khả năng liên kết với nhựa.
Than sinh học sau biến tính được đặt giữa các lớp của hai loại nhựa có khả năng phân hủy sinh học là PLA và PBAT. Cấu trúc nhiều lớp tạo thành các đường dẫn khiến sóng điện từ phải truyền qua quãng đường dài hơn, từ đó liên tục bị hấp thụ và suy giảm.
Trong thử nghiệm, các nhà nghiên cứu so sánh nhiều phiên bản vật liệu, gồm composite sử dụng than sinh học chưa xử lý, than đã qua gia nhiệt chớp nhoáng, than biến tính hóa học và cấu trúc không phân lớp.
Phiên bản tối ưu đạt độ bền kéo 25,5 MPa, cao hơn 81% so với vật liệu đối chứng. Độ dai tăng 173%, lên 2,68 megajoule trên mỗi mét khối. Khả năng kéo giãn trước khi đứt cũng tăng hơn gấp đôi, từ 11,5% lên 24,7%.
Khả năng dẫn điện được cải thiện rõ rệt. Composite tối ưu đạt độ dẫn 12,8 siemens/cm, trong khi phiên bản sử dụng than tre chưa xử lý chỉ đạt 1,7 siemens/cm.
Khả năng chống nhiễu điện từ cũng cho thấy khác biệt lớn. Trong dải tần từ 8,2 đến 12,4 GHz, vật liệu mới đạt hiệu quả che chắn trung bình 36,7 dB. Trong khi đó, composite không sử dụng cấu trúc phân lớp nhưng chứa cùng lượng chất độn chỉ đạt 7,5 dB.
Đáng chú ý, phần lớn khả năng che chắn của vật liệu mới đến từ hấp thụ thay vì phản xạ. Khả năng hấp thụ đóng góp khoảng 30,8 dB, trong khi phản xạ chỉ chiếm 5,9 dB.
Các nhà khoa học cho rằng mạng lưới carbon kết hợp với cấu trúc nhiều lớp buộc sóng điện từ phải di chuyển qua quãng đường phức tạp hơn trong vật liệu, qua đó làm tiêu hao năng lượng của chúng.
Theo nhóm nghiên cứu, việc kết hợp đồng thời khả năng chống nhiễu điện từ và độ bền cơ học cao trong một vật liệu có nguồn gốc từ than sinh học có thể mở ra hướng mới cho thiết kế linh kiện điện tử.
Thay vì chỉ đóng vai trò lớp chắn sóng, vật liệu có thể trở thành một phần kết cấu của vỏ thiết bị, vừa chịu lực vừa hạn chế nhiễu. Những sản phẩm như điện thoại, máy tính xách tay và thiết bị điện tử khác là các ứng dụng tiềm năng được nhóm nghiên cứu đề cập.
Theo IE

articles.title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
articles.text:
There's been a disturbance in the force. Only it's more like a farce.
It seems that Elon Musk, while crowing on X about how useful his Grok Bot AI agent was in ordering some Lego Star Wars kits on Sunday, managed to reveal via a screenshot to his more than 240 million followers not only the 10-digit Lego order number of his purchase, but also what he paid for the sets, the delivery and billing addresses, the last four digits of his credit card, and the email address his bot used to buy the bricks from Lego.
Faster than the Millennium Falcon making the jump to light speed, the inevitable happened. An X account holder named Enderman posted screenshots of interactions with Lego's customer service chatbot on its website, where the user seemingly managed—using the email and order number Musk kindly, but recklessly, provided—to get the system to cancel Musk's order.
It’s a Trap!
Within a couple of hours—possibly to see whether Enderman's scheme was actually successful—Musk replied and said his order had not been canceled after all.
But by this point, the folly of posting the purchase details on his account must have been evident. For example, another X user went back to Lego's AI assistant, called “Sophia,” and supposedly used the same details to reopen the delivery, this time increasing the order count to 400 and changing the delivery address, all while using Musk's original payment method. “Perfect! I'll get your Lego adventure back on track,” Sophia replied, according to screenshots posted on X.
Upping the ante to 400 sets could be seen as conservative, as a glance at WIRED's Spend Elon Musk’s Money tracker reveals that if you wanted to blow $1 trillion of Musk's cash on plastic bricks, it might have been possible to buy one billion $1,000 Death Star sets, each with 9,023 pieces.
Lego declined to comment when WIRED contacted the company to confirm if such activity took place on Musk's personal Star Wars order. However, internal safeguards for Lego's AI assistant could have flagged unusual activity on the purchase, and so hopefully fleshy humans were tasked with checking the changes.
Attack of the Clones
On Saturday, Musk suggested that Grok could make purchases online with a simple prompt. In this post, Musk suggested that all brave users needed to do to let Grok buy stuff for them was upload a picture of their credit card so the bot could search the web for deals and then complete the purchase. AI companies like Meta and OpenAI have also highlighted the utility of using their respective agents for shopping tasks.
However, at the end of last year, Visa warned about fraud in agentic commerce, advising that bad actors were building legitimate-looking sites that could fool AI agents into purchasing fake items simply by offering gear at super-low prices.
“Once the AI agent completes the purchase … the malicious merchant can harvest payment data and instantly use it for unauthorized transactions,” according to Visa's blog. Visa added that it observed a 25 percent increase “in malicious bot-initiated transactions” in the latter half of 2025, but in the US, this figure jumped to 40 percent.

articles.title: The Social Reckoning is flopping at the box office
articles.text:
As important as some of the messages in The Social Reckoning are, the movie has been drastically underperforming at the box office. Per Variety, Aaron’s Sorkin’s follow up to The Social Network only grossed a measly $5.5 million this past weekend against a budget that’s somewhere within the $30–42 million range. That would make it a certifiable flop that’s costing Columbia Pictures (and Sony) quite a bit of money — especially when you compare it to The Social Network’s $22 million opening.
The Social Reckoning is flopping at the box office
Meanwhile, Other Mommy is having an unexpected moment.
This isn’t entirely surprising given how middling reviews for the film have been. It’s currently got a 55% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and has widely been trashed on social media. All of this might be reflective of audiences hoping for a proper sequel to The Social Network, which won three Oscars for its screenplay (written by Sorkin), editing, and score. But it might speak to people not fully clicking with Mikey Madison’s performance as whistleblower Frances Haugen or Jeremy Allen White’s turn as Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz. (Madison, for her part, indicated to The Hollywood Reporter that it was Sorkin’s vision as director that kept from “authentically and faithfully represent[ing] a real person,” which she hopes to do in the future.) It also probably didn’t help that Jesse Eisenberg — who portrayed Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network — had no interest in being in the film, according to Sorkin himself.
Ironically, Blumhouse’s Other Mommy raked in an impressive $27.5 million this weekend, which likely suggests that people are more interested in novel horror as opposed to reminders of how social media has made everyone’s lives worse.

articles.title: Giá bạc đồng loạt tăng, bạc thỏi đắt hơn nửa triệu đồng/kg
articles.text:
Ở thị trường trong nước, đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay, giá bạc tại các doanh nghiệp kinh doanh bạc lớn đều được điều chỉnh tăng.
Giá bạc tại Công ty TNHH MTV Vàng bạc Đá quý Ngân hàng Sài Gòn Thương Tín (Sacombank - SBJ) đầu phiên hôm nay được điều chỉnh tăng khá mạnh.
Cụ thể, mở cửa phiên hôm nay, giá bạc miếng tại Sacombank được niêm yết ở mức 2,124-2,190 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), còn giá bạc thỏi của Sacombank được giao dịch ở mức 56,64-58,4 triệu đồng/kg (mua - bán). So với mức kết của phiên giao dịch cuối tuần qua, giá bạc miếng của Sacombank tăng 21.000 đồng/lượng, còn giá bạc thỏi của thương hiệu này tăng 560.000 đồng/kg ở cả 2 chiều giao dịch.
Cùng xu hướng, giá bạc tại Công ty CP Kim loại quý Ancarat cũng được điều chỉnh đi lên.
Công ty CP Kim loại quý Ancarat đầu phiên hôm nay kéo giá bạc miếng lên mức 2,113-2,179 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), tăng 11.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều mua và đắt hơn 12.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều bán so với mức chốt tuần qua.
Giá bạc thỏi của Ancarat cũng tăng 294.000 đồng/kg ở chiều mua và đắt thêm 320.000 đồng/kg ở chiều bán so với kết tuần qua, giao dịch ở mức 56,347-58,107 triệu đồng/kg (mua - bán).
Tương tự, giá bạc tại Tập đoàn Vàng bạc Đá quý Phú Quý đầu giờ sáng nay cũng có xu hướng tăng.
Giá bạc miếng của Phú Quý đầu phiên hôm nay được niêm yết ở mức 2,121-2,187 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), tăng 5.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều mua và đắt hơn 6.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều bán so với mức chốt tuần qua.
Giá bạc thỏi của thương hiệu này mở cửa phiên giao dịch hôm nay được niêm yết ở mức 56,559-58,319 triệu đồng/kg (mua - bán), tăng 133.000 đồng/kg ở chiều mua và đắt hơn 160.000 đồng/kg ở chiều bán so với kết phiên giao dịch cuối tuần qua.
Tại thị trường quốc tế, mở cửa phiên giao dịch đầu tuần, giá bạc được điều chỉnh đi lên.
Vào lúc 9h18' ngày 12/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá bạc giao ngay trên thị trường thế giới được giao dịch ở mức 61,09 USD/ounce, tăng 0,64% so với phiên trước đó.
Giá bạc thế giới phục hồi nhờ đồng USD suy yếu và lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ điều chỉnh giảm, từ đó hỗ trợ sức hấp dẫn của kim loại quý.
Trong thời gian tới, giá bạc nhiều khả năng tiếp tục chịu tác động từ diễn biến lợi suất trái phiếu, sức mạnh của đồng USD, giá dầu và kỳ vọng về chính sách lãi suất của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed).
Lợi suất trái phiếu duy trì đà tăng có thể khiến kim loại quý đối mặt với áp lực giảm sâu hơn. Trái lại, nếu lợi suất trái phiếu hạ nhiệt cùng với đồng USD suy yếu, thị trường bạc có thể tìm được động lực phục hồi.
Khi đồng USD giảm giá, kim loại quý được định giá bằng đồng tiền này có thể trở nên hấp dẫn hơn đối với người mua sử dụng các đồng tiền khác, mặc dù mức độ tác động còn phụ thuộc vào nhu cầu đầu tư và tình hình kinh tế toàn cầu.

articles.title: How to improve your Android phone's location accuracy - Engadget
articles.text:
How to improve your Android phone's location accuracy
There are a few settings to check if you're having issues with your map's location accuracy.
The best Android phones use built-in GPS to determine where you are, which is necessary to guide you with turn-by-turn directions. To accurately know how to get to where you want to go, after all, the phone first needs to know exactly where you are. You might also use this feature to send a pin of your location to someone, or maybe mark the location of your parked car so you can find it in a busy shopping mall. It's also useful for safety reasons in the event that you get lost or hurt. Bottom line: you want location information to be as accurate as possible. While precise location hinges largely on the phone's built-in GPS antennas, there are settings you can adjust to improve it.
The phone can use wireless signals, GPS, and device sensors to determine where you are, and even in what direction you're facing. A setting called Location Accuracy Service, formerly Google Location Services, is your first step to improving accuracy, especially if you're indoors or in a densely populated area where GPS signals aren't available or as clear. If the location is completely wrong, it means there's no working signal at all and the phone might be picking up where you last were and not where you are now. This can be frustrating, but it's easy to fix.
Improving location accuracy
A simple settings tweak can improve your location accuracy. Go to Settings > Location > Location Services > Location Accuracy with most Android 12 and above devices and Settings > Location > Advanced > Location Accuracy with Android 11 and below. Enabling this ensures that the phone uses any available wireless signal to determine your location, including GPS, Wi-Fi, and the cellular network and towers, along with sensors like the accelerometer, barometer, and gyroscope to also further determine your location. If Location Accuracy is off, the phone can only use GPS and the phone's sensors, which limits its capabilities.
Google anonymously collects information about wireless signals and sensors from your device and others, and basically crowdsources estimated location data to improve accuracy. It's similar to how apps like Waze crowdsource traffic information from users, or the best item trackers use Bluetooth on nearby devices to let you know where you left your keys or wallet.
Where you'll find Location Accuracy most useful is when you're in areas where a GPS signal might be blocked, like a dense urban area with a lot of tall buildings. It's also helpful when you're indoors and a GPS signal is not available at all. Keep in mind that you also need to go to Settings > Location and select App location permissions (or wherever this menu item might be on your phone) and ensure location is enabled for the apps you want to be able to use it.
Fixes in Google Maps
One of the most common apps you might rely on for location accuracy is Google Maps, which is now enhanced with Gemini integration. If the app is unable to determine your exact location, indicated with a light blue circle around the blue dot that signifies you (you might even see a "low accuracy" label), you'll want to first make sure that Location services in general are turned on. Go to Settings > Location and turn on Use location. Usually Google Maps prompts you to turn on Location Services to use it in the first place.
Turning on Location Accuracy using the steps noted above comes next. Make sure that you are connected to an active mobile data or Wi-Fi network and the phone isn't in Airplane Mode. If you're on a Wi-Fi network but the signal is weak, try disconnecting and using cellular data to see if that helps.
You can also calibrate your locations using Lens in Maps. Stand by a landmark or specific venue, search for the place on the map and select View. Point your camera at the place and this will let Maps know where you are to help it more precisely help you navigate to where you want to go. Alternatively, you can calibrate using the phone's compass. In Google Maps, make a figure eight with the phone a few times and see if this helps strengthen the location accuracy and remove the circle around your blue dot.
If the phone is still having trouble determining your exact location, your best bet is to move to a different spot. Completely shut down the app, walk to somewhere nearby where a signal might be stronger, and try again.

articles.title: Vì sao iPhone ở Việt Nam phải bóc seal, kích hoạt ngay? iPhone nhanh hết pin vì tính năng ít người để ý
articles.text:
Việc iPhone chính hãng phải bóc seal, kích hoạt ngay tại cửa hàng không chỉ để kiểm tra máy mà còn liên quan đến kiểm soát hàng tồn và phân bổ nguồn cung. Một tính năng cho phép ứng dụng âm thầm cập nhật dữ liệu khi iPhone đang chờ có thể làm tăng mức tiêu thụ pin, nhưng người dùng có thể kiểm soát dễ dàng.
Từ dòng iPhone 14 năm 2022, nhiều chuỗi bán lẻ ủy quyền của Apple tại Việt Nam bắt đầu siết yêu cầu khách hàng bóc seal và kích hoạt thiết bị ngay tại cửa hàng, đặc biệt trong những ngày đầu mở bán. Theo đại diện các nhà bán lẻ, quy trình này nhằm hạn chế tình trạng gom số lượng lớn iPhone để bán lại, đồng thời giúp kiểm soát lượng máy thực sự đến tay người dùng.
iPhone mới thường được yêu cầu bóc seal và kích hoạt ngay tại cửa hàng trong những ngày đầu mở bán. (Ảnh: tinte.vn)
Trong giai đoạn đầu mở bán, nhu cầu iPhone thường vượt nguồn cung, đặc biệt với các phiên bản Pro và Pro Max. Nếu được giữ nguyên seal, một lượng lớn thiết bị có thể bị mua gom, lưu kho rồi bán lại với mức giá cao hơn khi nguồn hàng khan hiếm. Yêu cầu kích hoạt ngay khiến hình thức đầu cơ này khó thực hiện hơn. Người mua cũng có cơ hội kiểm tra ngoại hình, màn hình và tình trạng thiết bị trước khi rời cửa hàng, qua đó hạn chế tranh chấp nếu phát hiện lỗi hoặc dấu hiệu bất thường.
Đằng sau thao tác kích hoạt còn có một chỉ số được các bên trong chuỗi phân phối quan tâm là Velocity, tức tỷ lệ thiết bị đã bán và kích hoạt so với lượng hàng tồn kho. Chỉ số này phản ánh tốc độ tiêu thụ sản phẩm và có thể được sử dụng làm một trong những cơ sở để đánh giá hiệu quả phân phối. Khi máy được bán và kích hoạt nhanh thay vì nằm lâu trong kho, nhà phân phối và các chuỗi bán lẻ có thêm cơ sở để tiếp nhận những lô hàng tiếp theo. Vì vậy, tốc độ bán ra trong những ngày đầu có thể trở thành yếu tố quan trọng trong cuộc cạnh tranh nguồn cung.
Tuy nhiên, iPhone nguyên seal vẫn tồn tại trên thị trường Việt Nam. Người dùng mua trực tiếp từ Apple Store Online hoặc một số kênh thương mại điện tử có thể nhận thiết bị chưa kích hoạt. Trong khi đó, tại nhiều chuỗi bán lẻ ủy quyền, khách hàng thường được yêu cầu thực hiện quy trình mở hộp và active tại chỗ. Sự khác biệt này cho thấy đây chủ yếu là chính sách quản lý bán hàng và phân phối của từng kênh, thay vì một yêu cầu bắt buộc áp dụng cho mọi iPhone bán tại Việt Nam.
Nguồn hàng và tốc độ kích hoạt có thể ảnh hưởng đến việc phân bổ iPhone cho các chuỗi bán lẻ trong những đợt tiếp theo. (Ảnh: SForum)
Yêu cầu kích hoạt càng đáng chú ý khi Việt Nam ngày càng được nâng vị trí trong hệ thống phân phối của Apple. Với iPhone 14, người dùng trong nước phải chờ hơn ba tuần sau các thị trường đầu tiên. Đến iPhone 15, khoảng cách giảm xuống còn khoảng một tuần. Từ iPhone 17 năm 2025, Việt Nam lần đầu nằm trong nhóm thị trường mở bán đợt đầu và tiếp tục duy trì vị trí này với iPhone 18.
Khi Việt Nam trở thành thị trường Tier 1, nhu cầu iPhone tập trung mạnh ngay từ ngày đầu mở bán, kéo theo áp lực lớn hơn về nguồn hàng. Quy mô kinh doanh Apple tại Việt Nam cũng ngày càng tăng, khiến tốc độ tiêu thụ và tỷ lệ kích hoạt trở thành những yếu tố quan trọng trong chuỗi phân phối. Do đó, việc bóc seal và kích hoạt iPhone ngay tại cửa hàng không đơn thuần là bước kiểm tra trước khi giao máy, mà còn gắn với bài toán kiểm soát hàng hóa từ nhà phân phối đến người dùng cuối.

articles.title: Muse Wonder Puts Meta Back at the AI Frontier
articles.text:
When Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg rebooted his company’s artificial intelligence efforts last year, it seemed to be a very expensive gamble. Meta’s latest AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, seem to show that the bet is finally paying off by putting the company back at the frontier of AI development.
Muse Wonder Full boasts frontier capabilities, Meta says, meaning that it is among the most capable AI models in the world. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” the company said in a blog post today.
The Muse Wonder models will be available through an API and through Muse Code, a tool for writing software with AI. Meta says the best version of the model will power features across its platforms, including its Muse personal agent.
Zuckerberg overhauled his company’s AI research last year by sinking billions into the recently formed Meta Superintelligence Labs, and hiring the former Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang to lead it. This effort has sometimes been rocky, with some researchers not sticking around for long.
Meta was once a trailblazer in AI. Its Llama series of models were the first frontier open-weight offerings from a big lab. Llama, which could be downloaded and run on one’s own hardware, was widely adopted by researchers and startups.
But the company fell behind after delivering several disappointing versions of the model, and as Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google rapidly introduced more capable models.
Meta announced the first model from its new lab, Muse Spark, in April of this year. The company has also released a small open-weight model called Muse Glimmer, and says it plans to release larger open-weight models in the future. It did not disclose details of how new Muse Wonder models were built or trained.
Muse Wonder was built to compete with the very best, however. Meta says the largest version of the new model outperforms Anthropic’s second-best model, Claude Fable 5.1, and ranks just below its best, Claude Opus 5.5, on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a widely used aggregated score of model capabilities.
Meta says the model outperforms OpenAI’s best model, GPT-6 Astra, and both Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 on some specialized benchmarks, including ones that measure a model’s ability to work with legal documents and to build software. Benchmarks are not always a reliable measure of real-world performance, but this is still a significant step forward for Meta’s models.
Muse Wonder also includes two novel features designed to help make agents more effective and less inclined to misbehave. The new features, called Active Memory and Active Focus, are designed to keep the model locked into a stated goal and prevent it from becoming confused. This can be a challenge when AI performs complex research or builds a large software project, for example, and can lead to expensive mistakes or compounded errors.
Meta says it has put significant effort into training Muse Wonder to refuse to generate dangerous outputs, such as recipes for building bioweapons or help with hacking. It says the company scores well on several benchmarks designed to measure how resilient models are to those prompts.
A series of recent incidents involving rogue AI agents from Anthropic, OpenAI, and others also shows how easily powerful AI models can stray when given open-ended commands. Meta did not disclose whether it has seen agents powered by Muse Wonder misbehave in testing or what it has done to mitigate this issue specifically.
Zuckerberg said in a post on X last month that the company had delayed the release of its Muse models to work on safety. Meta also revealed a framework designed to ensure that it scales its models’ capabilities safely in a blog post earlier this month.
Muse Wonder may add more fuel to an already furious race to develop more capable AI, however. It certainly suggests that Meta is once again competitive in the increasingly high-stakes AI race.

articles.title: Lãi suất ngân hàng hôm nay 12/10/2026: Kỳ hạn dài có biến động mới
articles.text:
VPBank vừa điều chỉnh lãi suất huy động đối với các kỳ hạn 15-18 tháng. Theo biểu lãi suất được đề cập, mức lãi suất mới cao nhất đạt 7,9%/năm, tăng khoảng 0,7-0,8 điểm phần trăm so với trước đó.
Mức lãi suất này được VPBank áp dụng cho một số sản phẩm tiền gửi, gồm Tiền gửi trực tuyến có kỳ hạn thường, Tiền gửi Hũ mục tiêu, Tiền gửi Thịnh vượng linh hoạt và Tiền gửi có kỳ hạn Phát Lộc Thịnh Vượng.
Điều kiện áp dụng cụ thể cần được đối chiếu theo từng sản phẩm và biểu lãi suất hiện hành của ngân hàng.
Ngân hàng giữ nguyên lãi suất tiền gửi các kỳ hạn còn lại. Theo đó, lãi suất ngân hàng niêm yết cho tiền gửi trực tuyến có kỳ hạn thường, tiền gửi có kỳ hạn Phát Lộc Thịnh Vượng, như sau: Kỳ hạn 1-5 tháng là 4,75%/năm, kỳ hạn 6-11 tháng là 7%/năm, kỳ hạn 12-13 tháng là 7,1%/năm, kỳ hạn 15-18 tháng là 7,8%/năm, kỳ hạn 24 tháng là 7,1%/năm, kỳ hạn 36 tháng là 6%/năm.
Bên cạnh lãi suất niêm yết, một số ngân hàng triển khai chương trình cộng thêm lãi suất hoặc ưu đãi theo điều kiện gửi tiền, đưa mức sinh lời tối đa lên trên 8%/năm ở một số kỳ hạn.
Tại Ngân hàng MB, lãi suất tiết kiệm kỳ hạn 6 tháng lên đến 8,2%/năm khi khách hàng gửi tiết kiệm trực tuyến từ 100 triệu đồng trong ngày cuối tuần.
Trong ngày thường, khách hàng MB gửi tiết kiệm kỳ hạn 6 tháng từ 20 triệu đồng cũng có thể được hưởng mức lãi suất lên đến 8%/năm.
Tại Techcombank, khách hàng đang không có sổ tiết kiệm tại ngân hàng sẽ được cộng thêm lãi suất lên đến 1 điểm phần trăm khi gửi tiền tại một trong các kỳ hạn 3, 6, 12 tháng. Ngoài ra, khách hàng hội viên đủ điều kiện cũng sẽ được cộng thêm lãi suất 0,1-0,15 điểm phần trăm.
Theo đó, lãi suất tiết kiệm kỳ hạn 6 và 12 tháng tại Techcombank cũng chạm ngưỡng 8%/năm nếu khách hàng hội đủ các điều kiện của hội viên.

articles.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
articles.text:
Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it’s now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the industry’s best.
Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
Meta says the models compete with the industry’s best and will soon power its Muse agent.
The new models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, are available for Muse Code subscribers starting today. Wonder can also be accessed through the Meta Model API, Meta said.
Meta says it eventually plans to power its Muse AI agent with Wonder, starting with subscribers, and will develop specialized models it “can bring to everyone using Muse.” It hasn’t shared specifics or provided a timeline for either.
The company says its new models can rival leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1, pointing to results from internal testing on several industry benchmarks. It’s unclear how they stack up against Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, whose capabilities are still coming into focus.
The launches are part of Meta’s aggressive push to reestablish itself as a major force in AI. The company has poured billions into talent and infrastructure and has been steadily expanding its AI lineup, including with image model Muse Image and a heavy focus on bringing useful AI agents to the masses through Muse.

articles.title: AMD puts 32,768 CPU cores in a rack built for AI agents
articles.text:
AMD has published Helion, an open rack blueprint for running AI agents rather than training models, with a CPU-only version holding up to 32,768 cores. Partner systems are due in November, and the pitch is how many agents fit in each watt.
AMD has published a rack blueprint for running AI agents rather than training models. It is called Helion, and partner systems are due in November.
The design appeared at the Open Compute Project summit in San Jose, The Register reported. It comes in a CPU-only version for hyperscale operators and a mixed CPU and GPU version for enterprises.
The CPU-only rack tops out at 32,768 cores. That is 128 sockets of AMD’s 256-core Venice chip on Zen 6, in 400W dense or 600W balanced blades.
The mixed rack is thinner on graphics than it sounds. It holds at most 16 Instinct MI350P accelerators, in two eight-GPU servers that AMD says run independently, with no scale-up fabric.
So this is not a frontier machine. AMD’s Helios rack carries 72 of the newer MI455X parts and 31 terabytes of HBM4, and remains the product for training.
Helion’s most interesting part is barely described. AMD says the enterprise rack carries a token router that sends agents’ model calls either to frontier models in the cloud or to open-source models running in the rack.
That detail appears only in AMD’s own release. Dan McNamara, who runs compute and enterprise AI at AMD, said the point was to let partners make efficient use of available power.
Power is the whole pitch. Matt Kimball at Moor Insights and Strategy said in a field note that the job is packing as many agents as possible into every watt.
He named sovereign AI operators among them, which puts Europe in the frame. Denmark’s grid operator paused new connections in March, with about 60GW of projects queued against peak demand near 7GW.
The constraint is not only Danish. Brussels adopted a Cloud and AI Development Act in June, aiming to at least triple the bloc’s data centre capacity within seven years.
Operators say the same thing. In a survey of 300 data centre decision-makers in the UK, Ireland and the Nordics, power availability came out as the leading obstacle to delivering sovereign capacity.
Helion is less finished than it reads. AMD has published no pricing, plans to contribute the specification to OCP rather than having done so, and named no European system builder among its partners.
Europe is still buying. The bloc has opened bidding for up to seven gigafactories at about €30B, each meant to hold 100,000 chips from suppliers including AMD.

articles.title: How much RAM does a Raspberry Pi actually need? - Engadget
articles.text:
How much RAM does a Raspberry Pi actually need?
It all comes down to how you're going to use it.
The Raspberry Pi has become the de facto option for single-board computers, thanks to its large community and growing library of online resources. The platform is capable of handling everything from light computing tasks to continuous server-esque deployments. My own home automation system ran off a Pi 3 stashed away in the closet for years. And even after I upgraded to a more powerful computer, I still use it for the occasional Raspberry Pi project.
Given the Raspberry Pi's versatility, you might be wondering how much memory you need. The Pi 5 specifically comes in five different versions, ranging from 1GB to 16GB of RAM. The choice matters more than a typical desktop PC too — you cannot upgrade the memory once you've taken delivery of it. At the same time, though, you could find yourself spending hundreds of dollars for extra RAM that you don't actually need.
You need less RAM than you think
You may recognize that most new laptops and PCs ship with at least 8GB of memory. The MacBook Air, for instance, includes 16GB of RAM in its base configuration and you can pay a few hundred dollars to upgrade that spec. Many higher-end laptops ship with 32GB of RAM too. Unless you have a specific use case, you probably won't actually need as much memory in a Raspberry Pi.
The difference between a typical computer and the Raspberry Pi is that the latter runs a much more lightweight operating system. Windows and macOS are designed to utilize available RAM, even when idling on the desktop with no additional programs running in the foreground. On the other hand, Raspberry Pi OS, which is based on Linux, doesn't typically engage as many resources or process a lot of intensive background tasks. In practical terms, the operating system consumes just a few hundred megabytes of RAM.
That's not to say you can get away with the bare minimum 1GB of RAM spec in all scenarios. Even on Raspberry Pi OS, running desktop-class programs like a web browser or word processor will quickly fill up the board's memory. Three or four media-heavy Firefox tabs can be enough to overwhelm the 1GB Pi and force it to use physical storage to swap programs in and out of memory (which can cause slowdowns).
How much RAM do I need on a Raspberry Pi?
For desktop use, a Raspberry Pi with at least 2GB of RAM has enough headroom to run multiple programs or tabs simultaneously. The Raspberry Pi 5's processor is fast enough for light multitasking and basic games, so you'll want more memory to take advantage of the available performance.
The downside is cost: each step up in RAM takes you further away from the $45 base price of the Raspberry Pi 5. The 4GB RAM model, for example, will set you back $110 without improving any other specs on the board.
So if the Raspberry Pi needs more RAM for multitasking, does that mean you should never buy the base 1GB version? Not quite — many people use the Raspberry Pi as a media server, network-attached storage device, smart home hub or security system with the official camera add-on. These projects all have one thing in common: you don't need a display connected to the Raspberry Pi. This is called headless operation, and allows you to squeeze more from limited hardware like the 1GB Pi 5.
Without a connected display, the Raspberry Pi can diligently perform tasks and quietly go about its business. That makes the 1GB model more than usable, and one of the cheapest entry points into the hobby. However, the Pi's value proposition doesn't hold up at higher price points. The processor is ultimately not powerful enough to replace an actual computer for intensive tasks.
Is the 8GB or 16GB Raspberry Pi worth it?
Unless you need the Raspberry Pi's compact form factor for a particular project, like a battery-powered robot, it's not recommended paying the premium for an 8GB or 16GB model.
The Raspberry Pi's greatest advantage is its affordable price tag. Even with competition in the single-board computer space ramping up over the past decade, the Pi 5's $45 starting price is still a bargain. The same cannot be said for the 8GB or 16GB models. At $175 and $305 respectively, though, you're paying a sizable premium for memory alone.
This isn't exactly a secret — you could buy the 8GB Raspberry Pi for just $80 when it launched in 2023. However, the ongoing RAM shortage forced the company to raise its prices across the board in 2025.
Rising component costs have affected all hardware manufacturers, but larger brands enjoy more negotiating leverage through bulk deals. Case in point: you can find a plethora of mini PCs with 8GB of RAM in the sub-$200 price range. These boast far more powerful CPUs, onboard storage and extra ports like dual-Ethernet and multiple display outputs.
I personally moved on from the Raspberry Pi years ago when I discovered that secondary markets like eBay are flooded with refurbished business-grade mini PCs. Some examples include the Lenovo ThinkCentre and HP EliteDesk lines. Even though these units typically feature older CPUs, they run circles around the Raspberry Pi 5. The only downside to mini PCs is that they consume more power, so the Pi is more efficient for round-the-clock use. Even then, the difference boils down to just a few dollars over the course of a year.
But if you're not trying to build a media server and just need a Pi for the occasional project, choose the 1GB or 2GB model and call it a day.

articles.title: iPhone Air 2 sẽ mỏng hơn bản tiền nhiệm nhưng có pin lớn hơn
articles.text:
iPhone Air 2 có thể sẽ có độ dày ngang iPhone Duo khi mở ra, camera 48MP và chip A20 Pro, hứa hẹn nhiều cải tiến đáng chú ý.
Theo blogger Hàn Quốc “yeux1122”, mẫu iPhone kế nhiệm của iPhone Air có thể trở thành chiếc iPhone mỏng nhất từ trước đến nay của Apple.
Cụ thể, iPhone Air 2 được cho là sẽ có độ dày khoảng 5,2mm, giảm 0,4mm so với phiên bản đầu tiên. Độ dày này tương đương với iPhone Duo khi mở ra. Mặc dù mức giảm 7% có vẻ không lớn, nhưng sự khác biệt này có thể cảm nhận rõ rệt khi cầm trên tay, đặc biệt với một chiếc smartphone được thiết kế với tiêu chí mỏng nhẹ.
iPhone 18 Pro hiện tại có độ dày 8,75mm, nếu những số liệu rò rỉ là chính xác, rõ ràng iPhone Air 2 mỏng hơn đáng kể so với thiết kế của chiếc smartphone cao cấp nhất hiện nay của “nhà Táo”.
Tuy nhiên, người dùng sẽ phải chờ thêm một thời gian để xác nhận độ mỏng thực sự của iPhone Air 2. Mẫu smartphone dự kiến sẽ ra mắt vào đầu năm sau, cùng với mẫu iPhone 18 cơ bản và một phiên bản giá rẻ iPhone 18e.
Thông tin chi tiết về iPhone Air 2 vẫn còn hạn chế, nhưng một số tin đồn đã xuất hiện. Jon Prosser, leaker (người chuyên tiết lộ bí mật) công nghệ nổi tiếng, đã công bố một video hồi tháng 7, cho biết iPhone Air 2 sẽ được trang bị camera siêu rộng 48 megapixel và camera ống kính thường 48 megapixel, đánh dấu sự nâng cấp đáng kể so với phiên bản đầu tiên chỉ có một camera duy nhất. Leaker cũng cho biết Apple sẽ thiết kế lại camera Face ID để tích hợp thêm ống kính nâng cấp.
Ngoài ra, thời lượng pin của iPhone Air 2 cũng được kỳ vọng sẽ cải thiện. Prosser cho biết điện thoại này sẽ sử dụng chip A20 Pro, giúp nâng cao hiệu suất và thời lượng pin, mặc dù không quá ấn tượng nhưng vẫn có thể nhận thấy.
Một thông tin rò rỉ khác cho biết iPhone Air 2 sẽ có pin 3.500 mAh, tăng 11% so với pin 3.149 mAh của phiên bản đầu tiên.
Cuối cùng, Prosser dự đoán rằng iPhone Air 2 sẽ sử dụng khung giữa bằng titan giống như phiên bản gốc, với màu tím oải hương thay thế cho màu xanh da trời hiện tại.

articles.title: They War-Gamed Dimming the Sun. It Went Even Worse Than You Think
articles.text:
When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. That was until one morning last September in London, when the climate researcher took part in the first in a series of war games. The goal: to prevent an uncontrolled global race to develop a technology aimed at cooling the planet but that comes with vast, unknown risks that could reshape life on Earth.
“I thought that would be such an easy thing. Like, we can all agree to do ethical research and make sure it's for the better of all humans,” she told WIRED. “And boy, was I wrong.”
The simulation, titled Exploring Geopolitical Tipping Points and Climate Cooling Strategies, saw a couple dozen foreign-relations experts, scientists, military personnel, and former government officials from across the world convene in a meeting room at Queen Mary University of London. After making introductions over coffee and little yogurts, they sat at tables arranged in a square with the name of the country or organization each person was playing: national governments, climate NGOs and nonprofits, indigenous groups, and tech companies. Golja was assigned to provide technical advice to help participants make scientifically literate decisions.
The point of the game was to stress-test the world’s response to a group of prospective technologies known collectively as solar radiation modification. These technologies promise to reverse global warming by reflecting away a portion of the sunlight reaching Earth, for example by spraying particles of sulphur dioxide or some other manufactured substance into the atmosphere. The cooling effect of this kind of solar geoengineering is widely accepted. It would mimic the well-known impacts of large volcanic eruptions, which temporarily cool the planet by half a degree or more. But the fallout is less certain—and less equal. Some regions will suffer: Models predict drying in sub-Saharan Africa and more intense tropical storms in the Atlantic. The cooling effect would also last only as long as the geoengineering continued; after that the global temperature could shoot back up with wild and hard-to-predict effects.
Until recently, the idea of solar radiation modification was a speculative niche of climate science. That has changed fast. Private firms are exploring solar geoengineering as a commercial opportunity: Last year, a US-Israeli startup called Stardust Solutions raised $60 million, and in May it released details of a suite of new inventions it claims would give humans the ability to dial down the global temperature as desired. In August, Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX might be a candidate for delivering geoengineering interventions, threw his voice behind solar geoengineering, writing on X: “Space satellites to control temperature and massive geo-engineering will be needed or it will be game over.”
The world is going to have to make decisions about how to govern this technology much sooner than most policymakers imagine, Cynthia Scharf, a former UN advisor, told WIRED. “It's not 15 years from now; it's in the next decade, easily.”
It was against this backdrop that Danielle Young, an assistant professor in international relations at Leeds University, arranged the war game. Its setting was a hastily convened UN committee charged with coordinating the international response to developments in solar geoengineering. The game unfolded over simulated meetings set at three points in time: the present, September 2027, and September 2028. Each step ratcheted up the stakes, with the game creators introducing new advances in sunlight-reflecting technology. As in real life, no one knew all the facts, and players had to respond to events that were bringing the world closer to a full-scale attempt at deploying solar geoengineering tech, even when they may not have a full picture of what had truly occurred—or what any of the others were up to.
The first session set the tone. Distrust and disinformation dominated. As participants discussed rules governing outdoor experiments in an attempt to agree an international deal, players representing both the US and China told the group they could not sign a deal that constrained their pursuit of research considered to be in their “national interest.” Nor could they accept a deal that would see their superpower rival taking the lead technologically. Speaking to WIRED, Jeffrey Nielsen, a major in the US Army who played the role of a US national security attaché, summarized the position as “worse than no deal at all is any deal that favors China.”
Tensions escalated when the team running the simulation handed the Russian delegates an “intelligence report” indicating they had found a plane near the Bering Strait believed to be involved in a US geoengineering research program. The US team—which was indeed flying research missions—accused Russia of disinformation.
Meanwhile, the US became convinced China was also conducting research and developing its own program. Beijing’s representatives had tried to insert language into a mooted deal that would ensure no retroactive punishment for past experiments. Then, China approached a player representing SpaceX to float the idea of a technology-sharing program. In a private discussion away from the group, the SpaceX player immediately reported the Chinese approach to the US team. The US demanded an international investigation. The finger-pointing continued, and countries abandoned the talks. The Canadian representative called it a “humiliating defeat.”
At the end of the session, Nielsen was pumped. He’d busted China and derailed any prospect of a global deal. In the context of the game, he told WIRED, it was a “humungous victory” for the Americans. But Young, the researcher who designed the scenario, said the Chinese were not, in fact, conducting experiments in the game. Mutual suspicion meant all parties left the room believing the others were moving as quickly as possible to build their own geoengineering capability.
What played out in the first session reflected “the likelihood, in my opinion, of the geoengineering arms race,” says Nielsen, who clarified he was speaking to WIRED in a private capacity and not representing the views of the actual US government. Most experts agree it would take a superpower’s reach to ensure the safe passage of planes needed to deliver payloads of dust to the stratosphere in a geoengineering exercise. But neither the US nor China would lightly cede control over the global thermostat, says Nielsen, and distrust and poor communication are a significant risk: “Any action related to the issue by one actor can be perceived as malintent by the other.”
The threat of falling behind a rival is “a very strong driver of research and development of capability,” a former British diplomat with a background in national security told WIRED. “But that's not at all the same thing as deployment.” There are similarities with nuclear arms dynamics—though solar radiation management, unlike nukes, has more obvious benefits as well as downsides, many of which are poorly understood. “There is an interdependence here,” says the former diplomat, who was not involved in the game and spoke on condition of anonymity to preserve relationships. “It's not an inherently zero-sum game.”
Scharf, who represented the US government alongside Nielsen in the game, told WIRED a “scientifically transparent international collaboration” between China and the US “might be the best we can do in terms of fending off a very dangerous competition between the two. But I certainly cannot imagine that happening under the Trump administration.”
Compounding the problem is a lack of information. Geoengineering has historically been viewed with suspicion and often ignored by the scientific mainstream. One researcher told WIRED he’d experienced ostracization and barriers to academic progression owing to his interest in the technology; he no longer works in the field.
This lack of scientific interest greatly frustrated Golja, who spent much of the game watching as a bystander while political posturing dominated. Given the low level of knowledge around solar radiation modification and its side effects, she was one of very few experts who could help the participants understand the climate impacts of what they were discussing—yet she was largely ignored.“I was just so surprised about how little anyone actually cared about the science,” she says.
In the next sessions, the organizers tried in vain to nudge the talks back toward the realities of climate change. The participants received frequent notifications of climate disasters. These barely registered. Golja had prepared an “emulator,” a real-world demonstration of the best available science on how solar radiation management might affect weather patterns in different regions. It was ignored. If country representatives asked her anything, it was usually a leading question looking for data that would serve their ends or frame a rival’s proposal as reckless.
Then, during the last day, players were trying to find a way to respond to reports that a major plume of aerosols had been detected. In the game, this had been caused by a joint US-Saudi test of Stardust’s technology, though not everyone knew this. Finally, scientific advice was at a premium. Countries needed to know how to establish a monitoring network of satellites and other observational tools in order to prevent tests like this from happening in secret. A player representing an NGO called the Climate Futures Cooperative approached Golja, offering her money to fund such a scheme.
“Great. Fabulous. Why wouldn't I do that?” she recalls thinking.
But it soon came out that the Climate Futures Cooperative was actually backed by the fossil fuel industry. The organizers had recognized that fossil fuel companies and major producing countries like the US and Saudi Arabia would have a clear interest in removing barriers from the development of a technology that could combat climate change without having to immediately stop burning coal, oil, and gas. The shadowy NGO spent the game subtly wrecking the vibe and carping about process—though mostly they just sat back and let it burn. Some players—Russia, the US, SpaceX and Stardust—figured out the CFC was not what it seemed, says Young. “But they assessed it was to their benefit and didn’t draw attention to it.” Then the CFC chose its moment to offer money to Golja, only to crater her credibility, isolating and fragmenting the voice of science in the room.
“It was a whole mess,” says Golja.
That final lesson in fossil fuel realpolitik was about all Golja could endure. By the end of the last day, she was in tears.
At no point did the countries in the game agree to a deal, despite multiple proposals being put forward. European countries and Canada tried to build support for safeguards and open scientific research, but the talks constantly got bogged down by delay tactics and veered into tense showdowns over duelling strategic interests. In their final report, the researchers running the simulation—whose work was sponsored by the UK government-funded Advanced Research and Invention Agency—concluded that “strategic competition and state sovereignty drove the simulations, not climate concerns.”
Simulations like this one are not supposed to predict the future. The outcomes depend on the design of the game and the relative personalities and experience of the players. Many of those in the room lacked first-hand diplomatic and national security experience. The UN forum, which organizers selected as the game’s setting, may also not be as effective as talks between smaller groups of major countries. But the experiment in London echoed and refracted through the real world, during and after the months it was running.
In March, two papers from conservative US think tanks urged the Trump administration to take the lead on solar radiation modification and counter China’s threat. One memorably invoked a new, MAGA-coded term: “Weather sovereignty.” This month, the Observer newspaper in London revealed that the UK Ministry of Defense had paid a deep tech security consultancy to conduct research into sunlight reflection. Then, last week, the British government released its first official policy paper on the field, backing further research but stating firmly that it did not support deployment and “does not plan to do so.” Stardust has continued its lobbying of the US and governments around the world; CEO Yanai Yedvab told WIRED its job was getting easier as, unlike before, “the majority of policymakers … are already aware of this technology.”
Stardust has always maintained that it will not conduct large-scale outdoor experiments, let alone full deployment, before global governance is in place. “We are developing a very powerful tool,” Yedvab says. “When you develop this kind of powerful technology—and you have many precedents—national interests will play out. We're not naive about it.”
Meanwhile, drivers of the climate crisis are intensifying. During the time span of the game, efforts to curtail the use of fossil fuels were being undermined by rising energy costs and political hostility. Week after week, an incredible summer of drought and heat pounded Europe. In the final week of August, the collapse of a glacier on the Tibet-Nepal border fulfilled the prophecies of decades of climate scientists, killing more than 1,450 people.
In the months since the simulation ended, Golja has reevaluated many things. On a corkboard behind her desk, she has pinned up a note to herself, laying out a vision for life in a world ruled by narrow geopolitical self-interest rather than science, evidence, and reason. Her answer: She plans to return to the small coastal town where she grew up in Connecticut and use her expertise to help local climate groups build the seawalls and coastal erosion buffers they will need to cope with the inevitable. “To try and make a difference where it feels like I actually have traction,” she says. After what she saw, pursuing science in the hope of informing global decisions no longer held as much appeal. “Now it feels a little bit more personal.”

articles.title: Elon Musk has donated over $276 million to Republican midterm efforts
articles.text:
Elon Musk has handed out at least $276 million to Republican groups since July, The New York Times reports, making him both the party’s top known donor and the biggest established midterm donor. $158 million of that money — one of the largest political donations in American history — has been funneled into the Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC that aims to secure and maintain a Republican Senate majority. Among others, it’s fighting to retain the party’s Senate seat in Texas, which serves as a major hub for Musk’s business empire.
Elon Musk has donated over $276 million to Republican midterm efforts
He’s by far the biggest known midterm donor.
He’s by far the biggest known midterm donor.
He’s also donated over $76 million to America PAC, a super PAC Musk founded in 2024 that canvasses for hard-to-reach Republican voters. Smaller amounts have also been given to other conservative groups, including:
- $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund super PAC for House Republicans
- $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, supporting Ken Paxton’s Senate Seat bid in Texas
- $10 million to the Republican Governors Association
- $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association
The roughly $366 million that Musk has donated to federal committees over the entire 2025-26 election cycle is significantly higher than the $290 million he gave out in 2024 to help President Trump return to office, when he pledged to spend “around $45 million a month.” That’s despite Musk announcing in May last year that “In terms of political spending, I’m going to do a lot less in the future.” He’s consistently failed to stick to that promise so far.

articles.title: OpenAI adds 200 Dublin jobs and builds its second applied AI lab
articles.text:
OpenAI is adding 200 roles in Dublin and building an applied AI lab at its EU headquarters, taking planned Irish hiring to 450. The move lands two days before Ireland hosts the International AI Summit under its EU presidency.
OpenAI is adding 200 jobs in Dublin and building an applied AI lab at its European headquarters. That takes its planned Irish hiring to 450 roles.
The company announced the roles in a statement on Monday, Bloomberg reported, and employs more than 120 people in Ireland. They include forward deployed, solutions and privacy engineers, plus sales and user operations.
It follows the 250 roles announced in July, when OpenAI took an 88,000 square foot lease at the Tropical Fruit Warehouse in the Docklands. The company moves in from December.
The lab is the second of its kind. It is a deployment unit rather than a research one, pairing engineers with customers building on OpenAI’s existing models.
The first opened in Singapore in May, with a S$300M commitment, about $235M, and roughly 200 staff planned. OpenAI has published no equivalent figure for Dublin.
Chief financial officer Sarah Friar said Ireland had been critical to the company’s success in Europe since the headquarters opened three years ago. OpenAI is also extending its OpenAI for Ireland programme for startups and smaller firms.
Taoiseach Micheál Martin called the investment a vote of confidence in the Irish economy, and IDA Ireland, which supported it, sent chief executive Michael Lohan. The timing is not accidental.
Dublin hosts the International AI Summit on Wednesday. Ireland holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU until the end of December, and Martin tied the announcement to both.
That presidency is contested. Ireland draws a large share of its corporate tax from the companies whose digital files it is now steering, and the Irish Council for Civil Liberties has asked it to recuse itself.
The Dublin entity also decides who can police OpenAI in Europe. The Data Protection Commission recognised OpenAI Ireland as the company’s single establishment in the bloc in February 2024.
That recognition has already killed a fine. A Rome court annulled Italy’s €15M penalty against OpenAI in March, finding the Garante had lost competence once the Irish regulator took over.
Main establishment status is not automatic. It requires the Irish office to take real decisions about how personal data is processed, and OpenAI is now hiring privacy engineers into it.
The hiring also lands in a city shedding tech jobs. TikTok proposed cutting about 300 Dublin roles in July, and Meta cut 8,000 globally in May.

articles.title: Why you shouldn't leave an extension cord plugged in all the time - Engadget
articles.text:
Why you shouldn't leave an extension cord plugged in all the time
Your wall outlet may handle the load, but that doesn't mean the extension cord will.
Extension cords are amazing at making temporary solutions permanent. You connect a laptop charger because the outlet is in an inconvenient location and you hide the cord behind your desk and six months later it's as if it's part of the furniture.
That's where the trouble begins. Extension cords are not permanent wiring additions and can become damaged over time if used continuously, according to the Electrical Safety Foundation International (ESFI). When you're done, unplugging one is a good opportunity to observe cracked insulation, loose connections or a plug that is getting hotter than you would prefer.
To be clear, an empty extension cord doesn't inevitably start cooking itself simply because its plug is still in the wall. The question is, what happens when that cord becomes a part of your daily routine? It can be trapped behind furniture, damaged (especially in the event of lightning) or simply asked to power something much more demanding than the phone charger it was originally being used for.
The electrical code doesn't treat extension cords as permanent wiring
The National Electrical Code (NEC) has a pretty clear definition of the difference. According to Section 400.12, flexible cords and cord sets should not replace a structure's fixed wiring. It also prohibits running them through holes in walls, floors and ceilings, through doorways or windows, or anywhere they are likely to be physically damaged. The specific version and amendments of the NEC that are in effect may differ from location to location.
There are also a few time limits referred to in extension cord tips, but they can be confusing. The NEC's temporary-installation rules have a 90-day limit for holiday decorative lighting and similar purposes. That doesn't mean every extension cord in the U.S. becomes prohibited on day 91. A separate rule of thumb from workplace safety organization MEMIC is that if equipment has been powered by an extension cord for over 30 days, it's time to consider a permanent solution.
For a home office, that might mean adding an outlet where it's needed, rather than an extension cord that will live behind your desk for the next five years. ESFI also recommends against covering cords because doing so can prevent heat from escaping, which can lead to overheating.
The cord has its own limit, too
Your circuit breaker is not a universal guardian angel for all things plugged into the wall. Extension cords are available in various wire gauges, lengths and current ratings and the cord must be able to support whatever you are plugging into it.
This is important because a laptop charger and a space heater place very different loads on a cord. Extension cords can overheat and cause fires, so the U.S. Fire Administration recommends that major appliances be plugged directly into wall outlets. Its guidance for portable heaters is even easier: Never use an extension cord or power strip. Plugging a power strip into a smart plug can create a separate overload risk, too.
Cord daisy-chaining isn't a neat trick, either. ESFI also recommends against daisy-chaining extension cords, and placing one under a rug or running it through a doorway creates another opportunity for heat buildup or damage.
These failures aren't purely theoretical. Loudoun County Fire and Rescue attributed a July 2026 house fire in Virginia to the electrical failure of an extension cord. Five occupants were displaced. The release didn't specify what was plugged into the cord or how long it had been in use, so the incident does not indicate that leaving a cord unused and plugged in was the cause.
The practical rule is less dramatic: Check the cord's rating, replace damaged cords and unplug temporary setups when you're finished with them. ESFI lists 25- to 50-foot 16-gauge cords for 1 to 13 amps, 14-gauge cords for 14 to 15 amps and 12- or 10-gauge cords for 16 to 20 amps.

articles.title: ‘The Sixty-Year Mission’ Brings the Legacy of ‘Star Trek’ to a New Generation
articles.text:
William Shatner wasn’t sure if the audience would approve of his new documentary or not.
When the 95-year-old star took the stage at the Regal Times Square theater for the New York premiere of The Sixty-Year Mission: How Star Trek Changed Television and the World he said “maybe you’ll like it, maybe you won’t.” But, the Captain Kirk actor declared, “you’re going to see a lovely film made by people who cared.”
Focusing on the original Star Trek series, which ran from 1966 to 1969, The Sixty-Year Mission is written and directed by Mark A. Altman, creator of the Inglorious Treksperts podcast. The documentary, which screened during New York Comic Con and hit select theaters this weekend, explores the show’s cultural impact and legacy, and also demonstrates how much it was a product of the political climate of the era in which it was made.
“I think audiences are pleasantly surprised that Sixty-Year Mission shows how the ‘60s shaped Star Trek,” Altman explains. For the film, Altman interviewed dozens of prominent fans and stars, from Shatner and Simon Pegg to Star Trek: The Next Generation stars Jonathan Frakes and Brent Spiner. The president’s niece—and Trek fan—Mary L. Trump praises the show’s pioneering representation, specifically Nichelle Nichols’ Lieutenant Uhura. George Takei, who played Sulu, gives a harrowing account of his time in an internment camp for Japanese Americans during World War II. Others discuss how characters like Spock became heroes for queer fans.
As has been well-documented, these considerations were important for Gene Roddenberry, the show’s creator, who died in 1991. He was a WWII veteran with a progressive bent despite years spent in traditionally conservative spaces like the US Army and the Los Angeles Police Department. Altman insists that “Captain Kirk was ‘JFK: Space Captain,’” and that President Kennedy’s idea of a New Frontier was the final frontier that Trek sought to explore.
Shatner, however, didn’t initially see the show that way at all. “I didn't think in those terms when they offered me the role,” says Shatner, who served as executive producer on Sixty-Year Mission. “I thought, ‘I got a regular paid job.’ Only later did the magic of Star Trek happen.”
Part of that magic, Shatner adds, is how “Star Trek had an effect on people’s lives.” Those people come from many backgrounds, and the show remained accessible because of the very special tension that existed within its politics, Altman explains. “Roddenberry was liberal on social issues but hard-nosed on defense, and that is absolutely what Star Trek is,” he says. “We need our phasers to defeat the Klingons, but we believe in a diverse crew.”
Karim Diané, who plays Jay-Den Kraag on Star Trek: Starfleet Academy, notes that as the person playing the first openly gay Klingon character in the franchise, he’s playing someone who means a lot to viewers. “I wish I could release the DMs because the love I've gotten is overwhelming,” Diané says.
Trek even had a point of view on AI that feels incredibly relevant in 2026 as Trump and Silicon Valley leaders talk about a new era of “superintelligence.” The franchise’s most recognizable AI—the android Data from Next Generation—was an ideal version of the technology. In that series Data consistently struggled to be understood, as both smarter than humans and incapable of emotional intelligence. One episode, “The Measure of a Man,” even addressed whether Data was his own being or merely property.
For Spiner, who played Data, AI’s modern incarnation is far from the thoughtful machine he portrayed. “If only AI could be what Data was: responsible, truly concerned about humanity, considering what serves humans best as opposed to what serves profit best,” he says.

articles.title: HPT D-DAY 2026: từ công nghệ thật đến kết quả thật
articles.text:
Ngày 15/10/2026 sắp tới tại Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, Công ty Cổ phần Dịch vụ Công nghệ Tin học HPT (mã HPT-UPCOM) tổ chức sự kiện HPT D-DAY 2026 với chủ đề R³ - Real Technology, Real Operation, Real Result (Công nghệ thật, Vận hành thật, Kết quả thật).
Đây là sự kiện công nghệ thường niên quy mô lớn của HPT dự kiến quy tụ khoảng 650 khách tham dự và gần 30 hãng công nghệ hàng đầu tạo không gian kết nối giữa lãnh đạo, chuyên gia công nghệ, doanh nghiệp, đối tác và các đơn vị ứng dụng trong nước và quốc tế.
HPT D-DAY 2026 - Công nghệ thật, Vận hành thật, Kết quả thật
Năm nay với chủ đề R³ - Real Technology, Real Operation, Real Result (Công nghệ thật, Vận hành thật, Kết quả thật), sự kiện công nghệ HPT D-DAY 2026 tập trung vào những công nghệ thực sự phù hợp với doanh nghiệp, những giải pháp giải quyết các bài toán vận hành thực tế và mang lại kết quả có thể đo lường. Bên cạnh các xu hướng như AI, dữ liệu, an toàn thông tin, hạ tầng số và tự động hóa, chương trình cũng đề cập đến những yếu tố quan trọng trong bối cảnh mới như đạo đức và tuân thủ.
HPT D-DAY là sự kiện công nghệ thường niên kết nối cộng đồng doanh nghiệp, chuyên gia và các đối tác công nghệ.
Chương trình "HPT D-DAY 2026" sẽ diễn ra trong cả ngày bao gồm Phiên khai mạc vào buổi sáng với nội dung về bức tranh công nghệ 2026 và xu hướng AI, khảo sát "Ứng dụng AI trong tổ chức"; 4 phiên chuyên đề vào buổi chiều về chiến lược công nghệ, hạ tầng & dữ liệu AI, an toàn thông tin & an ninh hậu lượng tử và ứng dụng công nghệ theo ngành.
Được định hướng theo mô hình diễn đàn công nghệ và ứng dụng, HPT D-DAY 2026 đề cao trải nghiệm và tương tác, tạo cơ hội để khách tham dự tiếp cận các mô hình vận hành thực tế, trao đổi trực tiếp với chuyên gia, đối tác và doanh nghiệp đã triển khai thành công các giải pháp, từ đó tìm ra hướng ứng dụng phù hợp cho tổ chức của mình.
Trong khuôn khổ sự kiện, khách tham dự có thể trải nghiệm các mô hình mô phỏng tình huống vận hành thực tế tại khu trình diễn và khám phá gần 20 gian hàng công nghệ tại khu triển lãm đến từ HPT cùng các đối tác là những doanh nghiệp CNTT hàng đầu tại Việt Nam và trên thế giới.
HPT D-DAY 2026 có các hoạt động kết nối, tư vấn nhanh và trao đổi chuyên sâu, giúp khách tham dự tìm hiểu khả năng triển khai giải pháp theo từng tình huống, điều kiện và yêu cầu thực tế.
Sự kiện HPT D-DAY 2026 nhận được sự quan tâm và đồng hành của nhiều đối tác công nghệ hàng đầu trong và ngoài nước như IBM, Microsoft, Oryza, Check Point, HPE, SearchInform, FIS, Fortinet, M.Tech, ADG, Misoft, NT&T, NetApp, Red Hat, Elite, Specter AI, Clientron, Dell, FUDO, KST Solution, Opentext, Tech Data, CADTECH, Mi2, Yubico, TechHorizon, VietSoft Vision và đối tác đồng hành truyền thông HCA (Hội Tin học Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh).
Đặc biệt, chương trình còn có sự đồng hành của các diễn giả khách mời đến từ Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam, Cục Thuế, Trung tâm Chuyển đổi số Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, Hiệp hội Dữ liệu Quốc gia, Hiệp hội An ninh mạng quốc gia, KPMG Vietnam, Tổng cục Công nghiệp Quốc phòng, Sacombank, Công ty VNG, sẽ mang đến những chia sẻ sâu sắc và thông tin chuyên môn hữu ích cho hội thảo.
Doanh nghiệp và độc giả quan tâm có thể tìm hiểu chi tiết sự kiện tại trang thông tin chính thức
Khảo sát "Thực trạng Ứng dụng AI trong tổ chức": doanh nghiệp đang ở đâu trên hành trình ứng dụng AI?
Để công nghệ thực sự đi vào vận hành và tạo ra kết quả, doanh nghiệp cần nhìn rõ mình đang ở đâu trên hành trình ứng dụng AI. Không chỉ dừng ở việc "đã dùng AI hay chưa", các tổ chức hiện nay cần hiểu rõ AI đang phục vụ mục tiêu nào, đã đi vào quy trình nào, tạo ra kết quả gì, dữ liệu và con người đã sẵn sàng đến đâu, cũng như việc sử dụng AI đã được quản trị có trách nhiệm hay chưa.
Năm 2026, HPT phối hợp cùng HCA tiếp tục triển khai khảo sát "Thực trạng ứng dụng AI trong tổ chức". Khảo sát năm nay được kế thừa mục tiêu cốt lõi của năm trước, đồng thời được nâng cấp về phương pháp, nội dung và cách phân tích nhằm phản ánh sát hơn thực tế ứng dụng AI trong giai đoạn mới: từ nhận thức, thử nghiệm đến triển khai, tối ưu, mở rộng và vận hành bằng AI.
Kết quả khảo sát hướng đến xây dựng một bức tranh trung thực, có hệ thống về mức độ ứng dụng AI của các tổ chức tại Việt Nam. Trên cơ sở đó, báo cáo sẽ giúp nhận diện xu hướng chung, các điểm mạnh, điểm nghẽn, khoảng cách năng lực và những ưu tiên cải thiện thiết thực trong thời gian tới.
HPT và HCA trân trọng mời Ban Lãnh đạo, Cán bộ Quản lý, chuyên gia và người phụ trách chuyển đổi số/AI tại các tổ chức tham gia khảo sát, cùng góp phần xây dựng bức tranh khách quan và thực chất về mức độ trưởng thành trong ứng dụng AI tại Việt Nam. Thông tin người tham gia được bảo mật và kết quả khảo sát không sử dụng cho mục đích thương mại. Báo cáo phân tích sẽ được gửi đến các đơn vị, cá nhân tham gia và trình bày chung tại sự kiện HPT D-DAY 2026.
