articles.title: Quán cà phê hoài niệm ở Hà Nội đóng cửa sau một thập kỷ
articles.text:
Trong nhiều năm, các căn hộ cũ, ban công và những tầng cao của tòa nhà được tận dụng để mở quán cà phê với phong cách riêng. Không gian hoài niệm, kiến trúc cũ và tầm nhìn từ trên cao giúp các địa điểm này thu hút khách hàng, đặc biệt là giới trẻ.
Một số quán cà phê còn chọn tầng thượng hoặc không gian penthouse để kinh doanh. Những địa điểm này thường được đầu tư thiết kế nhằm tạo trải nghiệm khác biệt, thu hút khách đến thưởng thức đồ uống, chụp ảnh và ngắm cảnh thành phố từ trên cao.
Theo quy định, căn hộ chung cư phải được sử dụng đúng mục đích. Hoạt động kinh doanh tại các căn hộ có công năng để ở có thể bị xử phạt nếu vi phạm quy định. Đây cũng là một trong những vấn đề đặt ra với các mô hình kinh doanh cà phê tại chung cư.
Quán cà phê Thi Nhân Các tại tầng 41, chung cư HH Linh Đàm (Hà Nội), chính thức dừng hoạt động từ ngày 1/10. Theo thông báo của quán, việc dừng kinh doanh nhằm thực hiện quy định của UBND TP Hà Nội về hoạt động kinh doanh thương mại tại nhà chung cư.
Trước khi đóng cửa, quán phục vụ cà phê kết hợp không gian đọc sách, giao lưu và chụp ảnh. Thi Nhân Các dự kiến trở lại tại một địa điểm khác với diện mạo mới. Tuy nhiên, thời gian và địa điểm cụ thể chưa được công bố.
Tại chung cư này, ban quản lý đã có văn bản yêu cầu rà soát hoạt động kinh doanh tại các căn hộ chung cư.
Cư Xá cũng thông báo dừng hoạt động từ ngày 31/8/2026. Quán được mở năm 2016 tại một căn nhà rộng khoảng 60m2 ở tầng 2 khu tập thể A11 Tôn Thất Tùng. Sau đó, diện tích quán được mở rộng lên khoảng 160m2.
Cư Xá tạo dấu ấn nhờ không gian gợi nhớ đời sống Hà Nội đầu những năm 1990. Nhiều vật dụng, đồ trang trí và món quà vặt gắn với tuổi thơ được đưa vào quán. Khách hàng còn có thể tham gia các hoạt động như chơi cờ, trò chơi dân gian, làm bánh chưng, làm đèn ông sao và vẽ tranh.
Không gian ban đầu gợi đến ký ức của những người từng sống trong các khu tập thể; về sau, quán cũng thu hút khách trẻ. Đại diện quán cho biết đây không phải là quyết định dễ dàng, bởi địa điểm này đã gắn bó với đội ngũ sáng lập và khách hàng suốt một thập kỷ.
Khó kinh doanh tại chung cư, tập thể cũ
Từng mở quán cà phê tại một khu tập thể ở Giảng Võ (Hà Nội), anh Hoàng Giang cho biết mô hình này có lợi thế nhờ không gian hoài niệm, thu hút nhiều khách hàng. Tuy nhiên, quá trình kinh doanh cũng phát sinh không ít bất tiện. Công trình xuống cấp, hạ tầng xung quanh hạn chế và thiếu chỗ để xe khiến việc đón khách gặp khó khăn.
Khi quán đông khách, tiếng ồn còn ảnh hưởng đến các hộ dân xung quanh. Quán cũng không thể hoạt động quá khuya. Sau một thời gian, anh quyết định đóng cửa và tìm địa điểm phù hợp hơn.
Ông Trần Khánh Minh Sơn, chuyên gia F&B, cho rằng các khu tập thể cũ và chung cư thường được người kinh doanh lựa chọn nhờ mật độ dân cư cao, vị trí thuận tiện và không gian mang nét riêng.
Tuy nhiên, căn hộ chung cư có công năng để ở phải được sử dụng đúng mục đích. Việc tận dụng căn hộ làm cơ sở kinh doanh có thể phát sinh vướng mắc về pháp lý, đồng thời ảnh hưởng đến sinh hoạt chung do tiếng ồn, lượng khách ra vào và nhu cầu trông giữ xe.
Ông Sơn nhận định một địa điểm có thể đông khách nhờ vị trí hoặc phong cách thiết kế. Tuy nhiên, nếu không phù hợp với công năng sử dụng được phê duyệt, hoạt động kinh doanh vẫn đối mặt với rủi ro pháp lý.
Trong bối cảnh cơ quan chức năng tăng cường quản lý việc sử dụng căn hộ chung cư, người kinh doanh cần xác định rõ địa điểm có được phép sử dụng để kinh doanh hay không.
Đây là yếu tố ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến khả năng duy trì hoạt động và thu hồi vốn đầu tư. Nếu bỏ qua điều kiện pháp lý, lợi thế kinh doanh trước mắt có thể trở thành rủi ro khi cơ sở phải đóng cửa hoặc chuyển địa điểm.

articles.title: Meta says its new Muse model has reached the AI frontier
articles.text:
Meta has released Muse Wonder, known internally as Watermelon, and says it matches ChatGPT and Claude on coding and professional work. It has not said whether the weights will be published, which decides what it owes under the EU AI Act.
Meta has released Muse Wonder, the most capable model to come out of the AI unit Mark Zuckerberg spent fourteen months rebuilding. Internally it was Watermelon.
It claims parity with ChatGPT and Claude on coding and on financial and legal work, chief AI officer Alexandr Wang told Bloomberg. The claim arrives without published benchmarks.
Meta has hit its own internal date. The Information reported in August that the company was targeting October for Watermelon, without establishing whether it would ship under the Muse name.
It is the third frontier claim this year. Wang said much the same about Muse Spark 1.3 in September, and Zuckerberg called the first Muse Spark a world-class assistant in April.
That first one came with a scorecard. Meta’s own figures placed it fourth on one index, at 52 against 57 for the leaders, and behind on two reasoning benchmarks.
Wang’s answer to doubters is that they should try it and judge for themselves. Benchmarks are a weak proof anyway, since they can be gamed and vary by task.
What has actually shipped is narrow. Developers can reach it through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, and it will power the paid tier of the Muse agent Meta launched last month.
The spending behind it is not narrow. Zuckerberg has committed hundreds of billions to infrastructure and paid $14B for a stake in Scale AI largely to recruit Wang. Shares rose as much as 4.7%.
For Europe the question is not the benchmark. It is whether Meta publishes the weights, and its record splits by size, open for a distilled 30B model, closed for the flagship.
Under Article 53 of the AI Act, a genuinely free and open model escapes some of the documentation owed to the AI Office. The licence has to be real, with weights, architecture and usage information public.
Meta has not said which way Muse Wonder goes. It had not decided for Muse Spark 1.3 either, and Zuckerberg has signalled caution about opening the most powerful systems.
The exemption has a ceiling regardless. Models carrying systemic risk owe the full set of obligations whatever their licence, and Meta declined to sign the code of practice written to operationalise them.
Speed cuts both ways here. Meta killed Muse Image three days after launch when its default settings turned out to opt public accounts in.

articles.title: The Yandex outage probably didn’t blitz Russian bots
articles.text:
Multiple Ukrainian drone strikes over the last week have taken Russian data centers offline and reportedly caused online bot traffic to plummet — but in reality it’s probably not the kind of bot activity most people associate with Russia.
The Yandex outage probably didn’t blitz Russian bots
At least, not the troll traffic that blights social media.
A chart citing Cloudflare data has been circulating around social media platforms, showing a sharp decline in bot traffic following attacks on Yandex servers — a technology company often described as “Russia’s Google.” While many people are inferring that the chart refers to bot farms that push disinformation, conspiracy theories, and other harmful content across online platforms, reputed troll farm exposer antibot4navalny says the data “has nothing to do with social media.”
In a thread on X, antibot4navalny says the chart is actually measuring requests from automated Yandex web crawlers. These bots have broad uses, so while they can be used maliciously to hack user accounts and target people with spam, they’re also very commonly used to index websites for search engines and provide customer service support. The chart is also specific to Yandex-based traffic, and not bot activity from Russia at large — which remains largely unchanged around the data center attacks, according to Cloudflare.
Other charts have also been shared that show the same alleged decline in Russian disinformation bot activity. One such diagram was shared on X by European Parliament member Tomáš Zdechovský, who claimed that online activity around the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) political party plummeted following the Russian data center attacks.
Computer scientist Raphael Wimmer says he suspects the source diagram shared by Zdechovský is AI-generated, pointing out several inconsistencies with the activity timeline it’s supposedly tracking, including a data point logged for a future date: October 15th. The image appears to have first been posted by Threads user Robin Schlingheider. The data’s source isn’t established, and the original doesn’t include any reference to Germany’s AfD party. Wimmer says Schlingheider has evaded his questions about where the image originated.
“Could we (and especially politicians, journalists and scientists who should know better) please stop sharing unverified images?” Wimmer said.
Meanwhile, the vast majority of Yandex-operated systems still appear to be offline following the latest drone strike, including the Yandex Pay digital payment service, leaving users unable to transfer funds, check balances, or make purchases. Yandex Fintech head Dima Pirogov said in a statement (translated via Google) that “we can’t yet give you a precise restoration timeline, but we promise: we won’t stop until the service is restored.”

articles.title: Google’s Fitbit Edge Debuts a Replaceable Battery—and Brings Back the Screen
articles.text:
Google’s screenless Fitbit Air made a splash, but it’s been three years since the company updated its display-equipped Charge 6. That older tracker is showing its age, lacking newer automatic workout detection, deeper health metrics, and an IP68 rating. That's where the new Fitbit Edge comes in.
Announced on Monday, it is the successor fitness tracker fans with a screen preference have been waiting for. It sits in a sweet spot at $180—not as costly as a Google Pixel Watch but offering a similar experience in a slimmer, pill-shaped design. And unlike the Pixel Watch, it's compatible with Android and iPhones via the Google Health app. Preorders are available now, and it goes on sale on October 27.
The Fixable Fitbit
The Edge has a user-replaceable battery, a Fitbit first, aligning with Google’s efforts to make its Pixel Watch more repairable. (Likely also due to new battery regulations set to take effect next year in the European Union.) Repair options will vary by region and availability.
If you find the Pixel Watch’s round face too bulky, the Edge's capsule-shaped alternative might suit smaller wrists better. If the Charge 6’s 1.04-inch display was too small, the Edge upgrades it to a larger 1.34-inch screen. The difference is noticeable, and that extra real estate could make a real impact when glancing at your metrics mid-workout.
The Edge borrows a few more attributes from the Pixel Watch, including an altimeter that uses atmospheric pressure to measure elevation changes. That means it can record elevation gain and loss during outdoor activities, track floors climbed, and add more context to your outdoor stats. It also has a far-field skin temperature sensor, replacing the standard device temperature sensor found in other Fitbits. By bringing some of the Pixel Watch’s more advanced hardware to a fitness-first wearable, Google is giving the Edge a compelling middle-ground position in its lineup at a Fitbit-friendly price.
The Edge inherits the Fitbit Air’s improvements while restoring several Charge 6 features the screenless tracker lacks, including built-in GPS and electrical sensors that work with the electrocardiogram (ECG) app. You can also control music playback on a connected Bluetooth device, as you could with the Charge 6, and Google Maps turn-by-turn directions will arrive later this year.
Google also announced more advanced automatic activity tracking for the Edge, using Gemini Intelligence to identify up to 100 workout types. It can track more than 50 exercise modes, up from 40 on its predecessor. Google will also roll out these features to the Pixel Watch 5 and Air. If they work as promised, it means users won't have to log every activity manually.
With a Google Health Premium subscription, the Edge can track blood pressure trends without manual calibration and insulin resistance trends without requiring a blood draw. Google first announced these capabilities alongside the Pixel Watch 5's debut, but they only became available at the end of September. They’re also available on the Air, keeping Google’s screenless tracker up to date as its lineup expands.
The seven-day battery life remains unchanged, but it’s one of the Edge’s biggest advantages over the Pixel Watch. Like the Air, it takes about 90 minutes to fully charge, which is half an hour less than the Charge 6.
One odd omission is a near-field communication (NFC) sensor, which means the Edge doesn’t support contactless payments through Google Wallet. That’s a downgrade from the Charge 6 and a strange function to lose on a fitness tracker that Google is pitching as a step up from its basic Fitbits.
Dressed for Every Occasion
The Edge introduces new digital and analog clock faces, and the Canyon band color returns from the Pixel Watch 5, alongside five other band styles (Active Band, Active Sport Band, Performance Loop Band, Magnet Band, and Metal Links Band). The Stephen Curry collaboration ($220), which also appeared with the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5, is back in the same brown-orange color.
Alongside the Edge, Google is also giving the screenless Fitbit Air a visual upgrade with a new Metal Mesh band. It’s an even dressier strap than the polyurethane Elevated Modern Band. The Air may have initially been designed to disappear on your wrist, but the new band makes it a statement accessory.
If you’re all in on the screenless Fitbit Air, the Edge won’t change your mind. But if you’re not ready to give up a display, the Edge might be a compelling and affordable alternative for both iPhone and Android users. Stay tuned for our review.

articles.title: Which accessories actually fit the iPhone Duo? - Engadget
articles.text:
Which accessories actually fit the iPhone Duo?
Shopping for iPhone Duo accessories? Here’s what you need to know.
If you own an iPhone Duo, you'll want to keep it insured and protected. You may also be asking which accessories actually fit the device.
Apple's new foldable measures 164.6 by 117.8 by 5.2 mm unfolded, and 84.1 by 117.8 by 11.3 mm folded, differing significantly from traditional iPhones. Apple provides manufacturers with a trove of dimensional drawings, which illustrate why older fitted accessories, particularly cases, will not fit.
Some accessories remain compatible. USB-C peripherals and most wireless chargers continue to work, but mechanical car mounts, most lens accessories, many screen protectors and cases will be incompatible.
What does fit? Apple's online store offers a curated collection of approved third-party accessories you know will be compatible, but it's expensive — even the company's infamous polishing cloth costs $9. But when looking to purchase new accessories, it's important to search for solutions built to match iPhone Duo's unique design in not only its size, but also its functionality.
What accessories fit the iPhone Duo?
The new dimensions are an opportunity for manufacturers to try new approaches with accessories. For example, ESR's vegan leather magnetic case protects the entire phone, including the hinge mechanism, and has a movable kickstand that doubles as a lens protector. Mous offers a thin aramid case manufactured using the same material used in body armor. While it lacks hinge protection, it adds just 1.7 mm to the 11.3 mm maximum thickness of the Duo. Spigen's cases use the iPhone's folding mechanism as a stand, while the Spigen Armor case offers much more robust protection.
Protection isn't just about the frame. Even if they fit, traditional tempered glass protectors will crack when you snap the phone shut. When purchasing screen protection for the iPhone Duo, you should seek flexible TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane) or PET (polyethylene terephthalate) film protectors designed for the foldable device. While less scratch-resistant than glass, these films can handle repeated folding and won't crack when snapped shut.
Apple promises a future software update to enable the USB-C Apple Pencil to work with iPhone Duo. Unlike the Pencil 2 or Pro, the USB-C model has its own independent charging and pairing facility using USB-C. Supporting the other models would have required the smartphone to host an additional high-power wireless charging coil capable of external-facing power exchange, which would have added to the device's thickness, cost and weight.
About MagSafe and wireless charging
The iPhone Duo supports MagSafe and 25-watt fast charging using the inbound wireless charging magnetic coils built into the rear panel of the device, underneath the camera. This means that existing MagSafe and Qi2 chargers should generally work. It also means MagSafe accessories should work, but as they are designed for the more traditional iPhone dimensions, you may find they overlap the device when connected.
MagSafe batteries will charge your device, but because they are designed to snap onto a longer iPhone, they will also hang off the edges of the frame. Accessory makers must create new MagSafe wallets and batteries to fit the new design.
When it comes to car mounts, magnetic MagSafe or Qi2 models should generally work with the iPhone Duo. Mechanical mounts may also be compatible, depending on whether their grips can accommodate the phone's dimensions.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 12/10: Thế giới xu hướng giảm, xăng hơn 28.000 đồng/lít
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Mở cửa phiên giao dịch đầu tuần này (12/10), giá dầu thế giới có xu hướng đi xuống.
Dữ liệu từ Oilprice cho hay, vào lúc 6h45' ngày 12/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent được niêm yết ở mức 103,8 USD/thùng, giảm 0,88% so với phiên liền trước. Còn giá dầu WTI được giao dịch ở mức 90,97 USD/thùng, hạ 0,96% so với phiên liền trước.
Trong tuần trước, giá dầu thế giới tăng khá mạnh. Tính chung trong cả tuần qua, giá dầu Brent tăng 2,4 USD/thùng, trong khi giá dầu WTI tăng 0,74 USD/thùng.
Giá dầu Brent đóng cửa tuần qua ở mức 104,7 USD/thùng, còn giá dầu WTI kết tuần trước ở mức 91,85 USD/thùng.
Giá dầu quốc tế trong tuần này được dự báo có xu hướng tăng, trong bối cảnh tình hình Trung Đông tiếp tục diễn biến phức tạp, làm gia tăng lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung năng lượng toàn cầu.
Reuters cho hay, các mối đe dọa đối với hoạt động vận chuyển dầu ở vịnh Ba Tư và eo biển Hormuz tiếp tục gia tăng trong tháng 10, khi cuộc xung đột giữa Mỹ - Israel và Iran bước sang tháng thứ 8.
Số vụ tấn công nhằm vào các tàu chở dầu đi qua eo biển Hormuz trong tuần qua đã lên mức cao nhất trong một tuần kể từ khi cuộc xung đột nổ ra.
Cùng với xung đột tại Trung Đông, căng thẳng giữa Nga và Ukraine cũng làm gián đoạn nguồn cung các loại nhiên liệu tinh chế như xăng, nhiên liệu bay và đặc biệt là dầu diesel.
Bên cạnh đó, giá dầu thế giới cũng chịu tác động từ cơn bão Isaias ở vùng vịnh Mỹ, khiến hàng loạt cơ sở khai thác dầu ngoài khơi phải tạm ngừng hoạt động.
Cơ quan Quản lý Khoáng sản biển Mỹ cho hay, tính đến ngày 8/10, các nhà sản xuất đã phải đóng cửa các giếng dầu có tổng công suất khoảng 1,3 triệu thùng/ngày, tương đương 62,9% sản lượng hiện tại của khu vực, để phòng tránh bão.
Những yếu tố này làm gia tăng lo ngại nguồn cung dầu có thể bị thắt chặt, từ đó hỗ trợ giá dầu thế giới.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (12/10) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 8/10, giá xăng E5RON92 tăng 1.134 đồng/lít, lên mức không cao hơn 27.703 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá xăng E10RON95-III tăng 1.065 đồng/lít, giá bán lẻ không cao hơn 28.254 đồng/lít.
Ở chiều ngược lại, giá dầu diesel 0.05S giảm 589 đồng/lít, xuống mức không cao hơn 29.128 đồng/lít.
Trong khi đó, giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S tăng 701 đồng/kg, lên mức không cao hơn 21.092 đồng/kg.
Dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương cho thấy, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp, đúng chỉ đạo và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng Chính phủ về các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: Tesla's robotaxis face a US safety review over school zone speeding
articles.text:
NHTSA has opened a defect petition review into claims that Tesla robotaxis exceeded posted speed limits in active school zones, covering about 1,000 vehicles with no reported crashes or injuries. Speeding is also the specific obstacle holding up Tesla’s bid for EU-wide approval of its driver-assistance software.
America’s road safety regulator is reviewing a claim that Tesla’s robotaxis speed through school zones. The petition says the cars exceeded posted limits in active zones with their automated driving systems engaged.
It covers 2026 model year Robotaxi, Model Y and Cybercab vehicles, an estimated 1,000 in total, Business Insider reported. The filing records no crashes, no injuries and no fatalities.
Those are the same 1,000 vehicles already under a separate NHTSA inquiry into how Tesla certified the Cybercab, which has no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors and which the company signed off itself.
The evidence is thin so far. An unnamed petitioner supplied three video links, the agency received the petition on 23 September and opened the review on 9 October.
This is not yet an investigation. A defect petition review decides only whether to grant or deny one, and the agency has set no deadline.
What makes it worth watching is the specific behaviour. Exceeding the posted limit is exactly what has stalled Tesla on the other side of the Atlantic.
Germany wants the system held to 10% above the limit and will argue that position in Brussels, while Reuters has reported the version Dutch regulators approved permits up to 50% over the detected one.
France and Sweden have both raised speeding concerns. The committee that was due to vote on EU-wide approval in October did not, and December is now the earliest.
The two cases are not the same system. Europe is weighing supervised software in cars with a responsible driver, while the American petition concerns driverless taxis with nobody at the wheel.
They share a company and a disputed speed setting. Regulators on both continents are now asking how fast the same manufacturer’s software decides to go.
There is a harder problem underneath. A King’s College London review of eight pedestrian detection systems found accuracy almost 20% higher for adults than children, and worse still in low light.
School zones have caught rivals too. Waymo was investigated after reports its cars passed stopped school buses, recalled vehicles in December, and in January one struck a child near a Santa Monica primary school, causing minor injuries.
Europe gets this question soon. Uber and Wayve already have approval in London for supervised autonomous rides, and Waymo plans a commercial service in the city.

articles.title: How Apple Puts Indigenous Languages on the iPhone Keyboard
articles.text:
Chuck Hoskin Jr. fondly recalls watching a room full of Cherokee immersion students crowd around a screen to watch How to Train Your Dragon. Except Hiccup and Astrid weren't speaking English—the protagonists were speaking Cherokee, dubbed by voices from the local community.
“They're hearing it in our mother tongue—that didn't happen a generation ago,” Hoskin Jr., principal chief of the Cherokee Nation, tells WIRED. “We're a long way, thankfully, from rote classroom instruction and memorization to a world where kids can see the sort of creativity that sparks imagination and helps every kid become more articulate and literate.”
The Cherokee Nation has around 1,500 active speakers left, and most are over 70. Hoskin Jr. says the community is rapidly losing that generation, which is why it has spent time training up second-language learners. It even has a baby immersion program, hoping their first words are Cherokee.
“The foes we’ve had historically are the so-called Age of Discovery, colonization, the displacement of our people economically and geographically, boarding schools,” he says. “But it's nothing compared to the mathematics we’re up against now. Which is why we’re filled with this urgency every day to do all we can to find partners that can help us accelerate what we want to do.”
One of those accelerants is Apple. The Cherokee Nation has long collaborated with the iPhone maker, and Cherokee was the first Native American language included in iOS in 2010. Today, Apple says its iOS keyboard supports more than 200 languages and language variants, with a handful added last year in iOS 26, like Haitian Creole and Nez Perce. In iOS 27, it expanded support for Indigenous languages to include other Native American languages like Blackfoot, Comanche, and Northern East Cree.
The goal is to meet young people where they already spend much of their waking hours: phone screens. Hoskin Jr. says that to revitalize and save a language, it has to become accessible. Apple says the effort isn't as simple as translating words. It’s a multi-year endeavor that requires deep research, and the company leans on community members for their expertise.
But the process doesn’t start in Cupertino. It actually begins with Unicode. You may have heard of the name—it’s the organization that approves and standardizes the new emoji that appear on your smartphone every year. It also handles time zone localization, currency names, imperial versus metric, and so on.
Before you can type or read a character on a smartphone screen, it needs to exist as a recognized character in the Unicode Standard. “Everything does start with Unicode in terms of a language, but it actually starts with characters and scripts,” says Unicode CEO Toral Cowieson. “We now have more than 157,000 characters that are included.”
Cowieson calls Unicode a kind of digital Switzerland—a neutral consortium where rivals like Apple, Microsoft, and Google sit at the same table as linguists and volunteer contributors. (Cowieson told WIRED earlier this year that Unicode had only four full-time employees.) Proposing a language, verifying it, and then encoding the character set can take three to five years.
After a script is encoded, platforms like Apple and Google need to add font support. Without this step, a character could appear as an empty box—often called “tofu.” Next is orthography: a set of rules and systems for writing a language. Often, languages have a well-defined orthography, but when it’s not standardized, communities use ad hoc replacements because historically available keyboards don't support it.
Take the glottal stop—the speech sound made in the throat between the syllables when you say, “uh-oh.” Some languages have distinct characters for glottal stops, but as some keyboards don’t support them, many indigenous cultures use alternatives, like a question mark, to represent the sound. That's when Apple connects with the community to figure out the best way to represent the sounds in digital text.
That brings us to the keyboard layout. When a community already has an established physical keyboard layout—like Osage—Apple adapts it directly to the software keyboard. Some cultures prefer the QWERTY layouts people are already familiar with.
Other languages need more custom approaches. For example, Nez Perce, or Nimipuutímt, does not use capital letters. Rather than having the Shift key toggle traditional uppercase letters, Apple repurposed it to reveal an accented secondary layer, so users don’t have to hold down individual keys to see those characters, which can slow typing. In the Cherokee language, each character mostly represents a consonant combined with a vowel sound, a form known as syllabary. Apple added adaptive vowel keys on the bottom row, so when a user types a consonant, these keys change to show the vowel combinations they can make.
That’s a newer change to the Cherokee keyboard—one Apple approached the community about, meaning building a keyboard for a language isn’t a one-and-done project.
But digitizing an indigenous culture’s language hasn't always been harmless. Genner Llanes-Ortiz, a Maya scholar and researcher at Bishop's University, studies how Indigenous people use digital technologies to reclaim language heritage. He recalls how Māori speakers rejected proposals to sell their language to tech companies.
“There’s a historical memory about the ways of dispossession that Indigenous peoples have experienced in the world,” Llanes-Ortiz says. “Māori working in their own revitalization efforts have been very firm in protecting access and storage of their linguistic materials because they have been exploited. They have experienced extraction of knowledge in the past.”
Language sovereignty and data ownership are top of mind, according to Chirasree Mandal, an Apple software engineer. “We don’t own anything, and we make it very clear that we are not trying to silo any data that we gain from this process,” she says. “It’s about making sure that the best choice for representing someone’s language is being made on our platform so they feel good using it.”
For its part, a Google spokesperson tells WIRED it has a long history of bringing lesser-known and Indigenous languages to its platforms so people can communicate, pointing to collaborations to integrate languages like Manx and Māori. Google also says it’s exploring how generative AI can simplify the coding and research required for new languages, but “successful integrations require direct participation from native speakers” for the keyboard to meet the community’s needs.
Hoskin Jr. says that writing in syllabary is seen as a badge of honor for young Cherokee speakers. People type their names in Cherokee on Facebook—that’s empowering. But he sees that progress as vulnerable to broader political rhetoric in the US that pushes a monolithic, English-speaking America, which he says bypasses several chapters, including Native American history.
“The greatest enemy we have right now for saving the Cherokee language is the passage of time and the fragility of human life,” Hoskin Jr. says. “Time is precious to everyone, but particularly precious to us in this mission.”

articles.title: Mechanism’s first Switch 2 case is as awesome as I hoped it would be
articles.text:
Most companies have slowed down releasing new Switch 2 cases, but one of my favorite accessory makers recently debuted its first, after a few delays. The $49 Basecase from Mechanism is a snap-on shell for the console that taps into the company’s modular lineup of mounts. You could already mount the Switch 2 in numerous ways with its $19 Basegrip (to your wall, to its Gaming Pillow, to a monitor arm, etc.). The difference is that this new product protects your console, makes its Joy-Con more comfortable to use, and has some interesting modularity.
Mechanism’s first Switch 2 case is as awesome as I hoped it would be
A $49 case that protects your console and offers customization via modularity.
The console shell allows for the full range of the Switch 2’s kickstand, and access to all of the ports, buttons, and fan vents. Notably, it fits more snugly than others I’ve tried because it clamps on near the console’s bottom USB-C port. This is a good thing. You can unlock its rear plate and replace it with a custom 3D-printed version for more fun and/or more utility. Mechanism sent over a couple of printed examples that hint at the possibilities — one that has Lego pegs on it for sticking on some minifigures, and another that has crannies for game cartridges.
The grips that slide onto the back of the Joy-Con protectors are modular, too. The set includes two sizes that add varying degrees of bulk, both of which make them more comfortable to use. Remove any of the grips, and there’s a spot for a game cartridge. It’s a fun way to bring extra physical games. Mechanism included some extra grip types that aren’t for sale to show what’s possible with a 3D printer. I really liked the pair that has a little shelf on each side to let your middle or ring fingers rest.
You can’t use the Switch 2 in its dock with the Basecase. So, Mechanism includes a dock adapter that takes a different approach — not necessarily better or worse — than Dbrand did with its Killswitch. Instead of cradling the Switch 2, it’s simply a female-to-male USB-C cable that you have to maneuver onto the dock’s video-out port. Installing it isn’t quite as easy as its marketing indicates, but I eventually got it working. Those who use a third-party USB-C dock from Jsaux or Genki won’t need to use this component.
The Basecase seems designed to address multiple points of failure in earlier Switch 2 cases released by Dbrand, Genki, and others that unfortunately let some quality control issues slip in an effort to launch cases first when the Swtich 2 first debuted.
For instance, the Basecase’s Joy-Con grips have a little rubber lip that fits around the top of the controller’s inner colored section. Dbrand revised its comfy Killswitch grip to add this after some users noted their consoles tumbling to the ground when they grabbed it by the controller without supporting the Switch 2’s weight. The Basecase does a good job of preventing this issue.
Also important: the swappable Joy-Con grips attach easily, requiring almost no effort to line up the latch pins to snap on. I could never quite get the feel for the ones included with Genki’s Attack Vector case (we’ll see how Genki’s upcoming Grips fare). Also, while most thin, plastic cases from competitors exhibit ill-fitting sections or flex, the Basecase feels tougher.
If you’re bought into Mechanism’s ecosystem of mounts and have a Switch 2, there’s a good chance that you’ve been waiting for this release (and, perhaps, you already own this case). For gamers who haven’t yet tried out the company’s system of mounts, this is a really good place to start. You can grab all of the 3D printer files at Makerworld or Printables.
Photography by Cameron Faulkner/The Verge

articles.title: The tech behind your car's adaptive cruise control - Engadget
articles.text:
The tech behind your car's adaptive cruise control
A radar sensor and a camera, that’s it.
Somewhere in the world right now, a car that nobody's feet are actively in control of has noticed the truck ahead of it is slowing, and eased off by itself. That's adaptive cruise control. For most of the last three decades, it's a technology that has fundamentally come down to a hidden radar in the car's nose, joined over the last decade or so by a camera behind the rearview mirror.
How it works in a Honda is a pretty typical example: A millimeter-wave radar and a camera measure the gap to the vehicle in front, and how quickly that gap is closing. Meanwhile, the car works the pedals to hold whichever of four following distances you've configured the car to maintain.
But since its introduction in the late '90s, adaptive cruise control has come a long way in terms of the software wrapped around it. Ford's BlueCruise, for example, can slow your car ahead of a bend using map data, while Hyundai's Smart Cruise Control studies how you drive so it can copy you.
How a car can see
This comes down to two sensors. Radar is one, sitting low in the front-end of a car, usually behind the emblem or the grille. It works by bouncing a radio signal off the car ahead and timing the echo, which gives it both a distance and closing speed measurement in the dark or fog. Because of this, a lot of owners can self-sabotage their adaptive cruise control by doing things like adding number-plate frames or stickers, or bumping into objects while parking.
The second sensor, a camera, has a much easier life up behind the windshield. One of its jobs is to monitor lane markings, so the system knows which car is the right one to follow. Honda says that's also how the system knows when somebody inevitably cuts you off. Some automakers supplement these sensors with other systems for a more seamless user experience. Ford's BlueCruise, for example, adds GPS maps, The Drive reported after a ride with Ford's engineers.
The hardware in adaptive cruise control systems peaked a while back. Bosch's long-range radar could already "see" about 250 meters back in 2014, and its successor "sees" 530. The more interesting changes since have been in terms of what a car does with the pictures. Honda's Low Speed Follow, for example, taught it to stop behind a queue and pull away again when you tap a button or the accelerator, making it genuinely useful in a traffic jam.
Rain and heavy traffic are still off limits
Despite the advances made with the tech, it's still only useful in favorable driving conditions. Toyota, for example, says its radar cruise control shouldn't be used in rain, fog or snow, on slippery surfaces, in heavy traffic, on sharp bends or down steep hills. The slippery-surface warnings are there because a computer-held throttle would carry the same speed into standing water, which is how a car hydroplanes, and a downpour blinds the hardware, too; Volvo says that its radar's ability to detect the car in front is reduced significantly during a heavy downpour.
Volvo also tells owners not to use adaptive cruise in dense traffic or at junctions, and admits that its sensor can be late detecting a car that suddenly cuts in close ahead. Honda, meanwhile, tells owners to only use the feature on relatively straight roads that will require little braking.
Other systems, such as Ford's Predictive Speed Assist, cut the set speed before a bend and drops it to a new posted speed limit before you get to the sign, while GM LiDAR-scans the roads its Super Cruise expansion adds 750,000 miles of rural roads to. In 2019, Hyundai built an adaptive cruise control that mimics your driving style via machine learning.
What adaptive cruise control won't do
Volvo, in that same manual, says that adaptive cruise control isn't a collision avoidance system, and that it doesn't brake for people or animals, for small vehicles like bicycles, or for oncoming, slow-moving or stationary vehicles; that includes a car sitting stationary in your lane. The system watches moving traffic, so a vehicle that's already stopped or at the back of a traffic jam might not register, meaning that you keep hurtling at speed toward it.
It's alarming then, that drivers have been found to put the wrong kind of trust in these systems. IIHS and MIT's AgeLab gave 20 volunteers cars for a month, half with adaptive cruise alone and half with cruise plus lane centering. By the end of the study, the lane-centering group was more than three times as likely to be playing around with a phone or the console as in week one, and 17 times as likely to drive with both hands off the wheel as at the start. An earlier IIHS study found that drivers with adaptive cruise switched on were 24%(!) more likely to speed on highways, and sped by higher margins when they did.
All this driving complacency has come from what is, at the end of the day, a simple system that manages a gap and a set speed. With that in mind, it's frankly scary to imagine how bad driving habits might manifest when self-driving cars that promise to handle all the driving become a more frequent sight on the road.

articles.title: Cụm điện gió Savan của T&T Group tại Lào góp thêm nguồn lực cho tăng trưởng
articles.text:
Dự án Nhà máy điện gió Savan 2 dự kiến vận hành vào cuối năm 2028
Theo Quy hoạch điện VIII điều chỉnh, nhu cầu tiêu thụ điện được dự báo tăng 10,5–12,9% mỗi năm trong giai đoạn 2026–2030. Thực tế vận hành năm 2026 cũng cho thấy áp lực ngày càng lớn khi công suất cực đại của hệ thống điện quốc gia đã đạt khoảng 58.500 MW trong đợt nắng nóng cuối tháng 6.
Quy hoạch điện VIII điều chỉnh dự báo đến năm 2030, điện thương phẩm đạt khoảng 500,4–557,8 tỷ kWh, còn công suất cực đại của hệ thống ở mức 89.655–99.934 MW. Quy mô nhu cầu dự kiến này cho thấy yêu cầu đối với ngành điện không chỉ là đáp ứng phụ tải trước mắt, mà còn phải chủ động phát triển nguồn và lưới điện để theo kịp nhu cầu sản xuất, kinh doanh, tiêu dùng ngày càng cao.
Trong bối cảnh đó, nhập khẩu điện từ Lào trở thành một nguồn bổ sung quan trọng. Quy hoạch điện VIII điều chỉnh đặt mục tiêu nhập khẩu khoảng 9.360–12.100 MW vào năm 2030, đồng thời chủ trương tăng tối đa khả năng nhập khẩu điện từ Lào. Triển vọng này càng được củng cố trong khuôn khổ chuyến thăm chính thức Lào của Thủ tướng Việt Nam Lê Minh Hưng đầu tháng 10/2026. Với sự chứng kiến của Thủ tướng hai nước, 17 giấy chứng nhận đầu tư và thỏa thuận hợp tác của doanh nghiệp đã được trao. Trong đó, dự án điện gió Savan 2 do T&T Group tham gia phát triển là một trong những hợp tác lớn nhất, với công suất 495 MW, tổng vốn đầu tư khoảng 768 triệu USD và dự kiến vận hành thương mại chậm nhất vào cuối năm 2028.
Theo thỏa thuận hợp tác liên Chính phủ năm 2026 giữa Việt Nam và Lào, Savan 2 nằm trong nhóm dự án năng lượng được tạo điều kiện triển khai xây dựng và vận hành thương mại phù hợp với pháp luật mỗi nước.
Trước đó, từ cuối năm 2025 T&T Group đã đưa vào vận hành dự án điện gió Savan 1 giai đoạn 1 tại tỉnh Savannakhet của Lào với công suất 300 MW, mỗi năm cung cấp khoảng 0,9 tỷ kWh điện về Việt Nam. Giai đoạn 2 của Savan 1 có công suất 195 MW cũng sẽ được khởi công xây dựng vào cuối năm nay. Như vậy, sau khi Savan 2 được hoàn thành đúng dự kiến vào cuối năm 2028, cả 2 dự án điện gió của T&T Group trên đất bạn Lào sẽ cung cấp về Việt Nam gần 1 GW điện.
Từ nguồn điện xuyên biên giới đến động lực cho tăng trưởng
Điện gió Savan 1 là dự án năng lượng đầu tiên của tập đoàn trên đất bạn Lào. Cùng với nhà máy, T&T Group đã đầu tư hệ thống truyền tải phục vụ Savan 1, trong đó có tuyến đường dây 220 kV dài gần 70 km từ dự án về Trạm biến áp 220 kV Lao Bảo và kết nối với hệ thống điện phía Việt Nam. Toàn bộ quá trình từ hoàn thiện thủ tục, xây dựng nhà máy, đầu tư hạ tầng truyền tải đến kết nối lưới điện được thực hiện trong khoảng 16 tháng.
Hạ tầng và kinh nghiệm đã hình thành từ Savan 1 tạo thêm thuận lợi cho quá trình phát triển Savan 2, nhất là trong tổ chức thi công và kết nối nguồn điện xuyên biên giới. Việc có thể tận dụng một phần hạ tầng truyền tải đã được đầu tư từ Savan 1 cũng giúp Savan 2 có thêm lợi thế về tiến độ và hiệu quả đầu tư, đồng thời cho thấy sự đồng bộ giữa nguồn điện, hệ thống truyền tải và khả năng kết nối với lưới điện Việt Nam.
“Ý nghĩa lớn nhất của Savan 1 và Savan 2 không chỉ nằm ở gần 1.000 MW công suất, mà ở việc hình thành một nguồn bổ sung dài hạn cho hệ thống điện Việt Nam trong thời điểm nhu cầu năng lượng tăng nhanh. Đây là một trong những giải pháp giúp nâng cao khả năng chống chịu của hệ thống trước những biến động về phụ tải, thời tiết và cơ cấu nguồn điện”, đại diện T&T Group chia sẻ.
Khi những dự án này được đưa vào vận hành, tác động không chỉ thể hiện ở lượng điện bổ sung cho hệ thống. Quá trình đầu tư nhà máy, xây dựng hạ tầng truyền tải và tổ chức vận hành kéo theo nhu cầu về xây dựng, vận tải, dịch vụ kỹ thuật, logistics và giao thương dọc hành lang Việt Nam - Lào, đặc biệt tại Savannakhet và các địa phương Bắc Trung Bộ kết nối qua cửa khẩu Lao Bảo. Những hoạt động này góp phần mở rộng việc làm, dịch vụ và lưu chuyển hàng hóa tại khu vực biên giới.
Từ 0,9 tỷ kWh điện mỗi năm của giai đoạn 1 Savan 1 đến gần 500 MW công suất dự kiến của Savan 2, chuỗi dự án tại Savannakhet đang từng bước chuyển nguồn tài nguyên gió của Lào thành nguồn điện phục vụ nhu cầu phát triển của Việt Nam.
Trong giai đoạn Việt Nam đặt mục tiêu tăng trưởng 2 con số, bảo đảm đủ điện không chỉ là yêu cầu của ngành năng lượng mà còn là điều kiện quan trọng đóng góp cho tăng trưởng, trở thành một mắt xích quan trọng trong chiến lược đa dạng hóa nguồn cung, tăng cường an ninh năng lượng và góp thêm một nguồn lực đầu vào cho tăng trưởng trong giai đoạn phát triển mới.
Phương Dung

articles.title: UK to keep testing OpenAI and Anthropic models before release
articles.text:
Britain’s AI Security Institute will keep testing the most powerful AI models before they are released, the UK government said on Monday.
AI minister Kanishka Narayan said the UK had worked closely with the US to keep that access, Bloomberg reported. It reverses a US move that put White House checks first.
“I want Britain to become one of the hardest countries in the world to attack using artificial intelligence,” Narayan said in a speech in London.
What changed
Last month, the White House asked OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models back from UK testers until US officials had checked them. Anthropic did not share its Mythos model with the institute, Bloomberg reported.
The Telegraph first reported the U-turn and said Narayan had lobbied for it. Narayan credited the recent King Charles summit for bringing ministers and tech bosses together.
Pressed on whether the deal would last, he was careful.
“When you’re reliant on someone else’s technology, you have to be clear-eyed about the permanence of any outcome,” Narayan told Bloomberg.
He said he was “very confident” the UK would be able to test the latest models.
A new task force
Narayan also set up a task force to guard UK government systems from AI-driven attacks. He said two pilots had used frontier AI to find more than 1,000 possible weak spots.
Set up in 2023, the institute is the best-funded government body that regularly tests frontier models, according to Bloomberg. Its testers have caught AI agents taking actions they were not asked to take.
The US has its own checks, with Google, Microsoft and xAI agreeing to pre-release reviews.

articles.title: Feds Got Warrants to Use Fake Cell Towers to Hunt Down Don Lemon’s Producer
articles.text:
US law enforcement agents obtained authorization to use a controversial surveillance device capable of intercepting cell phone signals to find and arrest a 21-year-old college student who helped produce journalist Don Lemon’s coverage of an anti-ICE protest, court filings show.
The former student, Jerome Richardson, who has since graduated from Temple University, is among 39 people charged with conspiring to violate worshippers’ civil rights and interfering with religious worship at Cities Church in St. Paul, Minnesota, in January. Protesters said they targeted the church’s January 18 service because one of its pastors, David Easterwood, also led ICE’s St. Paul field office. Those charged include journalists Georgia Fort and Lemon, a former CNN host, who say they were there to cover the demonstration.
Twelve days after the protest, judges in two states began signing warrants authorizing agents to use so-called cell-site simulators, commonly known as Stingrays or IMSI catchers, to target Richardson’s phone: one in Minnesota on January 30 and another in Pennsylvania the next day. The purpose, his lawyers wrote in a motion seeking to exclude the tracking evidence, was “locating and arresting him.”
Agents also applied for cell-site simulator warrants targeting the phones of Fort and Jamael Lundy, then a Minnesota State Senate candidate. They separately sought pen register orders, which can log the numbers a phone contacts, for Fort and a number WIRED traced to Lemon. It's unclear whether a judge approved any of those applications.
The records reviewed by WIRED do not establish whether investigators actually deployed a cell-site simulator to locate Richardson or whether judges approved the applications targeting Fort and Lundy. In a July letter filed in court, Fort’s lawyers said prosecutors “did not know” whether the surveillance applications had been authorized or had yielded evidence.
Cell-site simulators impersonate cell phone towers to locate a target’s phone. In doing so, they can also collect identifying information from any nearby cellular device, including those belonging to people who aren’t suspected of a crime. That indiscriminate collection has made the devices controversial among privacy advocates, who describe them as dragnet surveillance tools.
The use of cell-site simulators has long been shrouded in secrecy. FBI records released in 2023 showed that police borrowing its simulators had to agree to keep details of their use secret, even in court. Privacy advocates have long warned that the devices could be turned against protesters and journalists.
“Using an advanced surveillance capability such as a cell-site simulator against members of the free press for reporting stories that are unfavorable to the president is an appalling attack on the First Amendment,” says Cooper Quintin, senior staff technologist at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a tech-focused civil liberties nonprofit. Quintin has spent years researching the devices and developing tools to help people detect them. Using EFF’s detection software, WIRED found evidence suggesting a cell-site simulator was deployed near the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago, though who operated it and for what purpose remain unknown.
Attorneys for Lemon, Lundy, and Fort did not respond to requests for comment. Richardson’s attorneys declined to comment on the record.
The previously unreported warrants are a product of a campaign of contentious investigative tactics waged by federal agents in pursuit of people connected to the protest at Cities Church. According to court records, the Department of Homeland Security demanded journalists’ telephone and YouTube records under a customs authority that requires no prior judicial approval. Agents also sought records identifying everyone who had purchased a particular beanie at REI in the Minneapolis–St. Paul area over a period of more than two years. Defense attorneys have identified 92 customs summonses and are challenging the government’s authority to issue them.
The cell-site simulator warrants raise serious questions about both the accuracy of the information investigators presented to judges in their effort to obtain authorization for surveillance tool’s use, as well as why they sought such intrusive tracking to find Richardson in the first place.
The affidavits supporting the applications to track Richardson claimed video showed Fort, Lemon, Richardson, and others “chanting with agitators.” Prosecutors have since conceded that Lemon and Fort did not chant. According to her lawyers, the government acknowledged that the false claim appeared in at least 15 warrant affidavits.
DHS policy says cell-site simulators are deployed only “in the fraction of cases in which the capability is best suited to achieve specific public safety objectives,” but it’s unclear what specific public safety reason justified its use in this case. Investigators obtained a second simulator warrant to locate Richardson, then a senior at Temple University, two days before he walked up to a federal courthouse in Philadelphia and voluntarily surrendered. He was released on bond that afternoon.
The Justice Department responded to WIRED’s request for comment by writing in an email that the department “speaks through its court filings.” DHS declined to discuss ongoing investigations or investigative methods and referred questions to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota, which did not respond to a request for comment.
The warrant was signed January 31, the same day Richardson posted a YouTube video saying he expected to enter federal custody “in the coming days,” suggesting he had no intention of fleeing. It is unclear whether the warrant preceded the video, leaving questions about why investigators sought such an intrusive tool to find someone who was publicly anticipating his arrest and whom prosecutors agreed to release the day he surrendered.
While Richardson’s suppression motion asks to suppress evidence obtained from the phone tracking, it does not specify whether agents used a simulator or obtained evidence through either.
A former federal prosecutor who spent a decade working on counterterrorism cases says using a simulator to locate someone is not necessarily unusual. But based on the court records they reviewed about Richardson’s case, they called the government's tactics aggressive: “I don’t understand why it would be at all necessary.” They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak on the record
Richardson, a St. Paul native, had led an NAACP chapter at 16 and served as executive director of Minnesota Teen Activists, according to his fundraiser’s organizer. He described his work for Lemon as handling logistics and connecting him with local contacts. He drove the journalist to Cities Church, where Lemon livestreamed the demonstration and interviewed protesters and churchgoers. Prosecutors allege Richardson joined chants and obstructed congregants.
In his video, Richardson defended his role. “I was proud to support his work,” he said of Lemon. “This is the price of being unapologetic about humanity and love of Christ.”
The government’s initial effort to obtain arrest warrants met resistance from judges. A magistrate judge refused five of eight warrants, and after an appeals court rejected the Justice Department's bid to override that decision, the department withdrew its request. In a filing with the appeals court, the chief judge wrote that two of the five “were not protestors at all; instead, they were a journalist and his producer” and that there was “no evidence that those two engaged in any criminal behavior.” Prosecutors later secured a grand jury indictment on January 29.
The way the government chose to arrest some defendants has also drawn objections from defense lawyers. Lemon’s attorneys say in court filings that prosecutors rejected their offer to arrange his surrender; agents instead arrested him shortly before midnight at a Beverly Hills hotel while he was covering the Grammy Awards. Fort’s lawyers say agents arrested her at home rather than allowing her to turn herself in.
