articles.title: Android is the best and worst thing about Googlebooks
articles.text:
My first week with the new Android-powered laptops has been about as rocky as anyone’s, but I’ve slowly learned to like them, even if love still feels a ways off. Every moment that’s impressed me has been thanks to Android, whether I’ve been accessing a native version of a useful app or quickly checking my phone notifications from the laptop user interface.
Android is the best and worst thing about Googlebooks
As an Android devotee, I want to love Googlebooks — but they don’t make it easy.
Android is the best and worst thing about Googlebooks
As an Android devotee, I want to love Googlebooks — but they don’t make it easy.
But man, sometimes it just sucks.
Phone connectivity is flaky, app casting is awkward, and file-sharing seems to be flat-out broken. And that’s just the interaction between a Googlebook and a phone — I have a whole other set of gripes about the limitations of native Android apps on a $1,000 laptop.
If Googlebooks ever become a success, Android is going to get the credit. But if it all goes wrong, that’s exactly where the blame will lie too. So far, success feels a lot further away than failure.
Getting started
The Googlebook setup process is Android through-and-through. It’s similarly quick, just a few minutes from beginning to end, including time to register biometric logins, log into a Google account, and connect it to a phone to find your apps and backups. There’s a little variation in the exact setup between the Asus and HP models I’ve been testing, but mostly just whether it defaults to installing every app from your phone or only the desktop-optimized ones.
Things get janky once you’re into the OS, though. Even if you use an Android 17 phone to set up the laptop, it’s unlikely to remain connected afterwards for features like file sharing and app casting. Fully pairing either of my Googlebooks to a phone has required toggling cross-device settings on both devices, multiple restarts, and the occasional prayer, until the two devices find each other. Moving to a new Wi-Fi network broke things for me all over again, requiring a restart of the Googlebook to get the devices back talking to each other — and yes, they need to be on the same Wi-Fi network to talk, and to have Bluetooth enabled too, so the connection won’t work when you’re offline.
My Asus Googlebook has now formed a pretty reliable connection to an Oppo phone I’ve been reviewing, though it still refuses to recognize any other phones; my HP model flits between that Oppo and the Vivo X Fold 6, occasionally connecting to both at once. Yesterday, for the first time all week, it connected to my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, after both laptops had stubbornly ignored that phone for days — even though it’s Google’s own hardware.
Going native
I’ve loved elements of the Googlebook experience. It’s great being able to access quick, compact, desktop versions of apps I’d normally be stuck using through a web browser on my MacBook. It’s even better that some of those apps have different functionality for being mobile versions: being able to download series from HBO Max or Netflix and watch them offline means a Googlebook could replace my Android tablet, which is mostly just a device for watching movies on planes at this point.
But many, many more apps are a headache to use on an Android laptop. Some don’t have desktop-optimized versions — the mobile version of Slack is truly unworkable in a desktop environment, and Adobe’s Android apps are pale shadows of their desktop selves. Others claim to be “Optimized for desktop” in the Play Store, but in practice that usually means they’ve stretched the UI to fit a desktop scale and included basic mouse and keyboard support — “basic” being the operative word, with most not recognizing right-clicks or occasionally shifting into a portrait view. “Made for desktop” seems to be the only Play Store tag that really counts for much, and I’ve only seen it on a handful of apps.
Even Google’s own apps are often limited. Chrome is the worst offender, since you’re likely to use it so much. Google insists this is a desktop version of the browser, but it lacks feature parity with other platforms: there’s no support for switching profiles, opening tabs in a split view, or creating custom search engine shortcuts. Those are just the omissions I’ve run into from my daily MacBook workflow, and there are no doubt countless more.
And despite Google’s promise that Chromebooks offer the “entire Play Store library,” that isn’t entirely true. I’ve already run into two apps that I simply can’t install from the Play Store — Bluesky and the login authorization tool Okta. It’s not an Intel issue either, as Google alluded to on Monday: the Arm-based HP Googlebook also won’t run either app.
My laptop needs aren’t complex: I spend 90 percent of my time on my work MacBook Air inside Chrome and Slack, and most of the rest in Photoshop or Lightroom. But all four are subpar on a Googlebook right now, and it’s all because they’re fundamentally Android apps that can’t compete with true desktop alternatives.
Casting confusion
If Android apps on your laptop aren’t enough, Googlebooks also let you cast the Android apps on your phone to your laptop.
Some version of Android app casting or mirroring has been around before on both Windows and Chromebooks. The difference in Google’s implementation is that instead of mirroring the whole phone UI, you cast specific apps, either through a dedicated app drawer in the taskbar or by tapping into a synced notification from your phone. Those apps still run on the phone itself — which gets a notification that an app is casting — but are controlled via the PC.
It’s not well-suited to streaming music or video, or running multiple apps at once, but that doesn’t seem to be the intent anyway. Where casting shines is in quickly dipping into an app without reaching for your phone and unlocking it, like updating a payment in the settlement app Splitwise or sending a quick message in WhatsApp. I’ve really enjoyed being able to dive in and out of a phone task from my laptop, while minimizing the risk of getting distracted by Instagram.
Casting is clever and mostly works well, but I think I’ve found it useful because I’m new to the Googlebook and haven’t set every app up yet. Google argues it’s designed for apps you might want to use from your laptop but wouldn’t want to install there, but that’s a pretty short list, especially given that installing an Android app is generally quick, painless, and a minimal drain on storage. Long-term, I’m not sure how often I’d want to cast a mobile app when I could just install a native version, especially since you can’t copy and paste between native apps and cast versions, or access the Googlebook file system when casting.
Even when the cross-device connection runs smoothly, some apps — especially secure ones like my authorization app or banking app — won’t run. Others try to open but don’t work: my credit card app breaks on bootup, while Bluesky renders text illegibly. Casting some apps even create rendering issues when I next open them back on the actual phone.
The rest is a mess too
Then there are the other problems.
Continue On lets you start a task on your phone and pick it up on the Googlebook. It’s great when it works, but that’s rare. Only a handful of apps are supported, and even those trigger inconsistently. It works when I open a Google Drive document, but only sporadically in Gmail, and so far never for Calendar.
Notifications are powerful, but messy, with phone and laptop notifications mixed together. Phone notifications open via app casting, but the system gets confused easily. For various reasons, right now my Slack notifications open a casted phone app rather than the native Googlebook app; WhatsApp notifications don’t come through even from my phone; and I can either get notifications for my work Gmail account or my personal one, but not both at once.
File transfer is entirely broken. While I can see my phone’s storage as a drive inside the file manager, accessing those files is near-impossible. It can take minutes to load up the file system, and minutes more to open or transfer a single 5MB photo. It’s completely unusable. This should be fixable, at least. Quick Share — Android’s equivalent to AirDrop — is also supported, and the same files that take minutes over file transfer share in seconds with Quick Share.
It’s the Googlebook in a nutshell: the idea is wonderful, the execution entirely lacking. A week in, I’m learning to work around the kinks and headaches of this odd little OS, finding ways to make the most of it and to maximize those moments when my laptop and my phone just work together. When it clicks, it feels like the payoff to a decade and a half of using Android every day.
Right now, that feeling doesn’t hit nearly as often as it needs to, and certainly not enough to make up for the countless times Android just feels broken in this form factor. The question is whether Google — a company with a deserved reputation for giving up when the going gets tough — has the commitment to see this through and turn things around. It’ll need its own teams to fix what’s broken, third-party developers to pledge support en masse, and a rethink of how to integrate native apps with casting from a phone.
When I first saw the Googlebooks a few weeks ago, I really thought one might be my next laptop. After spending a week with them, I’m not so sure. I certainly wouldn’t buy a Googlebook as they are right now, but I wouldn’t rule out an Android laptop in the future — the execution just needs to catch up to the idea.
Photography by Dominic Preston / The Verge

articles.title: What you can do when your Ethernet cable gets stuck - Engadget
articles.text:
What you can do when your Ethernet cable gets stuck
A stuck ethernet cable can be extremely frustrating. Luckily, you can usually remove one pretty easily using these methods.
Frequently, Ethernet cables can be a cheat code to better network performance. This is mostly because they eliminate the range, interference and band congestion issues that Wi-Fi is vulnerable to. Seriously – if you're dealing with unstable streaming or gaming on your PC, just try hooking it up to your router with a Cat6 or Cat7 Ethernet cable.
They do come with some drawbacks. The main one is convenience, since Ethernet starts to become impractical for devices on the opposite side of the room your router is in, let alone the opposite side of your house. Also, even some of the best streaming devices for 2026 still use 100-megabit Ethernet instead of gigabit, actually making them slower than Wi-Fi. It's not clear why companies think they can get away with this in 2026, but we digress.
A small but not insignificant flaw is the connector type that Ethernet uses. It can sometimes get stuck, and if it does, you can't just yank a cable out with brute force. Fortunately, there are a few ways to remove a stuck Ethernet cable. One method involves jiggling it up and down while pulling, and you can also try using a small tool like a flathead screwdriver. If you're still unable to remove the cable, you may need to visit a professional or contact tech support.
How to safely remove stuck Ethernet cables
The reason caution is called for is because the connector is usually made of light plastic and designed to "lock" into a port with the help of a protruding tab. If you pull without thinking, this tab can break, leaving behind debris and preventing the cable from locking in again. There's also a risk of damaging data or power pins. In an extreme scenario, the tab may stay put while the cable's raw wiring strips away.
If an Ethernet cable refuses to budge, your first move (after turning off your device) should be to hold down the tab, then try carefully bending the connector up and down (or vice versa) as you pull. This should hopefully clear the cable from its moorings. If this doesn't work, you may want to try pressing the connector further in before pulling, while continuing to hold down the tab. Either way, keep holding onto the frame of the device your cable is plugged into, since this provides stability and resistance.
What can you do if the cable remains stuck? You might try using a tool like a flathead screwdriver or the tip of a pen to keep the tab as depressed as possible. Exercise caution here, though. While there shouldn't be any damageable pins near the tab, you could accidentally scrape the pins at the bottom if you successfully pull the cable out.
Avoid using pliers. These may help if nothing else is doing the trick, but the amount of pressure needed to clamp and pull risks breaking the connector, which, as we mentioned, is typically made out of light plastic. One half of the pliers will also be dangerously close to those data and power pins.
Is there anything else you can do?
Unfortunately, not really. Ethernet ports don't have emergency ejection buttons of any kind. If you've tried all of the steps above and the cable remains stuck, it's better to leave it in there unless you have no alternate ports or need the cable for something else. Contact tech support for your device, or bring the product to a local repair shop.
To be clear, the threat of a stuck Ethernet cable is pretty minimal. They're actually designed for easy removal, and it's possible to go your entire life without encountering this issue. But since it does happen in the real world, it's better to be prepared.
If you want to avoid trouble, it may actually be wiser to stick to Wi-Fi. With Wi-Fi 6 and Wi-Fi 7, it's now possible to achieve the same gigabit speeds as Ethernet, sometimes even faster. Range and interference barriers may not be as easy (or cheap) to solve, but you'll likely need to deal with those anyway, given how many products lack Ethernet as an option. There's no room for a jack on a smart bulb.

articles.title: 8 tỷ phú USD Việt: Từ tuyên bố đầy tham vọng đến các trụ cột kinh tế tư nhân
articles.text:
Tài sản tỷ USD và khát vọng đưa tập đoàn ra thế giới
Đằng sau sự vươn mình của kinh tế Việt Nam trong thập kỷ qua là dấu ấn của những doanh nhân dám theo đuổi các mục tiêu vượt xa giới hạn thị trường trong nước. Không ít tuyên bố ban đầu bị hoài nghi, nhưng qua thời gian, đã trở thành kim chỉ nam cho hành trình xây dựng những tập đoàn quy mô lớn.
Năm 2014, tỷ phú Phạm Nhật Vượng chia sẻ mong muốn những con phố Hà Nội và TP.HCM sầm uất như Hồng Kông (Trung Quốc) hay Singapore, đồng thời nhấn mạnh việc để lại giá trị cho thế hệ sau.
Trong hơn một thập kỷ qua, Vingroup và Vinhomes đã phát triển nhiều khu đô thị lớn như Vinhomes Riverside, Ocean Park, Smart City và Grand Park, kết hợp nhà ở với tiện ích, thương mại và dịch vụ.
Bên cạnh bất động sản, ông Phạm Nhật Vượng mở rộng hoạt động sang lĩnh vực sản xuất ô tô. Tại lễ khởi công tổ hợp VinFast ở Hải Phòng năm 2017, ông nêu mục tiêu đưa thương hiệu ô tô Việt Nam ra thị trường quốc tế.
VinFast sau đó chuyển sang sản xuất ô tô điện, mở rộng hoạt động ra nước ngoài và đầu tư cơ sở sản xuất tại Ấn Độ, Indonesia. Quá trình này vẫn đặt ra nhiều thách thức về cạnh tranh và hiệu quả kinh doanh.
Với tỷ phú Nguyễn Thị Phương Thảo, triết lý xây dựng Vietjet cũng bắt đầu từ một mục tiêu vượt ra ngoài hoạt động bán vé máy bay: mang cơ hội bay đến hàng triệu người chưa từng được đi máy bay.
Vietjet khai thác thương mại từ năm 2011, góp phần phổ biến mô hình hàng không giá rẻ tại Việt Nam. Hãng mở rộng mạng đường bay trong nước và quốc tế, phát triển đội tàu bay và xây dựng thương hiệu vượt ra ngoài thị trường nội địa. Từ một ý tưởng từng đối mặt với không ít hoài nghi, hàng không giá rẻ đã trở thành một phần quan trọng của thị trường vận tải hàng không Việt Nam.
Trong lĩnh vực công nghiệp nặng, Chủ tịch Hòa Phát Trần Đình Long từng khẳng định: “Hòa Phát sẽ làm những việc người khác không làm được”. Tập đoàn đã kiên trì đầu tư vào ngành thép, phát triển các khu liên hợp sản xuất quy mô lớn tại Dung Quất và vươn lên vị trí dẫn đầu thị trường thép xây dựng trong nước.
Việc chuẩn bị sản xuất thép đường ray phục vụ các dự án đường sắt quy mô lớn cho thấy Hòa Phát đang tìm cách tiến lên những phân khúc có yêu cầu kỹ thuật và giá trị gia tăng cao hơn, thay vì chỉ tập trung vào các sản phẩm thép truyền thống.
Ở lĩnh vực tiêu dùng, tỷ phú Nguyễn Đăng Quang từng đặt tham vọng mỗi gia đình Việt Nam có ít nhất một sản phẩm Masan trong căn bếp. Với các thương hiệu thực phẩm, gia vị và hệ thống bán lẻ, Masan đã xây dựng được sự hiện diện rộng rãi trong đời sống tiêu dùng. Đây là ví dụ về cách một doanh nghiệp tư nhân có thể phát triển từ sản phẩm thiết yếu thành hệ sinh thái tiêu dùng quy mô lớn.
Trong khi đó, các tỷ phú Hồ Hùng Anh và Ngô Chí Dũng lần lượt gây dựng Techcombank và VPBank thành những ngân hàng tư nhân có quy mô đáng kể, đóng vai trò quan trọng trong cung ứng vốn, dịch vụ tài chính và chuyển đổi số ngành ngân hàng.
Tám tỷ phú USD gồm ông Phạm Nhật Vượng, bà Nguyễn Thị Phương Thảo, bà Phạm Thu Hương (vợ ông Vượng), bà Phạm Thúy Hằng (em vợ ông Vượng), ông Trần Đình Long, ông Hồ Hùng Anh, ông Ngô Chí Dũng và ông Nguyễn Đăng Quang hoạt động trong nhiều lĩnh vực, từ bất động sản, công nghiệp, hàng không đến ngân hàng, tiêu dùng và công nghệ.
Tính đến ngày 11/10/2026, ông Phạm Nhật Vượng có tài sản 35,2 tỷ USD, đứng thứ 66 thế giới và là người giàu nhất Việt Nam. Bà Phạm Thu Hương có tài sản 4 tỷ USD, xếp thứ 1.067 thế giới; bà Phạm Thúy Hằng có tài sản 2,8 tỷ USD.
Cùng với tài sản cá nhân, các doanh nghiệp gắn với những doanh nhân này cũng mở rộng quy mô. Đến cuối tháng 6/2026, tổng tài sản của Vingroup đạt hơn 1,3 triệu tỷ đồng, Hòa Phát gần 279.000 tỷ đồng và Techcombank gần 1,3 triệu tỷ đồng.
Nguồn lực tích lũy tạo nền tảng để doanh nghiệp theo đuổi những mục tiêu lớn hơn. Trong bối cảnh đó, các tuyên bố từng gây tranh luận cũng phần nào phản ánh định hướng chiến lược và mức độ chấp nhận rủi ro của người lãnh đạo.
Kỳ vọng vươn tầm thế giới
Tuy nhiên, thành công tại thị trường Việt Nam chưa đồng nghĩa với sức mạnh cạnh tranh toàn cầu. Xét trên quy mô doanh thu, công nghệ, năng suất, thương hiệu quốc tế và vị trí trong chuỗi giá trị, phần lớn tập đoàn tư nhân Việt Nam vẫn còn khoảng cách đáng kể so với những tập đoàn hàng đầu châu Á và thế giới.
VinFast đang theo đuổi cuộc cạnh tranh khốc liệt trong ngành xe điện, nơi các hãng Trung Quốc, Mỹ, Hàn Quốc và châu Âu sở hữu lợi thế về quy mô, công nghệ, chuỗi cung ứng và kinh nghiệm sản xuất. Hòa Phát có vị thế lớn trong nước và đã mở rộng xuất khẩu, nhưng để trở thành một trung tâm công nghiệp thép có sức ảnh hưởng toàn cầu, doanh nghiệp vẫn cần nâng cao năng lực công nghệ, chất lượng sản phẩm và khả năng tham gia các chuỗi cung ứng giá trị cao.
Trong lĩnh vực công nghệ, FPT đã có bước tiến từ gia công phần mềm sang dịch vụ công nghệ, chuyển đổi số, trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) và những hoạt động ban đầu trong lĩnh vực bán dẫn. Dù vậy, doanh nghiệp Việt Nam vẫn chưa có vị trí tương xứng trên bản đồ thế giới ở những khâu công nghệ cốt lõi như thiết kế chip tiên tiến, sản xuất bán dẫn quy mô lớn hay phát triển các nền tảng AI hàng đầu.
Đây chính là thách thức và cũng là cơ hội của thập kỷ tới.
AI, điện toán đám mây, bán dẫn, vật liệu tiên tiến, năng lượng xanh và robot đang định hình lại nền kinh tế thế giới. Những lĩnh vực này đòi hỏi vốn đầu tư lớn, nguồn nhân lực chất lượng cao, năng lực nghiên cứu dài hạn và hệ sinh thái công nghiệp đồng bộ. Không phải doanh nghiệp nào cũng đủ sức tham gia, nhưng các tập đoàn đã tích lũy được nguồn lực đáng kể có lợi thế nhất định để mở rộng sang những lĩnh vực mới.
Vingroup đang mở rộng sự quan tâm và đầu tư sang công nghiệp, năng lượng, pin và công nghệ robot. FPT theo đuổi AI, bán dẫn và hạ tầng số. Hòa Phát tìm cách nâng cấp năng lực sản xuất thép. Các ngân hàng tư nhân đẩy mạnh số hóa, phát triển dịch vụ tài chính dựa trên dữ liệu, trong khi Masan có cơ hội ứng dụng công nghệ để tối ưu chuỗi cung ứng và bán lẻ.
Nhưng vốn lớn và tham vọng chưa đủ để bảo đảm thành công. Những cuộc đua công nghệ đòi hỏi doanh nghiệp phải lựa chọn đúng lĩnh vực có lợi thế, đầu tư có kỷ luật, xây dựng đội ngũ nghiên cứu, bảo vệ dòng tiền và kiên trì theo đuổi hiệu quả dài hạn. Việc mở rộng sang ngành mới cần đi cùng năng lực thực chất, thay vì chỉ chạy theo những xu hướng đang thu hút sự chú ý.
Vai trò của Nhà nước cũng rất quan trọng. Chính sách phát triển khoa học công nghệ, đào tạo nhân lực, bảo vệ quyền sở hữu trí tuệ, xây dựng hạ tầng và tạo môi trường cạnh tranh bình đẳng có thể giúp doanh nghiệp giảm chi phí, tăng khả năng đổi mới sáng tạo. Sự phối hợp giữa nguồn lực tư nhân và chính sách công sẽ quyết định khả năng hình thành những tập đoàn đủ sức cạnh tranh quốc tế.
Kinh nghiệm của Hàn Quốc cho thấy các tập đoàn lớn có thể trở thành đầu tàu công nghiệp hóa, nhưng sức mạnh của họ chỉ thực sự đóng góp lâu dài khi gắn với năng suất, xuất khẩu, đổi mới công nghệ và sự phát triển của mạng lưới doanh nghiệp phụ trợ trong nước.
Với Việt Nam, kỳ vọng không đơn thuần là xuất hiện thêm những tỷ phú USD hay những tập đoàn có vốn hóa lớn. Điều quan trọng hơn là các doanh nghiệp này có thể tạo ra sản phẩm công nghệ do người Việt làm chủ, nâng cao giá trị gia tăng trong nước, tạo việc làm chất lượng cao và giúp doanh nghiệp Việt tham gia sâu hơn vào chuỗi cung ứng toàn cầu.
Những tuyên bố từng thể hiện rất tham vọng, thậm chí bị nghi ngờ của các doanh nhân có thể là điểm khởi đầu cho những hành trình lớn.
Nhưng thước đo cuối cùng không phải quy mô tài sản của người sáng lập, mà là năng lực cạnh tranh quốc tế của doanh nghiệp và những giá trị bền vững mà doanh nghiệp tạo ra cho xã hội.
Việt Nam đã có những doanh nghiệp đủ lớn để nuôi dưỡng khát vọng vươn tầm. Chặng đường phía trước là biến nguồn lực tích lũy thành năng lực công nghệ, biến tham vọng thành sản phẩm có sức cạnh tranh toàn cầu và biến thành công của một số tập đoàn thành động lực thịnh vượng cho đông đảo người dân.

articles.title: Can My DNA Tell Me How to Exercise? I Tried AlterMe to Find Out
articles.text:
Easy-to-follow workouts based on my DNA and readiness score. Variety of chill yoga or breathwork sessions plus more intense strength, dance, and cardio workouts. The app tracks nutrition and sleep and analyzes meals.
TIRED
Workouts are short—ranging from five to 40 minutes. DNA results are interesting, but there’s no quick fix to fitness. Premium price.
When I was asked to review AlterMe’s fitness system that claims to use DNA and biometric data to create a personalized fitness, nutrition, and recovery program, I was intrigued. I’ve used some of the best fitness trackers before, but have never tried a system that combines DNA testing, personalized workouts, nutrition insight, and its own smart wearable all within a single ecosystem.
I’m someone who needs constant fitness motivation to stay on track. Rather than push myself through strenuous weights and cardio, I prefer feel-good Pilates and an ice bath at my local David Lloyd gym. But in an effort to step out of my comfort zone and try something a little more challenging, I decided to give AlterMe a go.
I’ve used numerous fitness apps over the years, such as Bala and Freeletics, but not one that suggests specific fitness workouts based on my DNA testing results. AlterMe combines guidance across exercise, nutrition, sleep, and recovery, going beyond simply reporting on your DNA and biometric data to suggest small, manageable actions to drive behavioral change over time.
There’s no denying that it comes at a premium price, but having workouts and nutrition guidance in one place helped me build better habits—even if the DNA insights weren’t particularly revelatory.
Getting Set Up
Photograph: Emily Peck
AlterMe’s all-in-one health and fitness program is built around a DNA test and a smart ring that measures data and provides insights and workouts in the app. It’s convenient, but this is an expensive offering. The entry-level AlterMe Essential plan is $1,299, and the AlterMe Advanced plan is $1,899. Both offer biometric tracking, nutrition insights, and fitness workouts accessible from the app, but the Advanced plan gives you a more in-depth DNA analysis and lifetime membership as opposed to the Essential’s three-year membership.
Upon signing up and answering questions on my weight-loss goals, height, weight, and general fitness levels, I was sent both a DNA cheek-swab kit and a ring sizing kit. I emailed AlterMe to confirm my ring size and sent the DNA swab back in the mail. Within two weeks, I received my AlterMe smart ring and had booked in a date to talk over my Fitness and Wellness Genetic report with an AlterMe representative. I’ve been diving in and out of the app and following the fitness workouts for over six months now.
A Tailored Fitness and Wellness Genetic Report
AlterMe app via Emily Peck
Research into genetic influence on athletic performance is still developing, and AlterMe acknowledges that its genetic findings reported through DNA testing have not been clinically validated. However, the company conducts its own research to produce a personalized Fitness and Wellness Genetic Report. It says it uses “a rigorous genetic interpretation process that adheres to strict scientific standards” with “scientific integrity” and “robust research.” AlterMe also states that saliva samples are processed in the US in a CLIA- and CAP-certified lab that meets local regulations.
With this in mind, I approached the DNA test report with equal measures of skepticism and intrigue, as should anyone curious to get more insight into their health and well-being.
The report claimed to use my DNA to reveal how my body responds to different types of exercise, nutrition, recovery, and stress. It suggested types of exercise to suit me and how I could approach training and recovery. Strength training, for example, was identified as the best fit for my genetic profile, while my genetic response to carbohydrates was rated as “lower than average.”
Perhaps not surprisingly, the report told me that I’m “externally motivated to exercise,” suggesting I may not naturally enjoy physical activity just for the sake of it. That certainly felt familiar.
Representatives at AlterMe explained how these assessments are determined: “Our assessment looks at markers associated with several traits, including how body composition changed during exercise interventions. For cardio-related body composition response, the markers in our scientific review are ADRB2 rs1042713 and LPL rs328. For resistance training, the model draws on a set of obesity and body composition markers, including variants near FTO, GNPDA2, NEGR1, and SLC39A8.”
So far, everything was sounding on point. But despite the personalized insights, I hadn’t discovered anything particularly groundbreaking.
Smart Ring Bling
Photograph: Emily Peck
AlterMe has its own smart ring wearable, designed to provide health insights and work alongside the app. The ring uses PPG sensors to monitor metrics such as heart rate and blood oxygen, alongside a temperature sensor and an accelerometer to track activity. It then uses data including my HRV, resting heart rate, sleep, and recent activity load to turn the raw measurements into a “Readiness score” from 0 to 100, before suggesting a workout tailored to my current state and my DNA insight.
This type of health tracking is similar to what you get with Oura's Ring 5 offering. The key difference is that AlterMe is a more closed ecosystem, combining its wearable data with its own genetic insights to generate an AI-powered workout plan every day based on my biometrics.
Oura, meanwhile, provides detailed sleep, activity, readiness, and broader health insights as well as guided fitness content within its app and integration with services such as Apple Health. Its primary focus, however, remains tracking and interpreting your health and activity data, whereas AlterMe puts more emphasis on the personalized workouts it prescribes.
The ring has a titanium outer frame and comes in either a gold finish, silver, or Stealth black. My gold finish has picked up some scuff marks over the couple of months I’ve been wearing it. While the gold finish looks good, I found the ring quite bulky—and thicker than the sleek Oura Ring 5—which means it sometimes gets in the way when I’m lifting weights.
Tailored Workouts Depending on ‘Readiness’ Score
Within the stats section of the app, I was able to view my daily calorie burn, step count, distance covered, sleep duration, and readiness score—all data the ring was providing. The app then provides a daily workout to follow. The workouts can be as low-key or as challenging as I want, depending on how I am feeling. I could choose from stretch, strength, cardio, yoga, or combat-style sessions, so there’s no excuse to skip a workout. As AlterMe representatives told me, the biometric data collected can help make a recommendation, but it can’t capture every detail about how I feel—soreness, illness, stress, injury, or demands of the day may change what feels right, for example—which is why you get the option to choose your level.
“Giving you a choice is also an intentional part of the AlterMe experience,” say AlterMe representatives. “Without choice, it’s hard for you to stay consistent. We want to offer useful guidance while leaving you in control of your effort. Your choice adds context and makes the plan easier to fit into real life.”
On the days I had poor sleep the night before, the app recommended a lighter workout or recovery session—the 15-minute breathwork session has become a particular favorite. On the days I’d slept well, I was tasked with a more strenuous session depending on my current level, from beginner to level 6.
While the workouts are easy to access and follow, I found them short—20 minutes was the average workout time, with 40 minutes being the longest session I tried. But it is possible to stack the workouts if you want to push yourself further. There’s also a way to track activities such as a run or group workout outside the guided library of workouts.
I trust that the app was recommending workouts to suit my health stats and genetic traits, and I mostly felt good when following them. But there were some days when I was feeling terrible due to poor sleep, and the app was telling me that my readiness score was high, which left me feeling a little confused. But I dutifully obliged with the suggested workout—even if I did opt for a shorter 20-minute session. On the days I had forgotten to wear my ring to bed the night before, the app would ask me to self-score from 1 to 10 on how I was feeling before a workout was suggested.
AI Nutrition Coach and Body Scanning
Exercise is just one piece of the fitness puzzle, and one of the pros of the AlterMe app is that it has a nutrition tracker. Rather than having it provide a single diet plan, I like the way the app can generate meal and snack ideas by referencing my DNA to keep me hitting my macro targets. You can generate a recipe and then log it if you decide to make it. Simply by clicking “generate recipe” I could get breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snack ideas in under 20 seconds. The recipes are pretty enticing too—Zesty Lemon Herb Grilled Chicken Qith Roasted Green Beans and Quinoa was one I tried. But I found the snack ideas most helpful, as I’m always thinking about snacks—Roasted Edamame With Smoked Paprika and Sea Salt is a particular favorite.
In the Nutrition tab of the app, I could access personalized calorie and nutrition guidance based on my DNA results, weight, BMI, activity level, and weight-loss goals. My DNA report suggested I have an average response to protein and a low response to carbs and fats. I like how easy it is to log food in the Nutrition tab in the app and instantly see whether I’d hit my protein, fat, and carb macro goals. I often forgot to track everything I ate, but on the days I remembered to do so, I found it easy to track my calorie intake and meals.
AlterMe app via Emily Peck
The app also has a 3D/body composition scanning feature to analyze body shape and provide stats on things like BMI, estimated body-fat percentage, and lean mass.
You do need to put in your height and weight when you sign up, but this feature adds more. As AlterMe told me, BMI is calculated from height and weight, but the scan provides a much fuller view by creating a standardized 3D model and estimating body-fat percentage, lean mass, body shape, and body part circumferences. Repeated scans help show whether and where the body is changing, giving members a clearer way to compare their progress with their goals. You need to use your phone camera to capture a picture of your body shape, but turning as it takes photos. I found this feature a little intrusive, as I didn’t really want to take photos of myself to put on the app. But if this doesn’t bother you, I think this is a compelling extra.
Is the AlterMe App Worth It?
There are numerous workout apps and wearables that can track your health data, but this personalized program that combines DNA testing, a smart ring wearable, and on-demand workouts in one ecosystem is a unique offering. It’s convenient, but pricey, and it's important to note that while the DNA testing can be insightful, it hasn’t been clinically validated. There are also understandable privacy concerns around handing over DNA data, although AlterMe notes on its site that it destroys samples after testing and extracted DNA is retained for just 45 days for quality assurance.
My journey with AlterMe has generally been positive, but it hasn’t altered me. It has made me more aware of what I eat and made me feel physically stronger due to the regularity of my training sessions. I like wearing the ring and having an app that suggests an optimum workout based on my biometrics. Having a tailored workout to follow has made me feel good—particularly on the days that I haven’t felt like training. When I feel stuck in the gym and not sure which exercises to do, I take out the app and simply follow a workout. It makes me feel like I have a personal trainer in my pocket, ready to bark orders at me whenever I need a little push. I think if you’re willing to follow the workouts and track your nutrition, AlterMe can be a helpful tool for building positive habits and improving fitness. You could, alternatively, use the money and invest in a good personal trainer—whatever you decide, it’s always nice to have options.

articles.title: Britain steps up its defences against AI risks
articles.text:
The UK government will extend a programme using frontier AI models to find vulnerabilities in its own systems, and will consider legislating on AI incident reporting and loss-of-control risk. The pilot behind it found 407 weaknesses across nine government organisations in a month for £13,000 in tokens.
Britain will expand a programme that points frontier AI models at the government’s own code to find flaws. It will also look at legislating for AI incident reporting and for systems that escape human oversight.
The package came on Monday from the Cabinet Office, the AI Security Institute, the National Cyber Security Centre and the culture department, according to the announcement.
Kanishka Narayan, who in July became the first AI minister to attend cabinet, set it out at Imperial College London. He wants Britain to be “one of the hardest countries in the world to attack using artificial intelligence“.
The government says two pilots have found and fixed more than a thousand potential vulnerabilities. The case study it cites gives a smaller figure, because it documents only one of them.
That pilot produced 407 findings across nine government organisations over a month of weekly hackathons, at a cost of £13,000 in tokens.
Teams chose their own methods. One built a six-stage agent pipeline in which each stage challenges the last, another layered model stages over conventional scanners, and a third distilled an audit of hundreds of services into five Claude Skills.
The worst finding sat in legacy GitHub Actions on a repository behind a key government service. A crafted comment on an open pull request could run arbitrary code on the build machine and reach its secrets.
The warnings come from the government too. Agents produced candidate findings faster than people could check them, and the case study notes that “finding isn’t the same as fixing“.
Narayan had a message for the labs as well, that a company unable to control a system’s risks should not release it. In September, though, the White House asked OpenAI and Anthropic to withhold new models from the AI Security Institute.
Anthropic held back Mythos 5.1. Britain is urging restraint on labs whose newest systems its own institute cannot reliably see.
The institute is still evaluating the current generation. In July it found that every model tested for the behaviour tried to cheat, and that one attacked its evaluation systems.
Ministers will also explore strengthening the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill so hospitals and utilities are covered against AI risk, including loss of control, and how near misses get reported.
The next phase moves from public repositories into closed government systems. AI will also sit at the centre of Britain’s G20 presidency next year.

articles.title: How is Microsoft's Magnetic Connect different from Apple's MagSafe for MacBooks? - Engadget
articles.text:
How is Microsoft's Magnetic Connect different from Apple's MagSafe for MacBooks?
Microsoft is pretty excited about its new charger.
While Microsoft's October press event was heavily AI-oriented — to the shock of no one — the company did have major announcements regarding the Surface Laptop Ultra. It's powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform, and sports up to 128GB of shared system and graphics RAM. In a demonstration, Microsoft showed it running apps like DaVinci Resolve and Gears of War: E-Day simultaneously without missing a heartbeat.
One smaller point that captured our attention was a new power port dubbed Magnetic Connect. Charging tech isn't normally a big deal, yet Microsoft devoted a portion of the show to it. That's remarkable when the company could've easily spent a few more minutes elaborating on Spark or Windows 11's AI upgrades.
For Apple fans, the tech was immediately reminiscent of one thing: the MagSafe charging ports on MacBooks. There are a couple of important differences, though, and we wouldn't be surprised if Apple changes course to copy Microsoft. That would be an interesting reversal.
Fixing MagSafe's problems for future PCs
The major difference is that whereas MagSafe is a proprietary port — in the unfortunate tradition of other Apple formats, like Lightning — Magnetic Connect really isn't. It's just a Power Delivery-equipped USB-C port paired with a custom magnetic charging cable. The cable's connector aligns with the port automatically and uses a special funnel-shaped tip to slide in smoothly. No jokes, please.
Why does this matter? As Microsoft notes, it means that the port can be used for other functions when you're not charging. You can hook up an external monitor, a keyboard, your smartphone or any other peripheral you can think of. Laptops tend to have very few ports to begin with, so it's a welcome change to get a magnetic power hookup without sacrificing valuable real estate. Beyond Magnetic Connect, the Surface Laptop Ultra has two additional USB-C ports, plus HDMI, USB-A, an SD card reader and a 3.5mm headphone jack.
Significantly, Microsoft seems open to the idea of other companies adopting the technology. At the event, it said that it's hoping to lead the ecosystem, even if it didn't explicitly mention anything about licensing Magnetic Connect to other manufacturers. Doing that would likely be beneficial, since while Surface devices would no longer be special, owners would also have access to a wider variety of accessories that they could use interchangeably. Presumably, no one's buying the Ultra just for its charging options.
One big problem with MagSafe, in fact, is that while third-party cables are available, those are unlicensed. The only sanctioned and fully reliable ones come from Apple, which charges $49 apiece. Since Magnetic Connect is just a combination of USB-C and magnets, even knockoff products are likely to function just fine.
Is magnetic power really a game changer?
Yes and no. The reason Apple, Microsoft and others are interested in magnets is that, without them, there's a risk of tripping on a charging cable and sending your laptop hurtling to the floor. It's also mildly more convenient, since there's no effort wasted trying to align anything. That's it — there's no wireless transmission involved, and it's not as if you can't plug non-magnetic charging gear into the Ultra.
If Magnetic Connect does gain traction beyond Microsoft, it's liable to improve laptop design across the board by freeing up that port space we mentioned. Apple would be hard-pressed to look the other way, especially given that one of the reasons it finally adopted USB-C on iPhones was compliance with European Union regulations on mobile charging tech.
Don't expect Magnetic Connect to become a truly universal standard, as USB Power Delivery tops out at 240W. That's plenty for most laptops, but some gaming models require even more power to support the high-end CPUs and GPUs they're equipped with. That means both custom ports and giant charging bricks.

articles.title: No Man’s Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
articles.text:
The No Man’s Sky universe is about to get a little bit smaller — but in a good way. Hello Games announced that its long-running sci-fi exploration game will be coming to iOS, with versions for both the iPhone and iPad available starting on October 28th.
No Man’s Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
A decade later, and the No Man’s Sky updates just keep coming.
According to Hello’s Sean Murray, the mobile version of the game is essentially the full No Man’s Sky experience. “I guess I should say this is not No Man’s Sky Lite,” he wrote in a blog post. It includes all of the game’s many, many updates that have come out since launch — like the gigantic Voyagers expansion from last year — and the only major features missing will be multiplayer and the planetary settlements. Murray likens the iOS version to when the game initially launched on the original Switch. “On Switch we have listened to players and built from there, including with a much expanded version on Switch 2,” he says. “Based on feedback and player numbers we will support iOS in a similar way.”
The game will be playable on the iPhone 11 and 3rd generation iPad Air and above, and the studio says that the download comes in at a surprisingly scant 5GB. It also has newly-designed touch controls, as well as support for controllers, screen casting, and mouse-and-keyboard on the iPad. Murray also notes that “Perhaps most importantly we’ve put tons of work into battery life and thermodynamics, and we’re super proud that No Man’s Sky can be enjoyed for really long comfortable play sessions.” It’ll be “free to try” at launch, though it’s not clear how much the full version will cost.
It’s now been a decade since No Man’s Sky first launched, and the game has changed dramatically since its debut. iOS will be joining a huge list of supported platforms, including Mac, PC, and essentially every modern console, and there’s also a VR version available. Just as significant, Hello has continued to keep the game vibrant with a constant stream of free expansions, including the recent Cosmos update in September, which fleshed out the vast expanse of space with more things to explore.

articles.title: IonQ to buy cybersecurity firm Elisity for up to $1.3bn
articles.text:
The Maryland-based quantum computing company announced the deal on Monday. IonQ wants its security arm to guard against attacks aided by AI and, one day, quantum machines.
What Elisity does
Founded in 2019, Elisity makes software that stops attackers and ransomware from moving through a company’s network. Hospitals and healthcare firms are among its main customers.
IonQ says Elisity has more than 100 customers using its tools, including a growing number of Fortune 500 firms. It says sales and the customer base doubled in a year, and none of those customers left.
Boss James Winebrenner will keep running the business. The deal should close by the end of the year, once regulators sign off.
“We will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era,” IonQ chief executive Niccolo de Masi said.
“Our customers need to prioritize post-quantum cryptography initiatives while securing existing assets,” Winebrenner said.
A run of deals
IonQ is the biggest listed firm that only does quantum. It is worth about $16bn. It bought chipmaker SkyWater for $1.8bn in January and UK startup Oxford Ionics for $1.1bn last year.
Its security arm already sells tools built to resist quantum attacks. It has built quantum-safe national networks in Switzerland, Poland, Romania and Slovakia. Future quantum machines could crack the codes that protect data online today.
Rivals are raising money on the stock market too. France’s Pasqal listed via a SPAC. IonQ is also among the firms in DARPA’s final test stage for useful quantum computers.

articles.title: A New Anti-Aging Drug Looks to Turn Back the Clock on Skin Age
articles.text:
A wave of biotech companies is looking to prove that it’s possible to slow down the aging process. Mountain View, California–based Rubedo Life Sciences is starting with the most outwardly visible sign: the skin.
The company’s experimental treatment is showing early promise that it may be able to reduce the appearance of aging, according to data the company presented at the Aging Research and Drug Discovery meeting in Boston earlier this month.
In a small clinical trial, Rubedo tested its topical cream on 11 people with atopic dermatitis, an inflammatory skin condition and the most common type of eczema. The drug targets a mechanism of cellular senescence, a biological state in which damaged or stressed cells permanently stop dividing but do not die. These senescent or “zombie” cells accumulate as people age and can release substances that contribute to inflammation and tissue damage, which contributes to disease.
After four weeks of using the cream, participants lowered the biological age of their skin by about two years, on average. That estimate was based on an aging “clock” designed by a different company, Mitra Bio, which performed an independent analysis on participants’ skin samples. One person in the trial had a reduction of more than 11 years in skin age. Separately, Rubedo found that its treatment was tied to a reduction in inflammation-related markers and a 10 percent increase in a type of collagen associated with skin elasticity and structure.
Biological or epigenetic age is an estimate of how well a person is aging compared to their calendar age. Aging clocks like Mitra’s attempt to calculate this number by looking at patterns of methylations, chemical modifications to DNA that regulate how genes function and can change over time. That metric doesn’t necessarily prove that the body or a particular organ or tissue has become functionally younger, though.
“Our idea is to find ways to change the trajectory of how we age,” says Marco Quarta, Rubedo’s cofounder and chief scientific officer. “Aging is complex. There are many mechanisms, but cellular senescence is one of them.”
Senescent cells are also involved in normal biological processes, such as wound healing and tumor suppression, but their accumulation over time is associated with many age-related conditions. Getting rid of them is one of the leading strategies that anti-aging and longevity companies are pursuing.
Rubedo’s approach aims to clear out senescent cells by targeting a protein known as GPX4, a gatekeeper for cell survival. By transiently turning off GPX4, the drug is designed to make senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis, a regulated form of cell death, while reviving stressed, non-senescent cells nearby.
In a separate study, researchers looked at the drug’s effect on actinic keratosis, a skin condition caused by sun damage and produces rough, scaly skin patches and can sometimes progress to skin cancer. In a trial of 18 people, the cream led to a 46 percent reduction in total lesions after a month of use.
Rubedo is studying the same drug for psoriasis and skin with sun damage. Soon, the company will add androgenetic alopecia, a type of hereditary hair loss, to the list. CEO Frederick Beddingfield, previously the chief medical officer at Allergan, where he launched Botox, sees potential in a lower-potency, over-the-counter version for general skin aging, which would compete with retinol. The company is also formulating the drug into a pill to study whether it can be used to treat metabolic conditions associated with aging.
“It's great to see them doing this work,” says Eric Verdin, president and CEO of the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, which has developed several aging clocks. “I would probably be a little circumspect about what these clocks really measure, because right now, there are a proliferation of them.”
Plus, the results that patients will care about is how their skin actually looks and feels, not a result from a biological aging test.
And senescence is just one piece of the aging puzzle, says Anthony Rossi, a dermatologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. “Some senescent cells are good because they turn things off, like cancer progression.”
He says the science is novel but the work is still very early-stage, and it will be interesting to see how it affects biological aging in people with healthy skin, not just those with certain skin conditions. “The best anti-aging routine right now is sleep, a good diet, and exercise,” he says. For now, at least.

articles.title: WhatsApp users may soon be able to schedule messages - Engadget
articles.text:
WhatsApp users may soon be able to schedule messages
Set recurring reminders, manage time zones and handle business communications off-hours.
WhatsApp users have long requested message scheduling to do things like set recurring reminders, manage time zones and handle business communications off-hours. The lack of such a feature is notable since it's been available on rival Telegram's app since 2019. Now, it looks like Meta's messaging app will get that feature soon, according to a WhatsApp Android beta spotted by WaBetaInfo.
The new feature appeared in the WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.8.11 update. It works just as it does in Telegram: users access the feature by tapping and holding the send button. That opens up a dialog at the bottom of the screen, letting you choose the delivery date and time. It also offers a dedicated section to manage scheduled messages before they're sent.
The message will be sent at the desired time, even if your device is offline. As with any message, scheduled ones supports text, links, photos and videos, while being protected by end-to-end encryption. Messages can be scheduled for as little as 10 minutes ahead of the current time, or up to two weeks in advance. The feature is also compatible with group chats.
The feature is now in beta for some WhatsApp testers on Android, and should be rolling out to more accounts in the coming weeks. With a formal beta now available, you can expect an official release in the near future.

articles.title: Gỡ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh vì nợ thuế: Kinh nghiệm thực tế về cách xử lý nhanh nhất
articles.text:
Hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh được thực hiện ra sao?
Theo hướng dẫn của Cục Thuế, việc hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh được thực hiện ngay khi người nộp thuế đáp ứng đủ điều kiện. Quy trình cụ thể tùy thuộc vào tình trạng mã số thuế và nghĩa vụ thuế của từng trường hợp.
Đối với doanh nghiệp, hộ kinh doanh đang hoạt động: Cơ quan thuế thực hiện hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh khi số tiền thuế nợ còn phải nộp xuống dưới 500 triệu đồng. Đối với hộ kinh doanh, cá nhân kinh doanh, ngưỡng tương ứng là dưới 50 triệu đồng.
Đối với người nộp thuế không hoạt động tại địa chỉ đã đăng ký (trạng thái 06): Người nộp thuế cần hoàn thành các nghĩa vụ thuế, hóa đơn và thực hiện thủ tục khôi phục hoặc chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế theo quy định. Khi đủ điều kiện, cơ quan thuế sẽ ban hành thông báo hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh.
Đối với cá nhân là người nước ngoài hoặc người Việt Nam xuất cảnh để định cư ở nước ngoài: Cơ quan thuế hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh ngay sau khi xác định người nộp thuế đã hoàn thành nghĩa vụ thuế.
Theo quy trình điện tử, hệ thống của cơ quan thuế xử lý, xác định điều kiện và gửi thông báo hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh sang hệ thống của Cục Quản lý xuất nhập cảnh trong tối đa 8 phút kể từ khi nhận được chứng từ nộp thuế từ ngân hàng. Hệ thống xuất nhập cảnh tiếp tục xử lý trong khoảng 5 phút để cập nhật thông tin tại các cửa khẩu hàng không.
Kinh nghiệm gỡ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh thực tế
Chia sẻ với PV VietNamNet, bà Phạm Thị Hòa, Giám đốc Công ty Luật TNHH UCASE, cho biết thời gian gỡ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh do vướng nghĩa vụ thuế phụ thuộc vào tình trạng của doanh nghiệp và mức độ phối hợp với cơ quan thuế.
“Điều quan trọng nhất là xác định đúng nguyên nhân bị tạm hoãn xuất cảnh. Khi phát hiện mình thuộc diện này, người đại diện doanh nghiệp cần kiểm tra quyết định tạm hoãn xuất cảnh để biết cơ quan thuế quản lý, lý do và thông tin liên hệ. Nếu chưa rõ tình trạng của mình, nên liên hệ trực tiếp cán bộ thuế theo thông tin trên quyết định tạm hoãn xuất cảnh hoặc đến cơ quan thuế để được hướng dẫn”, bà Hòa lưu ý.
Cơ quan thuế có thể cho biết doanh nghiệp đang thuộc trường hợp nào, chẳng hạn mã số thuế ở trạng thái bị khóa do bỏ địa chỉ kinh doanh hay người đại diện bị tạm hoãn xuất cảnh vì khoản nợ thuế vượt ngưỡng. Từ đó, người nộp thuế mới xác định được hướng xử lý phù hợp.
Đối với trường hợp doanh nghiệp bị tạm hoãn xuất cảnh do nợ thuế nhưng vẫn đang hoạt động, nếu số tiền nợ vượt ngưỡng áp dụng thì việc hoàn thành một phần nghĩa vụ thuế để đưa số nợ xuống dưới ngưỡng là hướng xử lý cần xem xét.
Theo kinh nghiệm xử lý cho khách hàng, bà Hòa khuyến cáo, người nộp thuế nên chủ động liên hệ cơ quan thuế để xác nhận điều kiện và thủ tục cụ thể, thay vì mặc nhiên cho rằng hệ thống sẽ tự động gỡ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh ngay sau khi nộp tiền.
“Thực tế, khoản tiền đã nộp không phải lúc nào cũng được hệ thống thuế ghi nhận ngay. Có thể mất khoảng 1-2 ngày để hệ thống ghi nhận khoản tiền và hạch toán giảm số nợ. Nếu cần xử lý gấp, người nộp thuế nên chủ động xuất trình biên lai nộp tiền cho cán bộ thuế để kiểm tra, đối chiếu và cập nhật hồ sơ khi đủ căn cứ”, bà Hòa nói.
Trường hợp doanh nghiệp không hoạt động tại địa chỉ kinh doanh, phải thực hiện thêm nhiều thủ tục như nộp hồ sơ đề nghị chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế hoặc khôi phục mã số thuế, bổ sung các tờ khai còn thiếu và nộp tiền phạt, thời gian xử lý sẽ dài hơn.
Từ xử lý thực tế, bà Hòa cho hay nếu hồ sơ đơn giản và người thực hiện chủ động hoàn thành từng bước, có thể mất khoảng 1-2 tuần.
Trường hợp phải rà soát nhiều nghĩa vụ thuế, bổ sung báo cáo và chờ ban hành quyết định xử phạt, quá trình này có thể kéo dài khoảng 3 tuần.
Thông thường, người thực hiện cần nộp hồ sơ đề nghị chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế hoặc khôi phục mã số thuế, tùy nhu cầu của doanh nghiệp.
Sau khi tiếp nhận hồ sơ, cơ quan thuế kiểm tra và xác định những tờ khai còn thiếu. Nếu doanh nghiệp chưa phát sinh hoạt động và hồ sơ đơn giản, có thể chủ động rà soát, nộp các tờ khai còn thiếu ngay từ đầu.
Khi cơ quan thuế tiếp nhận tờ khai, hệ thống sẽ ghi nhận tình trạng chậm nộp và làm căn cứ xử lý vi phạm. Việc lập biên bản, trình ký quyết định xử phạt cũng cần thời gian. Sau khi có quyết định, người nộp thuế phải hoàn thành tiền phạt, tiền thuế còn thiếu, tiền chậm nộp và các khoản liên quan, trong đó có lệ phí môn bài nếu phát sinh.
Nếu chủ động nắm được các thủ tục cần thực hiện, người nộp thuế có thể tự rà soát và hoàn thành một số công việc song song, thay vì chờ cơ quan thuế hướng dẫn từng bước. Tuy nhiên, việc nộp tiền trước hay chờ hệ thống cập nhật số phải nộp cần căn cứ vào hướng dẫn cụ thể của cơ quan thuế. Với hồ sơ thuận lợi, quá trình có thể rút ngắn; còn nếu phải chờ rà soát, cập nhật nghĩa vụ và hoàn thiện nhiều thủ tục, thời gian sẽ kéo dài hơn.
Bà Hòa cũng lưu ý, nhiều người nhầm tưởng mình không còn nợ thuế khi tra cứu trên eTax Mobile không thấy khoản phải nộp, hoặc chỉ còn một khoản nhỏ đã thanh toán. Tuy nhiên, thông tin hiển thị trên ứng dụng chưa chắc đã phản ánh đầy đủ nghĩa vụ thuế của doanh nghiệp đã bị khóa mã số thuế từ nhiều năm trước.
Chẳng hạn, một doanh nghiệp thành lập năm 2015 rồi bỏ địa chỉ, không nộp báo cáo thuế và bị khóa mã số thuế từ thời điểm đó. Khi chủ doanh nghiệp làm thủ tục giải thể hoặc khôi phục mã số thuế vào năm 2026, cơ quan thuế có thể phải rà soát lại nghĩa vụ kê khai, lệ phí môn bài, tiền phạt và tiền chậm nộp trong khoảng thời gian liên quan.
Ở một số trường hợp, dữ liệu trên ứng dụng chỉ dừng ở thời điểm mã số thuế bị khóa, nên người nộp thuế không nhìn thấy đầy đủ các khoản phát sinh cần xử lý.
Vì vậy, theo bà Hòa, không nên chỉ dựa vào số liệu trên ứng dụng eTax Mobile để kết luận đã hoàn thành mọi nghĩa vụ.
Cách chắc chắn hơn là liên hệ cơ quan thuế quản lý, yêu cầu kiểm tra và xác định đầy đủ số tiền, hồ sơ còn thiếu trước khi thực hiện các bước tiếp theo.

articles.title: WhatsApp may soon let users schedule messages
articles.text:
WhatsApp is testing a feature that lets users schedule messages between ten minutes and two weeks ahead, spotted in an Android beta by WaBetaInfo. The main business use for it, sending work messages outside hours, is regulated across much of Europe, and nothing marks a delivered message as scheduled.
WhatsApp is testing a way to schedule messages. Users hold the send button, pick a delivery time and the message goes out on its own. The window runs from ten minutes ahead to two weeks.
The feature appeared in an Android beta spotted by WaBetaInfo, Engadget reported. It is reaching some testers now, with wider access expected over the coming weeks.
The change lands harder here than in America. WhatsApp has around 500 million monthly users in Europe out of roughly two billion worldwide, and it carries work conversations that Americans hold elsewhere.
Mechanically it is unremarkable. Scheduled messages send at the chosen time even with the app closed, carry text, links, photos and video, and keep end-to-end encryption.
WaBetaInfo found limits Engadget does not mention. Only one photo or video can go in a scheduled message, and in a group it reaches only the people who were members when it was set.
Telegram has offered this since 2019, so WhatsApp is catching up rather than inventing anything.
What matters is the use case being advertised. Handling work messages outside hours is a legal question in much of Europe, and France made ignoring after-hours email a right in 2017 for firms with more than 50 staff.
Others followed. Italy legislated the same year, Spain in 2018, Belgium in 2018 and again in 2022, then Portugal, Ireland and Greece in 2021 and Slovakia in 2024.
Portugal went furthest. Its labour code restricts contacting staff outside working hours except in emergencies, with inspectorate fines attached, in a bloc where employee monitoring must already be necessary and proportionate.
Scheduling is therefore a compliance tool as much as a convenience. A manager writes at eleven at night, and the message arrives at nine in the morning.
Nothing marks it as scheduled. WaBetaInfo says recipients cannot see that a message was held, and get no notification if the sender deletes it first.
That moves the timestamp rather than the working hours. The eleven o’clock message still got written at eleven, and the record will say otherwise.
There is still no EU-wide rule. Parliament called for a right-to-disconnect directive in 2021 and it remains in drafting, so the protections stay national and uneven.

articles.title: Microsoft's president says AI is less regulated than a carton of milk - Engadget
articles.text:
Microsoft's president says AI is less regulated than a carton of milk
Brad Smith said the lack of US action gives the UK a unique opening to lead in terms of regulating AI.
Milk can't hack companies and governments like AI definitely can, but it's still subject to more regulation, Microsoft president Brad Smith told ITV on Friday. "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI," Smith said in the interview. "Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."
Major US AI giants like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google's DeepMind have spoken in favor of an AI development slowdown. However, US President Donald Trump has said that, if anything, the US AI industry needs to accelerate to stay ahead of China.
Rather than government, Trump would prefer that AI companies regulate themselves. At his so-called Super Intelligence summit, AI bosses including Google Sundar Pichai, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Elon Musk and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang signed a pact with several key tenets. Those include implementing self-regulation, safeguards to keep pioneer models from going rogue and using "independent auditors" to assess models.
Critics were unimpressed, though, with one telling the BBC that it allows firms to "define what counts as safety" and another saying that "the accord should be ignored for the distraction it is."
Microsoft's Smith thinks the lack of US action gives the UK a unique opening to lead in terms of regulating AI. "In Washington DC, people don't look at the UK and they don't look at London the way they look at Brussels — that's a strength," he said. "I hope that's the role we can play as a company. I hope that's the role the UK can play as a country. [W]hen you look at models that are so powerful that they're putting the world's cybersecurity at risk, I would say: the moment has arrived."

articles.title: Far-Right Election Groups Are Now Targeting Nursing Homes
articles.text:
With just weeks to go until the midterms, election denial groups have found a new target: nursing homes.
The groups, led by the right-wing Election Integrity Network, have claimed without evidence that left-wing organizations are perpetrating voter fraud inside nursing homes, care homes, and assisted-living facilities. The network is now recruiting their followers to contact and question those facilities.
“These left-wing groups go into the nursing homes, and they go into the group homes, and they basically steal the votes of these most vulnerable,” Cleta Mitchell, the Election Integrity Network’s founder, said in a recent appearance on Steve Bannon’s War Room show.
As evidence, Mitchell referenced a case in Wisconsin from 2020 in which a sheriff alleged that eight residents in a care home had their votes filled out for them. The Wisconsin Election Commission rejected the claims. Mitchell told Bannon the case could have cost president Donald Trump the 2020 election, though that wouldn’t be possible: Trump lost Wisconsin in 2020 by over 20,000 votes.
Mitchell’s group has been urging followers to download a toolkit from the Election Integrity Network website and email and call nursing homes in their area. The group has also created multiple images for followers to share on social media which reinforce the idea of widespread voter fraud at nursing homes.
In one campaign, the network shared a series of posts that mapped residential care facilities in competitive congressional districts in states including Arizona, California, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, and Virginia. The posts identified “vulnerable residents” who “may become targets for political predators seeking easy access to ballots.”
Mitchell and the Election Integrity Network did not respond to requests for comment.
The effort is part of a much broader push by election deniers to undermine trust in the midterms. And just like the claims of noncitizen voting and widespread mail-in voter fraud, they have been supercharged by the Trump administration.
In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) issued a memo that removed previous guidance on how staff at nursing homes could help residents to vote, such as assisting with mail-in voting or transporting residents to polling locations. The new memo replaced that guidance with threats of prosecution if staff “engage in inappropriate coercion or other violations of residents’ rights.”
The memo also claimed that the agency has “become aware of several allegations of instances in which resident rights were unlawfully violated.” However, the examples cited in the memo did not lead to any proven cases of voter fraud. CMS did not respond to a request for comment.
In August, senators led by Elizabeth Warren and Alex Padilla slammed the changes, writing in a letter to CMS that rather than protecting the country’s 2 million nursing home residents, the new rules would disenfranchise them.
“CMS issued a memo that appears to be an attempt to intimidate nursing home staff from assisting residents in the voting process,” the senators wrote in the letter, addressed to CMS administrator Mehmet Oz (who himself has flip-flopped on whether the 2020 election was rigged).
But now, with less than a month to go before the midterms, groups like the Election Integrity Network—which has close ties to the White House—are pushing the narrative that nursing homes are a hive of vote rigging activity.
Another election denial group, the New York–based Project Civicia, has launched a similar campaign, entitled “Adopt a Care Facility.” The group told WIRED that it could not share how many people were taking part in the campaign but repeated the claims made by CMS about voter fraud in Wisconsin, in addition to other allegations.
“We do not presume wrongdoing by a facility because its residents need voting assistance,” Kim Hermance, cofounder and president of Project Civica, tells WIRED. “There are other public cases of forged absentee applications and similar problems. Separately, in our own review of New York records, we noticed people over 85 who appeared to register and vote for the first time shortly before an election. That is not illegal by itself, but it raised a basic question about how facilities handle the process.”

articles.title: The OnePlus 16 is the company’s most interesting phone in years
articles.text:
Today the OnePlus 16 launched in China, the company’s first flagship phone since quitting both the US and European markets this summer. As luck would have it, it also looks like the company’s best phone in some time.
The OnePlus 16 is the company’s most interesting phone in years
But it’s not launching in the US or Europe.
But it’s not launching in the US or Europe.
Like most OnePlus phones, the 16 is positioned around performance, with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, and up to 1TB of storage and 16GB of RAM. That’s backed up by an enormous 9,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, one of the biggest seen in any Android flagship yet. 100W wired and 50W wireless charging complete the power setup.
On the display front, the phone jumps to a 185Hz OLED panel for the first time. That’ll not only be used for 185fps gaming in compatible titles, but can also run at up to 165Hz throughout the system UI — a first for high refresh rate panels like this.
Even the cameras, not usually OnePlus’ strong suit, have had a meaningful upgrade. The main camera has a higher resolution (200 megapixels), larger sensor (1/1.4-inch-type), and faster aperture (f/1.4) than the OnePlus 15’s. That should help, given we found that phone’s camera had frustrating “imitations in low light.” 50-megapixel ultrawide and telephoto cameras round out the rear trio, and the latter also enjoys a big bump to a 1/1.95-inch sensor.
There’s a design flourish too, with the phone’s silver finish including LED lighting that features a big “16” and what the company claims is a set of galactic coordinates. While the shapes of the lights are fixed, they’ll reportedly flash with different rhythms to notify you of calls, messages, battery level, and more.
The OnePlus 16 is available in China starting from ¥5,699 (about $850). With OnePlus no longer in either the US or Europe, there’s no hope of a launch for the 16 in either market.

articles.title: The pros and cons of importing foreign phones to the US - Engadget
articles.text:
The pros and cons of importing foreign phones to the US
There's a lot to consider before buying a new phone from abroad.
There are plenty of smartphone options to choose from in the US, from the iPhone to the Pixel. But there are also really interesting phones you'll never find in an American store. Xiaomi's foldables like the Mix Fold, Honor's Magic series and OPPO's Find X phones are a few examples that offer unique designs or features not generally seen in the US.
While phones like these are harder to find in the country, it's possible to import them, but bringing a phone from abroad has its downsides. You may have problems using your phone with local carriers or getting warranty coverage, among other trouble. If you're considering an imported phone, always check a few points first.
What you should know before buying a phone from another country
Buying an imported phone has become a lot easier in recent years. Most smartphones are now designed to work globally on most cellular bands. Still, some phones may not work with those used by your US carrier. Start by checking whether the phone you're considering is compatible with your carrier's frequency bands. Buying the wrong version could leave you stuck on the LTE network with no 5G support.
Carrier-specific features can cause issues too. Features like Wi-Fi calling, VoLTE and visual voicemail usually require certification for each device. So even if your imported phone works fine on your carrier's 5G network, it might not be able to access all these features in the US. Network requirements may also change, so a model that works fine today may run into problems in the future. It's worth checking forums like Reddit to see what people who've bought the phone you want have to say.
Then there are software updates; the rollout of Android updates may be tied to carriers or regions. Also, some Chinese phones are not compatible with Google Play Services, which are a core part of the Android experience most people expect. You may have to install updates manually, and the software might include Chinese apps and services that aren't relevant to you (or readable).
Additionally, getting warranty service in the US for these phones may not be easy. Some of these brands have no official representation in the country, which also means no customer support. Dealing with problems like a dead battery or a cracked screen may require taking your phone to a third-party repair shop with no official authorization from the manufacturer.
The benefits of importing a smartphone
If you're okay with all these hassles, importing a phone from abroad can be a lot of fun and open you up to new hardware that isn't available in the US. There are a lot of Chinese companies putting out exciting products, like three-screen foldables, flagships with DSLR-quality cameras and devices with massive batteries. The Xiaomi 18 Fold is a new foldable phone that looks similar to the iPhone Duo, but it has a bigger battery and better cameras. It also costs less (the equivalent of about $1,640 currently), but you'll need to buy it abroad if you want to use it in the US.
For those who want the latest releases, importing a phone often gives you the chance to get it before the official US launch. Also, many international models still support two physical SIM cards — a feature that most phones sold in the US have already ditched in favor of eSIM. If you don't mind the potential drawbacks, it can be a rewarding experience. But if it's important that you have official support nearby and know all features will work properly on your network, it's easier to buy a phone that's officially supported in your country.

articles.title: Microsoft says Maia 300 chip will run its AI services from 2027
articles.text:
Microsoft will make its own Maia chips the primary system for running AI in its products starting in 2027. The company set out the plan on Monday as it unveiled the Maia 300, the third generation of its custom AI chip.
Microsoft plans deployments measured in gigawatts starting next year, which could mean more than a million Maia 300 chips in 2027.
The chip is built for inference, the work of running AI models once they are trained. Microsoft said it targets long conversations, reasoning, and AI agents that carry out multi-step tasks.
For each megawatt of power, Microsoft expects Maia 300 to generate 40% more tokens, the units of text AI models produce, than top GPU systems.
It did not say which systems it measured against. A full rack also delivers up to seven times the output of its predecessor, Maia 200, the company said.
Each rack holds 96 chips and draws about 167 kilowatts. By comparison, Nvidia’s latest GB300 racks hold 72 GPUs and draw about 142 kilowatts, according to Reuters.
Inside, Microsoft has split the chip into smaller pieces, called chiplets, for computing, memory, and data transfer. The computing parts use TSMC’s N2P process, and each chip carries eight stacks of HBM4 memory.
“It’s basically delivering more intelligence for every watt, every dollar, and every byte of memory by optimizing across the entire system,” Rani Borkar, who runs Azure hardware systems and infrastructure at Microsoft, told Reuters.
Maia 200 is already in use. It serves Microsoft Copilot and runs OpenAI models alongside Microsoft’s own MAI models, and it will support GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry by the end of the year.
The launch follows a push by cloud giants and AI firms to cut their reliance on Nvidia. Google and Amazon have their own AI chips, and OpenAI has built its own chip with Broadcom.
Microsoft has also been working to secure factory capacity. In August, The Information reported that it was in talks with TSMC to make more than 300,000 Maia 300 chips for 2027.
Microsoft plans to share more about the chip at its Ignite conference in San Francisco next month.
